It can be a great game with countless hours of enjoyment.. But it can also be a giant waste of money and
.. And more than likely, something you will not play for more than few hours, or weeks ever.
As someone who's played Eve for the better part of
years. I've done practically everything at one point or another. Been in giant alliances and fought wars against russians. Got bored of industry and planetary crap, did the whole small corp pvp, stealth bombers and black ops. I've lived in 0.0, did the whole wormhole life and pve side of the game and quite honestly I just simply don't care for it [the game] anymore as a whole.
The "expansions" CCP launch every year, do offer new and decent content
. However, MOST of the content CCP provides for EVE is
And as such, I've known many players who basically experience NONE of the new stuff provided in expansions,
and are, more or less, playing the exact same game from 4 - 5+ years ago.
There is a very real problem with EVE that I will get into in just a bit. But what EVE succeeds at ... it does... Pretty well.
It's a decent game if you have people to play with, people who know what they are doing. If you are able to join a decent corp.
If you have no friends, or no one to play EVE with, it's normally an extremely lackluster experience, very boring, and very very lonely. EVE can also be very harsh. You can get scammed, lose all your assets, and lose hundreds or thousands of dollars worth of items in game.
I knew a person who after playing the game for a month, bought a bunch of plexs. Who then undocked, and was then blown up. He lost about $300~ worth of plex. Needless to say, he quit the game shortly after.
EVE, for the most part, is a very ruthless game. You need to play it almost in the mindset of something like an even more hardcore dark souls. Expect to die, or lose your ship. Don't fly stuff you can't afford to lose, don't put all your eggs in one basket. Plan our what you're doing, where you're going. Know what you are doing, before you do it. Which, can be a little much when you are starting out.
I've known a lot of new players, and have helped a lot of new players with the game.
But, there are a lot of misconceptions. Mostly thrown off by CCP themselves, with how they portray the game... And there's a lot of unknowns and things that you just will not get your head around till you've spent a lot of time/money in the game (For the most part).
I've known plenty of people who spent months trying to get a certain ship, only to find out.. That ship was not what they expected, and they were extremely dissapointed and wound up leaving the game due to it. It's depressing to work for a carrier for many months, then to finally get it and realize.. Oh, you can't actually really use it unless you have other people or accounts to play with. There's a lot of aspects in the game that are awesome, however... They (Honestly) are not executed well imo.
Over the years, instead of EVE changing them to make them better. They've stuck with their somewhat flawed design in ways that has left a lot of people basically... In the dust. It keeps the regulars, but for the most part... A lot of other people just can't stick with it.
A lot of things in EVE really just are not designed that well for a solo player in specific scenarios. And generally, for a new player starting off... That is how it's played. Which is AWFUL. Then there's the dissapointment people get when they realize, they can't do what they thought they could. Or what they want to do. This is a
EVE is a game for groups of people. If you play by yourself, you will almost certainly be bored out of your mind more than likely. You will more than likely quit the game within the first few hours.
EVE is just not good at that, and probably never will be.
Don't get me wrong, I love EVE. I always have, even though I have a lot of problems with it. I still play it to this day. I've had numerous accounts over the years and it's still something that I usually come back to for a few months every expansion. Then drop off, of course once I realize there's still nothing there for me.
Most people I knew that were hardcore into EVE and used to nolife the game, have never played it again.. There's usually two types of EVE players. Those that love it, and play it all the time. And those that play it, hate it, and never play it again.
I'm a bit of an odd one stuck in the middle but oh well :P
I hope that one day CCP can actually change some of the things that HOLD eve online back from being the best it can be. But I know that will probably never happen, I still enjoy seeing and hearing about the fleet fights, watching the killboards, and playing every now and then but... EVE can get extremely stale for a lot of people, and that's why even people who love it might never come back.
Honestly, would I reccomend EVE? Not really because MOST people (Once again, talking about in general) do not like it, and have a real hard time with the game.
There, of course, are people that love EVE and eat it up like there's no tomorrow. Great, but for most people.. It just isn't worth it.

Have played Eve-Online on and off since 2007, Eve is the only "Real" mmo, there is no alternative to eve.
Eve is alot more about skill/knowledge than "levels", the progression has some depth but alot more width, a new player can become very useful to a fleet in a matter of days and specialize into effective roles in a relatively short time, Eve is what you make it, if you find friends, take chances, make plans and show initiative Eve is like no other game, if you are looking for a themepark you will be disappointed, tho pve has become alot more interesting over the years and the addition of planetary structures gives budding industrialists a real chance to compete, especially when there are big wars being fought.
Dont listen to the haters who claim eve pvp is "spreadsheets online", Eve pvp is about speed, angles, situational awareness and keeping a cool head, especially pvp in small gangs is amazing and the possibilities for outsmarting people and blowing them up are endless, pvp includes aggressive trade, spying and sabotage, extortion, propaganda, harassment, demoralization, hit and runs, shameless ganks, massive logistics, small gangs, big fleets, fighting for money, fighting for honor, fighting for fun, flying cheap ships destroy expensive ships, flying expensive ships with inventive setups with other skilled pilots to take on a much more numerous enemy, forming up with a bunch of newbies in cheap ships and get a torrent of bitter-veteran tears when their expensive toys get swarmed and exploded and you only lost cheap ships, win the $ war, win the scoreboard war, win the territory war, or just profit from other peoples wars, its all up to you.
Eve is 1 world 1 server, fight with/against Russians/Japanese/Portuguese/Indians/Egyptians, make friends/enemies with people you struggle to communicate with, Dont underestimate the value of playing on one server with people from the entire world, its Amazing.
Its a great time to start playing, there is a major war going on, one that will splinter into alot of smaller power struggles, whether you fancy yourself a combat pilot, pirate, Ore miner, industrialist or trader this opens up alot of possibilities, and the new player resources and oppotunities are amazing compared to when I started playing.
No eve is definately not for everyone, but if Eve is for you then there is nothing that compares, you may not always play, but you will never truly leave.

A repetetive game, but a classic.
The basis of the game is revolved around match-3 gameplay, with bonuses being given for matching 4 or 5 "gems" in a row. However, since you're versing someone, you can't really just score points for matching. Nope, you have to kill them! For that, you have a few methods. You can attack them with your weapon (which costs action points...which you also have to gather) you can match skulls (which are like gems...) or you can use spells. Essentially, some spells give other spells bonus damage, or your weapon, or whatever. You have to create combos with these attacks, and thus defeat your opponent. But remember, they are trying to do the same to you! It's a great mix of strategy, puzzling and questing down into dungeons. Great for a price, great for wasting time, just great in general.

I'm only giving a thumbs up to this game because I know the game is good, and I would definitely recommend it, which is what the thumbs up means. HOWEVER, I recommend getting it on another platform. While the port doesn't have any glaring issues at first glance, there's plenty of technical issues that start to pop up.
First, the visuals. While the inferior graphics don't bother me personally, they falsely advertised the game on the store page by posting screenshots with PS4-level graphics, and false advertisement is always a no-no. Also, knowing KT, they probably purposely made the PC version this way so that the PS4 version will look better, since that's their main moneymaker, which is pretty sad but true. The colors are dull and washed out, the rendering distance is quite poor since you can't see the buildings in the background, and the shadows, textures, and lighting are all PS3 quality. If you're fine with that, then go for it. Mods can improve the colors and sharpness, but the lighting and textures will be unaffected.
Then there's the controller issues. The game didn't recognize my controller right away, since apparently I had to switch it to Dinput mode to get it to work. Even then, not all of the buttons were remappable on the options menu. Even DW8XL had better controller options. I had to resort to using joytokey in order to get some of the buttons to emulate the console layout. Only official Xbox 360 controllers are supported in this game, as stated by Bandai. However, if you have a controller that can act as a 360 controller or can be recognized as one, then it should work. There's absolutely no mouse support in this game, and the keyboard controls are far from ideal, so you're basically forced to use a controller to enjoy the game fully.
Then there's the bugs that are present. Apparently there's a graphical options bug that makes the game stuck at the lowest settings, so you can't even change it. Bandai's looking into it right now. Then there are plenty of other bugs, such as black screens, crashes, microstuttering because it's 59fps, and in-game graphical bugs. One of the most noticeable is that some characters' models start flipping out whenever devil fruit powers are used, particularly Logias. Body parts go missing, clothes disappear, and some body parts don't transform when they're supposed to. There's also sometimes a random plane of light protruding out of the character's bodies, and it sometimes is so big that it obstructs the whole screen. Bandai, you need to fix this stuff before I consider re-purchasing the game.
Personally, I refunded the game because of all the in-game issues I encountered, and am waiting for a fix. Until then, I cannot recommend this game for the PC platform, but please don't think it's a bad game. It's a great entry to the Musou series, and it's even better for One Piece fans, and I totally suggest that all Musou/One Piece/hack'n'slash fans try it out. Just not on PC. Cheers

Ok so it's been like a hundred years since I played this, but now I have a firm opinion on it.
Even Digital: A Love Story showed hints of a game designer that knows so well how her interface works and what's the player relationship with it that she can predict your desperation when it fails - deliberately. Everything in Analogue is made so that you get used to, addicted to even, knowing more about the setting and the characters. As a game, Analogue teases you, makes you care about Hyun-ae with the sheer force of its information flux. It hides and shows and you want to unfold the mysteries even if you're not particularly attached to them. This is Christine Love strongest point.
This is, however and of course, her biggest shortcoming.
Every choice is a moral dichotomy and a very obvious one at that. *Mute is not a character you can relate to. She was not made to be relatable, I suppose... she's more like a storytelling prop. Analogue asks you if you think women are inferior and, if you're sane, you'll say no. Choices inevitably lead to Hyun-ae. The only way to get *Mute's route - if we should call it that way - is through a conscious, rational effort. But this is when the string behind the puppet appear and you play the game knowing its rules, doing things because you need to and not because you want to. So there's depth to the game, but you don't submerge. Instead, you're given a sonar.

I want to give this game a glowing review, I really do. You can just feel the amount of work that went into this project when you start it. The opening cinematic is great and the characters I've seen so far are all brilliant.
So why the negative review?
It's simple, no rebindable keys. I live in Belgium and over here - like in many other countries around the world - our keyboard standard is not QWERTY, it's AZERTY. Normally this wouldn't be too much of a problem. You go to the control options and remap A, Z, Q, W and M and you'd basically have the game covered. Simply setting the PC to EN helps, but when a quicktime event pops up, I tend to push wrong buttons because I'm not used to finding them in other spots than their normals spots.
For someone who doesn't see the problem because they are used to the QWERTY keyboard: just try playing a game where your Z button is walking forwards.
And even beyond my problem is not being able to rebind keys (something most games are able to do since the start of PC gaming), what of left-handed people who feel more comfortable with a different set-up? What of gamers with a disability who remap the keys to something they're more used to? They too have problems accessing this game that for all else seems like a marvelous piece of work.
I could play with a controller, but the old-school adventure game lover who prefers to game on a PC doesn't like to hold a controller for times upon end.
I think I've played every single Telltale game out there over both PC and PS3 (the switch to PC was due to the reasons stated above) and it always felt like Telltale treated the PC market as an  after-thought. I just wanted to make clear that we are customers as well. And I recommend everyone with a none QWERTY keyboard thatd oesn't play using controllers to let this game be for as long as we cannot use a better control scheme.
All that said, the moment the problem with the controls is fixed, you can be sure a glowing review praising attentive game developers will replace this piece.

A pure shoot-and-loot game. Even though this review is mostly for Borderlands 1, it applies to all three, so I copied it to all three. Since the games have been out for quite a while, there are convenient bundles with two or all three of them etc., make sure you check them out before purchasing.
At first, I didn't get "it" and thought that the game sucks. I thought it was just a generic shooter (and once again with failed FOV - *sigh*) with gimmicky cartoon shader, very generic loot containers, guns with somewhat randomized values, and the super obvious fetch quest cliché.
But then, a year later, I tried again - and I got "it". It's a well done generic shooter (whose FOV can be edited in a file) with an interesting fun-depressing otherworldly feel, cartoon shader, reliably balanced generic loot containers, a surprisingly powerful procedural weapons system, and simple quests that make you deal with all these things in various places and that give you some story background. What makes all this work is the whole that emerges from it. It's like acid music of the 1990s. The Roland TB-303 alone sounds boring, but if you use it right and let it play together with other stuff, it's a very powerful driver, and music history might remember you for
.
I ended up buying and playing through BL1, BL2, BL The Pre-Sequel (which came out after 1&2 but whose story plays between 1&2), and almost all DLC. No regrets. It was not a perfect experience, but there's a reason I bought and played
games, and the story didn't contribute much to this reason. It's just the mix of all the gameplay ingredients and - excuse me - the mindlessness of it. A simple but sufficiently deep shoot&loot trip that goes on for tens of hours. (According to
, roughly: BL1 20-60, BL2 30-80, BLps: 20-40)
The quests become available over time, and you can choose freely which of the ones you soaked up into your quest management screen you tackle at which time. There's an indicator expressing how hard they will be for your current character level.
I thought the procedural weapons approach would probably be stupid, that it would be e.g. just a bit more power or range. But no! There are many changing variables, even the weapon designs (and visual effects) change, fitting the weapon's character. Hunting / comparing for the best weapon and learning about where you'll probably find those and where rather not turns into a passion.
Too bad the inventory interface is not half as good as it should be. Well, at least you can mark weapons as garbage so that you can bulk-sell them once back at a vendor or machine, and you can even do a buyback for the identical price. But what
thought it would be a good idea to have the inventory interface move around incessantly? And you need to realize: You'll spend
with this interface, because comparing your guns is a core element of the game.
Then there's the fact that the game will just forget where you have already killed people - they'll just be back on your next visit and loot containers will be refilled, you don't even have to die or reload/restart the game for this. This has upsides, of course, which would be why they decided for this, e.g. now you can keep grinding, and you can enjoy your new toys and your leveled-up character against old foes. It's rather important for balancing that you can't just wipe the world clean. But even though hypothetically, people would repopulate fortresses in reality, you will have to make yourself blind to the feeling that all you're doing is in vain, your actions leave almost no lasting consequence in the world. Just like in real life, right? Except in real life, you don't constantly whip the lands with powerful guns.
What also sucks (but again makes sense, of course) is that you lose a lot of money whenever you die. There will be deaths, though, that are just unnecessary or unfair, or you might even get caught in a loop of dying, which maximizes frustration. This happened to me when I fought Wilhelm and didn't realize that I could just travel away via the obvious terminal. Why didn't I realize? I was mostly blinded by the fact that the arena is a place you can only reach by dropping in from a height that you can't jump, so you can't get out again. This clear message and the fact that I was still relatively new to Borderlands made me blind to the fact that there was an electronic exit right there.
You can't save your game. At least it's not a classic campaign shooter quicksave that bakes every relevant world state detail into a nice file. Instead, you have your character profile which will change as you progress (e.g. incl. money loss from deaths; hint: If you Alt+F4 while you're still dying, nothing is lost.), and it's rather one of those "general player state" and "checkpoint" saves. On the one hand, this very character of savegame is a good thing: Checkpoints have the clear upside of getting you more involved and making the reality more real because you can't beat it into obedience by saving/loading at your leisure. The downside is: The game completely forgets everything but you. While fortresses have been repopulated when you revisit them even without loading, there are a few aspects of the world that stick - until you exit to main menu or out of the game and then continue playing, that is. It all couldn't revolve
just around you.
And there are the quite hard boss fights. Personally, I don't like boss fights, so ignore this paragraph as an actual negative, but I just find them stressful, and what others might misinterpret to be a sense of achievement in me is really just the relief that I managed to overcome this obstacle between me and more of the satisfying gameplay I want to enjoy. You know, like 1990s Eurobeat "music" (That I never liked.) where the painful hectic rap was the desert you had to endure before reaching the next fountain, making the refrain ever so slightly better than it actually was. The game does not have a whole lot of boss fights, but I had to throw everything into them and was often very frustrated when I didn't manage, because dying cost me a bunch of cash, and I had to start the fight completely from scratch.
But Borderlands is fun. A well done shoot&loot world to forget yourself in.
Not all Borderlands games have FOV settings, but with some config file editing, you'll always get what you want.

I'm a huge fan of Dragonball and have been looking forward to picking this up when my time allowed, but I was disappointed from the get go. The Character Creation is lacking, with several features being shared and/or unavailable for races. I understand this on the basis of Namek v Saiyan, but not when Saiyans and Humans should have (more or less) the same access.
The combat is uninspired, and lacks the sophistication and, thus the feeling of reward, for special moves or pulling off combos, and what difficulty there is is brought about by the delay in action between button and action on screen.
The story is well done, (seemingly) well done, but the core mechanics for a fighter/action/adventure game just aren't there to any large degree. By attempting to cater to the fans of all three game styles, Dragonball XenoVerse ultimately falls flat, and leaves the player wanting.
Go back and re-play Budokai if you want a solid, well-rounded Dragonball Fighter, and give this one a miss. Even the most hardcore of DBZ fans will feel let down by the poor implementation of a great idea.

Many people will tell you that Rimworld is very similar to Dwarf Fortress--and they would be right. Rimworld is an amazing homage to Dwarf Fortress in all its complex descriptions and chaotic colonist dealings. Have you ever wanted to tame a cougar and sic it on enemy mechanoids as they storm your base? What about replacing parts of your colonists brains so they no longer feel pain as they throw themselves against the ancient horrors crawling from the laboratory you dug up?  Or, if your tastes are less violent, why not farm a country-sized crop of hay to feed your army of lizards that keep breeding and have overrun your colony? All of this and more is possible in Rimworld, which make it an amazing way for any traditional RPG-loving gamer to play out the life and times of colonists in the brave fronteir, just doing what they do. Almost infinite replayability, with every new set of colonists having their own unique drama to play out before your eyes. Yes, your artist who is newly married might plaster the entire base with porn of his fiance, but hey? Isn't that what games are all about?

Eve is one of if not the best Sandbox MMO in history. I have been playing the game for almost 10 years. And the game keeps delivering... That being said it's not to say that I don't take little breaks from the game over time. But I'm always active in training even if I'm not logging in every day.
Eve is a game with a little bit of a scary learning curve that some new players have a  hard time with. But for that there are 2 words (walls of text) of advice I have for you.
#1 If you are a solo player.  The game has 0 Theme park learning or gaming style for the most part (small set of noob missions only). Most of eves solo play is DEFINED buy YOU. Eve gives you many different avenues (tools) and styles to play and has many things to do. Try to figure them out 1 by 1 and not get lost buy the shear amount of different things.
If you focus initially on how complex the game is more often then not a new player will get lost and overwhelmed. Or board from doing only the one task that you start off with. Take the game in stages and when you start to feel like your grinding in any way take time to look into different aspects of the game... The most important thing about this is that eve does not HAND HOLD or lead you into doing anything... even if there are many things to try and do.
You have to decide what to do and what to focus on buy yourself. If you don't like that type of play style then Eve might not be for you... UNLESS you can handle option number 2.
#2. Don't play the game SOLO :) Eve has a very rich community and the most enjoyment for a lot of players is banding together and fighting for something. And that’s were we get to some of Eve's strongest points. Most MMO's have you fight for nothing more then gear and or a position on a leader board. Something that I as a long time gamer no longer have any interest in. fighting people for an item that you wear or your name on a list does not really impact the game or other people much if at all…
This is where Eve is different. In Eve you can OWN ships and structures that you can deploy in space. and best of all you can LOSE them all. This makes the game more meaningful and also promotes working together and having real goals. As after you learn about the small roll building your own structures in space is like you take it to the next level and TAKE OVER areas of space needing a team of people (corps-Guilds) and alliances or groups of alliances.  The space you take over needs to be defended from... anyone or everyone some times. You have to defend with structures and your own ships (fleets of ships your friends) ALL which can be lost and destroyed. So therefore you and your friends in game have an investment in what you do one that can be taken and destroyed if not defended.
This type of game play can hurt but it's also is the reason why most players are attracted to the game. What you do in game matters and can effect anywhere from one person to thousands. Some players are legends in the game. And just because your new does not mean that in some smaller circles or even larger one in time you cant be as well.  The wonderful thing about Eve is you dont have to be a legend if you dont want to be. You can strive to be great, or you can pick the roll of support where you make ammo and ships or mine, any number of behind the scenes rolls.
There is so much to say and learn about eve and its learning curve can be a little daunting. But the key to getting into a game like eve is understanding that you will have to LEARN how to play the game. The game will NOT hold your hand and make you progress from A to B to C. Instead it gives you  A B C D E F G H I etc. and says here you go figure it out have fun!
And if that’s to involving for you then maybe eve is not for you and that does happen some people just can't handle that type of play style. But if all you see about the game peaks your interest. Remember that there are many players in eve that want you to stay and play and will take time to teach you. Also there are some evil guys in the game as well and there in game job is to make your life a living hell and blow up your stuff. Because that’s what the game is about. It not griefing its part of the game.
Some of those people are actually nice people and are just playing a roll some are seriously♥♥♥♥♥hats lol.. but thats also part of the sandbox. Eve you can do almost anything. and you will die and lose stuff doing it so try and get used to death loss and how to avoid both.

PQ2 is a sweet little coffee break game. It involves a simple concept: a puzzle game with rules similar to Bejeweled, and then takes this concept and stretches, twists, and rebrands it into a series of related minigames that are just different enough to feel like different concepts.
The overall system is a loosely cobbled together RPG. You have a character, who has stats, that goes on quests, and gets loot. Every combat, test, and "Roll", however, is judged by your performance in the Bejeweled-like game. In combat you play versus the AI, in lock picking and trap disarming you play solo but with a limited number of moves to make matches, etc. There's no mistaking it: PQ2 is the same puzzle, rebranded over and over.
The story is paper-thin, and is basically an excuse to fight fight fight, but the puzzle is a brain-teaser, and the AI can get pretty rough. There's also a multiplayer dueling mode for online play. It's also a very chill game that can be played for a few minutes at a time.

Analogue is a lovely little sci-fi JRPG which has you tap into a long forgotten system and discover the depths of the secets hiding within.
I played this game a long time ago, completing 1 playthrough, which took roughly 3 hours. The game is a roleplaying game, and provides little action events, and is moreso built on storybuilding through narrative and text (ie there's quite a bit of reading). But, that isn't a bad thing, and works really well in the environment sculpted in the game.
Insightful, dark and comedic at times, the game hits a number of topics which are not usually seen in games of this sort. If you're the patient sort, and you feel this would be your type of game, it probably will be. But don't expect Die Hard 5; expect a well written story told in an enjoyable environment, with dynamic and vivid characters.
There's replayability here too. Each event has multiple "endings", so you can re-do your story and play from different angles!
Check it out!

This game came to me as a suprise. I was expecting a brutal battle against robots and quiet stealth missions to avoid detection when in reality, the fear factor had me watching every corner to make sure nothing moved without me knowing what it was. Most of the maps are completely dark and require your flashlight and red dot sight to help target enemies; however, there is one problem. Moving to much like running or jogging gives away your location so that the robots know where you are. Flashlights are great visual ques to them as well, so be carefull where you point them. There are two types of robot: a rusher that attacks with only melee attacks while the other is a bot with a gun that can take you out pretty fast if you aren't carefull. The game has been in alpha for a long period of time which is slightly dissapointing; the updates aren't as frequent as they should be and sometimes don't hold all that much content. I would say that this game adds a good sense of horror into a relatively stealth like shooter. I can't wait to see what the developers give us on the day of full release.

First of all, my steam hours is not true. I brought this game years back on the mana games site and I played like 1000+ hours.
Tennis Elbow 2013 is a tennis simulation game devoloped by mana games. It has character custamization which can be compared to a RPG game. It has a very deep learning curve unlike anyother tennis game, so dont execpt to hit amazing winners and win in the first few hours. every stroke matters, the way you position matters, whether you hold down the strike button or not matters. I'l l tell you one thing, when you create that angle from the right side corner of the court to the left end corner of the court for an animalaistic winner....its AWESOME.
Pros :
-character custamization
-career mode is HUGE
-easily moddable (can play with real pro players on real courts)
-no issues in multiplayer execpt for very rare lags (Damn turtles)
-you can host a game and even be in another room (it will give you a sound when someone joins)
-replayability (played 1000+ hrs and still not even slightly boring till now and wont ever be for me)
-Website dedicated for tournements with other players (ITST)
-dev is active and actually punishes toxic players
-community is really kind towards newbies
-nice ranking system with reputation
-can run on any PC easily
-AI has LOTS of diffuculty levels to choose
-large variety of shots (fake drops, defensive and offensive lobs, topspin and power shots just to mention a few)
-split screen (I've played with friends...its good and really fun to play)
-the ball's physics (no game can replicate the real life spins as good as this game....the way the ball passes and hits the backboard when you ace... the ball's spin when you slice etc)
Neutral :
-Reputation (It may help you find fair players but at the same time it doesn't mean a player with bad reputation is not a fair player and vice versa)
-Elite mode in game (Its really unforgiving...you made that slight positioning or timing mistake? that ball is gonna fly out before you know it just like in real life)
-graphics (doesn't bother me but may bother some of you)
Cons :
-occational lags
-small community, 80 to 100 at a given time (hopefully growing)
-character movement (can feel weird or clumsy at times)
-cant remember all the pros :P
The ranking system is ELO based :
400-799= club
800-1299= junior
1300-1999= pro
2000-3499= master
3500+ = Incredible
New player (plays like ****)
Club (can hit shots and getting familiar with the system)
Junior (can hit decent angle shots and rips an easy ball)
Pro (More consistant than junior, good with positioning, can create good angles from most of the court)
Master (Very consistant, almost never makes an unforced error, starts to anticipate where you hit and already moving)
Incredible ( never played one before so no idea but obviously can kick anyone's a**)
Total noob? no problem. The AI's lowest difficulty is probably worse than you (no offense :P)..Master or even incredible? no problem..the AI's higest difficulty will prolly give you a good fight or may even win you.
Those who are complaining about the graphics (Ironically some own pixel graphic games lol) please play virtua tennis 4 or some game you like ;). All aside, I have 1000+ hours and i just turned master and I can easily say this is the best tennis simulation or mabye one of the best simulation games ever. I've been dying to grab and play this game since I first found it on steam 2 months prior to release. I held my breath on instant purchase since I don't really know much on what defines a good or bad game port, but it felt like my worries were pointless. Or perhaps, I've been really, really lucky.
First of all, I've been a fan of the One Piece series for years. This can be looked upon as a biased review, or not. Well, other than the fact that the characters' arms have a weird shading from possibly bad graphics. The gameplay is extremely solid, you will rarely have a moment in which you feel aggravated that the game has not registered damage properly, or that the game has not done what you told it to. The shooting feels tight, and the action feels intense, gritty and realistic.
The guns, while few there are, feel like realistic too, they give an extremely satisfying feeling when shot, everything just feels right, the balance, the recoil, sound, damage, etc. I could go on.
Graphically the game is spectacular, while on a texture to texture comparison with some AAA shooters it may not live up to the mark, it more than makes up for it in atmospheric lighting and post processing, few games can compare to it's incredibly detailed rain effects and sounds, you can, at times be completely immersed by your environments, and it's remarkable.
Aside from the occasional animation glitch; which by the way are a spectacularly hilarious event to behold, the game will immerse you in it's arenas.
By now you're most likely wondering why I have such high praise for the game, yet have not recommended it. This is one of those reasons. A lot of early adopters, myself included, were promised a lot on the side of story, we were promised a heavy emphasis on it, with great variety in how we want to experience it, in fact they still seem to be promising this after years of development, with no story to show for it. If you're wanting this game for story, you have two options, put your trust in the developers that they will hold true to their word, or look elsewhere, which you choose is your own prerogative.
Again, this is another reason I cannot recommend the game, while the game is very cheap, and has plenty of content for a multiplayer experience, to put it simply, it cannot compete with other multiplayer games already on the market, some of which are free, and I struggle to see how it will ever compete with them while it maintains its focus on that market. It's a sad state of affairs, but it's multiplayer scene is not large, and you most likely will not get many hours of enjoyment out of it's multiplayer alone, which sadly is all it has to offer as of this review.
I will not slander the developer for the slow development of the game, I understand that in development unexpected things can happen that can massively hinder progress. But that is not something that increases the value of the game, and sadly the game is not in a state that I could recommend, I really hope that changes in the near future, I have very high hopes for this game, and what is in place now, what framework there is, looks extremely promising.
If you want to help with it’s development, go ahead and purchase, but I would not purchase the game with the expectation that the game is going to be good value for money in it’s current state.

TFTB is the funniest game I have ever played, and also one of the greatest over all. The story is the best I've seen since Life Is Strange, the humor is genuine, the graphics are gorgeous, the music is spectacular, and the action pieces are actually exciting. Rhys and Fiona have firmly planted themselves in the list of my favorite main characters of any video game. They are both just so human, with real motivations and complex choices that go way past "good" or "bad". And the supporting cast is, without question, the best supporting cast of any videogame ever. Sasha is a total badass with a heart of gold, but at the same time still acts innocent and curious throughout the story. Vaugn starts out somewhat annoying, but then develops into an extremely likeable character who delivers some of the funniest lines in the game. *Brofist* Gortys is literally the most adorable thing to ever appear on a video game, and then there's Loader Bot. I could write sonnets on the greatness that is Loader Bot.
The plot of TFTB is one of the most exciting, and interseting ones I have ever played, with countless twists, multiple layers, and excellent character development. The plot device that the whole thing is Fiona and Rhys telling their story to their mysterious captor could have been a mess in another company's hands, but Telltale handles it perfectly, and the plot twist that comes out of that is, without a doubt, the best I have ever incountered in a videogame. Every episode is excellent, and the story gets more serious as the stakes get higher throughout the season, but episode 5 is on a whole other level of greatness. I laughed, I cheered, I teared up, it was a good time.
Even if you have never even heard of Borderlands, You need to play this game ASAP. 10/10
Also, the big action piece in Episode 4 is the hardest I've laughed in a long time.

While it's true that the development of this game has been slow (I believe I bought it back in 2013 but didn't play it much until recently), it has finally crossed the threshold wherein there is enough content and enough things to do to warrant the price tag of $20 (give or take). If you like multiplayer tactical FPS and care about innovative gameplay, then this is for you.
Pros
+ Core gameplay is very refined; it's obvious that they mastered this first then built the game around it
+ Great first person movement/shooting mechanics (you have an actual body!)
+ Innovative / original mechanics like a dynamic weather system, helmet-based HUD and so on
+ Co-op missions are promising
+ Hell Week is really well designed as a "Battle Royale" or Hunger Games inspired game mode - the size and diversity of the playing area blew me away
+ Unique sci-fi setting, definitely a cut above the brown, military themed shooters that dominate this genre
Cons
- Lacking in content: only a few weapons, Co-op mode is barebones, no variety for armour and loadouts (everyone looks the same and has the same kit) etc
- Not very optimized, doesn't even hit max fps on powerful GPUs
- No campaign yet, everything seems centred around training
All in all, if this is your kind of thing there is definitely enough of game here for you to enjoy. I can also vouch for the developers as I am %100 certain they will keep working on this for the months and years to come!

This game is Alpha and obviously has a lot of work ahead of it but what impresses me is most of the major features seem to work.  It has the potential to be the game I will call home for the foreseeable future.  Skill based system, player crafting economy, player housing/cities/nations and many other great features.  It all reminds me of UO and SWG (both early era) which are two of my favorite games.  If you have never played a skill based game before try it with an open mind.  No more leveling, what you actually do is what you become good at.
First off, the game is very rough around the edges.  It’s Alpha so expect Alpha.  For Alpha however it is very impressive compared to others I’ve backed.  Everything in general works.  It might not be pretty but it works.  My review will just be an example of a single play session as a complete noob:
Log in, check my in game e-mail for any quests I’m interested in.  If one looks good I take it, if not I simply ignore them.  I hit the local bar/pub (allows you to enter a resting state that makes entertainment abilities usable) to do some Entertainment activities such as dancing and storytelling (this is the game’s buff system, the more people around using entertainment skills the faster you seem to stack buffs and of different types).

Once I get 6 stacks of all the buffs I can that last more than an hour, I head out of town, with my Adult Setlang pet and start murdering stuff with my rifle (gaining rifle skill and animal handing doing so).  I harvest any lumber or metal I can find as well as the corpses of the fallen (gaining survival skill and knowledge of what I kill).  Using my survival skills I upgrade the resources harvested as far I can (quality in materials matters to crafters).
I’m working on my personal short term goal of building a speeder bike so I focus on the mats needed to create this (found by access an outside website for crafting, expect plenty of this).  If enough time goes by I also use my survival skill to create a camp in the wild to enter a resting state (same as the bar) and refresh my buffs.  If you have 6 stacks with a minute left, it only takes 1 more stack to refresh all stacks to max duration.
I find any baby animals I can tame and do so to raise animal handling.  I also have to craft food for my pets and feed them every hour so they can continue to grow to adulthood.  Eventually I’ll be able to turn them into mounts if I choose depending on the animal.
Every fight I gain skill in Stealth, light armor and whatever other skills I use.  If I have to run and heal I gain in healing skill.  What you do is what you become good at, you get the idea.
That’s a very basic example of what’s going on and it all works.  The animations are rough, the sounds are not great and not directional, the graphics glitch and the engine lags at times especially around what appear to be server lines but it’s still Alpha.  If the game can get polished up it will be a real gem.

This game is hard.
I'm going to start there. The learning curve is so steep it might as well be a brick wall. Three days in the game and I'm barely comfortable leaving the main city to poke trash mobs, and Ive barely started nibbling on crafting.
This game is also incredibly complex, beautiful, and clearly much loved by its developers.
Dont look here for WoW. Dont look here for SWTOR. This is truly an "Old School" game from the days of Star Wars Galaxies or the very first Everquest. This is a game for the MUD nerds and the Tabletop masters with skads of reference material on-hand from the days of grid maps and notebooks.
There is very little hand holding, there are no classes. Dont complain about haivng to craft a hundred different sub-components to get your speeder bike. Because that's what this game is about! It's about complexity and spending hours to master some tiny aspect of the game that makes you an invaluable cog in the greater machine. I love this game. I love it /because/ it is overwhelming. It gives me so much content dropped into my lap like a knotted fishing reel that I'll spend forever pulling apart the strands until I understand the mechanism.
That's what this game is about, and it does it very well for being so very early access.
Now, dont get me wrong. It /is/ still early access. There are glitches, texture collisions, quest-killing bugs, and the framerates grind a bit. But for all its warts, I can see the diamond underneath, and I cant wait to see where they take it.
In conclusion : Buy the game with the understanding that this is a HARD game, and it is an EARLY game. But it smacks of nostalgia, and it's a wonderfully refreshing challenge in a world where MMOs are designed to cater to the whiny masses and dragons practically slay themselves.

Fighting system is nowhere near as fluid and captivating as other games available around, and ends up with just clicking on series of aptitudes that would remind DAOC and its combos. Besides that the quest system is broken and some missions require too much time running around to cover long distances to collect very little and have even less in return. The game is not rewarding.
This said it will certainly please its own crowd but feels very frustrating and disappointing from my point of view. I will probably not pursue it past the alpha/beta phase unless a lot of things get square out and fixed to make it more attractive.
And yes one last but very important thing: grinding has stopped being fun a hell of a time ago. If I wanted to aim for a grindfest kind of game I'd know exactly where to go and that also precisely places where I'm keeping away from. Please check TESO for that matter. Greatest PvE system seen in a while. I haven't been as far as trying the PvP system but there are just too many obstacles for me to even consider pushing that far into the game.

Time to have a blast with friends or witness those friendships come to an end in the mini-game mayhem that is Move Or Die.
From my viewpoint, it seems as though there was more mini-games in Move or Die, but in total, there’s only 27. Now although the quantity seems disappointing, the variety is not. Be it the mini-games or the modifiers that you’ll see as well, there’s always a twist to the games you play.
The mini-games ranges from avoiding a homing rocket or a laser controlled by your opponent, finish first in a race, duel your opponents with rifles or chainsaws, splatter yourself all over the room or clean up most of the mess, steal more treasure than your opponents,… I think you get the idea, there’s lots to choose from.
You can acquire more content through leveling up and the content ranges from more mini-games, different characters to choose from or other miscellaneous stuff. There’s a problem with this though, because of the amount of content that can be unlocked, unlocking everything can take “Hours”.
To save time, you can purchase said content through the marketplace on Steam, but not everyone will want to make those purchases, especially when you can unlock everything in-game in the first place.
Another problem that should be mentioned is that when you get new content from leveling up, sometimes what you get is not new at all, rather something you got already. This can be frustrating for those that seek to unlock everything in the game.
As mentioned in the previous section, you need to level up in order to unlock new content. The best way to do that is by playing multiplayer games and winning them will be even better. When playing a multiplayer game, should the host quit the game early, the match ends immediately.
This can be frustrating to the others involved, because they don’t get any experience or any sort of compensation for the host quitting the game prematurely, nor is the designated host of the match switched to another player.
While I do not recommend this game for completion purposes, I can recommend it for the overall fun factor. I had fun playing this game with my friends and whether you want to play this with your friends or complete strangers, this is a game that shouldn’t disappoint you.

The fourth Storm game in the Naruto Shippuden Ultimate Ninja Storm series, a dynamic and intense 3D fighting game set in the Naruto Universe as the name suggests, this game is purely made for the fans of the show and manga. It is faithful to both and has a large amount of characers to choose from and has beautiful cutscenes that top even the anime itself, thanks to it's visually impressive graphics. Though it's not without it's problems.
The Story:
The game begins with the Nine Tails demon fox attack on the Hidden Leaf Village (Konoha) and you get to play as memorable ninja like the Fourth Hokage Minato Namikaze and the Third Hokage Hiruzen Sarutobi. If these names sound unfamiliar to you then you haven't seen the show and thus won't really appreciate what this game has to offer, for it's story though it does attempt to bring newcomers in with the first mission fighting the tailed beast in an epic boss battle in the Leaf Village.
After that the game fast forwards to a more recent timeline where our hero Naruto is renowned as the Hero of the village for defeating Pain in the previous game and has earnt everyone's respect. The game continues to tell the story in a open world-ish style where the player controls the characters and explores the world completing main story missions that contain very nicely done cutscenes, alot of talking and with some fights in between which really will please the Naruto fans with it's narrative newcomers will most likely be confused though, despite this the story mode is one of the best features in this game for me anyway.
Gameplay:
Naruto Storm 3 is a fighting game with many mechanics involved you can attack with strings of combos at the push of a button and moving the analogue stick (if your using a controller which is reccommended) up or down, you will get a different combo. You can use chakra to perform jutsu's and ultimate jutsu's which are flashy and over the top and is faithful to the characters, chakra can be used for dashing and enchancing shuriken throws.
You can team up with two other support characters in team matches if you get tired of the single matches and this opens up new gameplay strategies, you can select what role your support characters can be such as support, defense and attack type. Each member can be summoned out and attack the opponent or called upon during a combo dash attack, once the team gauge is completely filled though you can perform a team ultimate jutsu combo, you can pick characters that work in a team in the show or completely make up your own team as there are loads to choose from. Although most of the characters use the same formula just with a different skin, each one has their own personal movesets and fighting style, making this game incredibly easy to just pick up and play which might turn off some professional fighting gamers.
The boss battles are definitley a highlight in this game as they are both exciting and visually appealing it really shows how much time and effort the developers have put in to make these memorable fights epic, they even add some of their own cinematic fights in the game, such as extending the Naruto and Sasuke fight when they've reunited after Sasuke killed Danzo. The fights cutscenes are mostly QTE's but you do actually fight them like a normal match and the QTE's appear in certain moments of the fight, you are graded when completing the boss battles and it's satisfying to get an S rank on everyone of them.
Another mode within the story campaign is the Mob battles which are similar to the Dynasty Warrior games, at certain points in the story mode you fight a mob of enemies and try to reach the goal this is an interesting element to the series, but the moments are short lived and there isn't that many which is dissapointing,.
One last thing that Namco Bandai have added is the Ultimate Decision mode which allows the player to select decisions in the story, choosing Hero will result in an easier fight but with less rewards and experience to level up your item slots however Legend will have a harder fight but will have better rewards. The outcome doesn't matter that much but the fights themselves will change accordingly like in the Nine Tails attack you can choose to fight the Masked Man as Minato first, or fight the Nine Tails instead.
Graphics:
Naruto Storm games are known for having impressive and stunning visuals for it's graphics this really shows during the cutscenes, they aren't animated in fact they are full 3D models that are very detailed that contrast well with the colourful environments during the battles. Although the map is mostly scenery and window dressing even after the map has been blown up by Naruto's Tailed Beast Bomb ultimate jutsu, it even shows an explosion during the scene and somehow the environment remains untouched in future I would like a more dynamic battlefield,
Sound:
The music in this game although decent isn't very memorable I couldn't tell you what my favourite tracks were as I can with Payday 2, it's mostly repeated songs during fights and aren't very entertaining mostly piano symphonies if your into that kind of thing, which isn't to say it's bad just that you won't be downloading the soundtrack at anytime. Voice acting in English is fairly well done though I highly suggest playing Japanese voices. The sound effects themselves are great Naruto's Rasengan sounds like a Rasengan, Sasuke's Chidori sounds like how it should be you get the idea.
Overall Naruto fans will love the story mode and the wide variety of familiar characters to choose from the game isn't completely up to date with the manga but it finishes off fairly close to where the anime left off at a certain point. I decided to review this game as the manga is ending within 5 weeks I hope you all enjoyed my review and will consider getting into the series, as it has it's action, comedy, interesting characters and some deep messages within for you to experience.

As far as battling goes, It's your run or the mill kaiblast spam enabled fighter where you can either sweat it out with actual skill or 200 Million volts amal virtually the whole game. It does feel less enabled to do that seeing as the moves are very easy to do and a flick of the stick an change to varying combos. (or I really need to play newer games because a lot of newer games are just doing things right.) Nonetheless, instead of the normal something is about to happen here is what it is and a small flashback as to why, like sonic games and such. This game gives more of an RPG like place in the game, letting you observe details and characters from the beginning, and actively letting you use them, accompanied with allies who may have also been present. Alright, so let's start with my first comment: BUY THIS GAME. It is absolutely fantastic and a vital piece of gaming media for a Dragon Ball fan. I didn't think I'd like it, then I played it and now it's one of my favourite online games.
I can assure you, you will love it.
Now, let's get down to pros and cons.
PROS:
Easy to pick up gameplay, tricky to master but not exactly "hard".
A fun, engaging experience that will have your attention for hours on end.
A steady levelling system that has you work for it, but doesn't grind your face in the dirt or require you put in hours to get a single level.
Gameplay and advancement are well-paced and don't require too much effort, though you're not just handed everything either.
Nice simple graphics that don't tax an average rig too much even at full power; a good offset to the major problem of PC gaming.
Smooth, comfortable integration of USB controllers, although the keyboard controls are just as easy to learn.
==
CONS:
Some ridiculously difficult Parallel Quest scenarios that will have you seething with rage as if you were playing Street Fighter or KOF.
Server can be a bit laggy and interfere with multiplayer experiences at times; I played with someone only a few miles away and we still had a tricky time with collision detection and movement lag.
Customization. It's another game that presents itself as being highly customizable in terms of character creation, however when you actually get down to it, it's pretty limited. You can only change colours on a very small selection of outfits; the others are based off outfits from the franchise, and as you would expect, they kill the "character creation" function because the moment the average gamer is given a creativity toy, their first instinct is to make things they already know, so everyone thinks they're Goku, everyone thinks they're Gohan, etc. and very few people actually bother to make an original character in this.
It's a Namco Bandai game. They do this all the time; they bring out a great game that shows so much promise, only give it a little bit of content expansion and then abandon it to work on an inferior title, in this case that new One Piece thing. With SoulCalibur V, they did the same thing to work on TTT2 which was massively inferior. So while they make great products, they're a rather careless and irresponsible company that don't care much for their own products (although they're definitely no Konami or EA).
==
SUGGESTIONS:
Needs more interactive environments, especially in the hub world.
They should put in at least quite a few more expansions that focus on character creation. Most specifically, let us colour any outfit and let Majin go barefoot; perhaps also some footwear like sandals or ankle guards. What we have is extremely limited despite being presented as bigger than it is.
An actual chatbox so players can talk to each other with text. I appreciate the effort to filter out spam by giving us preset messages, but come on - a private chat window at least.
I hate to sound like a feminazi, but there are SO many great female fighters in the Dragon Ball universe that you completely ignored. There are about a half dozen playable females in this game and several dozen males. Just look at the Dragon Ball Wikia and take your pick; you should put in at least 10 more females.

Addictive blend of Bejeweled clone, turn-based strategy, and RPG elements. Tactical decision making is surprisingly deep given the wide array of spells per class. Itemization, while somewhat diverse, is a bit lacking and arguably meaningless at times. Similarly, on normal difficulty the game doesn't present too much of a challenge and the penalty for losing combat is a counter intuitive -- you actually gain experience points for a failed encounter. That said, the positives far outweigh the negatives and one play through will give you roughly 40ish hours of entertainment depending on the number of side quests completed.  Additionally the classes are distinct enough that you'll probably want to check all of them out potentially quadrupling your game time. There are also Endurance, Tournament, and an online Versus mode that yield even more replay value. A terrific bargain at the $10 list price and an absolute steal at any significant discount.

The original trailers, concepts, and promises of Interstellar Marines were a significantly better alternative to viagra for gamers who love realism and tactics. This alone made it a dream game, and the fact that it was paired with an interesting and unique setting with an emphasis on Co-op rather than deathmatch made it all the better.
Unfortunately, after following this game for a very long time, most of those orignal promises have faded away. The only content that seems to be dropping pertains to multiplayer. I'll admit that Hell week is actually pretty fun, and that I don't mind it, but it's not what was originally promised for a game like this.
Basically, purchasing the base game isn't a bad idea if your interest is piqued after researching the game, but hold off on Spearhead until your confident that it's a worthy investment.

One Piece Pirate Warriors is a great game.. for One Piece fans.. who have finished the series. It's a very repetetive dynasty warrior like game. The graphics are okay and it loads fast on a decent PC.
The good : The Character development and Battle Animations are pretty good. The story is nearly as expansive as the actual One Piece Story. Same voice actors from the show and the character animation is very well done ( I wish the Anime was done as well as the animation in this game)
The bad: It skips over minor characters in certain arcs ( I don't blame them this game would be VERY long if they really put everything in) The play style is VERY repetitive, doesn't really offer much new from level to level so if you're not a Fan of one piece and the story you're probably going to get bored very easily. That being said I think this game is really just for One Piece fans, and even then I think that you'd really have to love One Piece to Love this game.
I honestly just wish the pacing of the story was a bit better, it was hard for me to get invested in the ARCS because they skip over random details , so emersion is low.
Overall a good game, the actual game play is average but I highly recommend it to diehard One Piece fans.

This game gets a lot of unneeded flak, and I can see why: the visual novel genre isn't for everyone. At its core, this game is basically a novel that has a pretty interface and an interactive narrator, that once you read everything available, you have to do a little bit of thinking and some work to get to the next part. There are also some REALLY clever puzzles in this game, including one that involves creating a paradox to achieve an ending that would otherwise be impossible.
If the words Ever17, Corpse Party, Collage, and 999 conjure positive images for you, then you will love this game.
If you've never played a Visual Novel before, there's a demo.
As for me, I think Steam needs to get some more Visual Novels.

I'm going to start by saying this: I started playing Mabinogi since late G2 when Paladins were a new thing and left when Alchemy came to be.
Recently felt some wanderlust for games I played in the past. One of them being Mabinogi, which was a fun MMO that introduced me to some great moments: Hanging out in the Resturant in Emain Macha, fighting in Coill Dungeon, Even soloing Rabbie Dungeon and fighting my first Succubus.
But anyway, the point I want to bring up is it was all awe inspiring to me back then. And after returning to the Land of Erinn, I can safely say that the feeling is still there for me. There is SO many new things that'll make your head spin. Heck there's still so much I've yet to find [I recently found out about transformations outside of the super forms you get]. The music is just as beautiful as I remember it being. Heck I still have one of the tracks on my phone to listen to. Gameplay changed a lot when they added a new action bar under the F1-F12 one. More buttons to press and more room for customizations. Speaking of which, the character customizations looked more flushed out than last time. So many styles and the like that I haven't seen before. Only gripe is the graphics, but at the same time, I'm fine with the N64 look.
I would say that if you want an MMO that's filled to the brim with content, try Mabinogi now. It's free to play, so the only thing you'll be paying for is time.

This game has steadily (about once every 2 months there is a large patch.)  been making great progress ever sense initial alpha 1.   Alot of people call it "vapor ware" but it is a smaller stuido making a very complex and interesting game.   Bottom line this is an alpha but its in great condition for an alpha.  It does have bugs yes but the core features are implemented and there is plenty to keep anyone busy.
Is this game for you? Maybe maybe not.  This is the true spiritual successor to SWG.  The crafting system is the most complex and challenging (in a good way) crafting system ive ever seen in an MMO.  It is also the most rewarding crafting system due to this.  When you actually accomplish producing something you feel as if you have accomplished a great task.
This is also a sandbox no hand holding here folks.  It does have a basic tutorial to get you introduced to the game but after that you better be able to tell your on tale and make goals on your own as to what you want to do.
Overall 8/10 right now due to alpha i will hold my 10/10 for release.  Would have paid more to play it and been perfectly happy.

Quantum Conundrum isn't a Valve game, but it really aspires to be. As everyone by now knows, Kim Swift was one of the key contributors to Portal and it's spiritual predecessor, Narbacular Drop. And you can't help wonder if Narbacular Drop would have turned out a little more like Quantum Conundrum if Valve hadn't turned it into Portal.
But her time at Valve has certainly rubbed off. You have a first person perspective, the classic Valve learning curve, a silent protagonist, a guiding voice, Team Fortress-style graphics, and no annoying cutscenes whatsoever.
Although it never reaches Valve's high quality-bar, QC is funny, charming, inventive and has just enough variety of puzzles to keep you going. It suffers from being just a little too easy (and I don't think I'm being immodest!), and from a very basic plot which only offers any true feeling of peril in it's closing minutes.
What QC does well is to remind you that fun and originality don't have to be confined to indie titles. Well done Square Enix.

While not the greatest DBZ game ever, its a huge breath of fresh air after the last several ones.
This game can be summed up as a more polished Battle of Z. It holds many of the same concepts like the team battle system but it doesn't feel like your forced to carrying your team all because one person made a single mistake. Although the battle system is a bit flawed due to the nature of Super Saiyans, the combat is pretty enjoyable and a bit deeper then it actually seems. Things get really interesting when you go with a more physical character instead of relying on using your Ultimate over and over again. That is something else to talk about, custom characters... THIS is a function that I and many other people have been waiting years for and even though it was first in Ultimate Tenkaichi, this game does it right... Mostly... The customization options are amazing and there are so many things you can do. There are only 2 things I wish could have been done better, hair and clothes. Anime is pretty notorious for hair but your character surprisingly doesn't have many options if your a Human or Saiyan. I also don't like how the males and females have different hair selections considering the options they have are pretty gender-neutral. Also Super Saiyan only turns the user's hair gold, it doesn't actually change it's shape. The clothes have problems in two different areas. The first is pretty well talked about being that clothes have stats. This sucks because it means you are not making clothes to look good but using them for stats. Either make clothes have no stats or allow the player to have seperate slots for what clothes are being used for stats and what are being used for show. The other issue is that most clothes can't be colored. Any clothes used by a character can't be recolored in any way meaning not only will many people be stuck with the same clothes for stats, but they will be the exactly same color too. The main problem with the game though is the RNG(Random Number Generator). This item drops in this game are so filled with randomness, this game might as well be called Dragon Ball RNGenoverse. It annoys me to no end when I complete a mission 10 times and I still can't get that 1 super attack or that 1 piece of clothing I so want.
This game overall is good, especially compared to last couple games that came out but it has some obvious flaws. Xenoverse feels like a huge step in the right direction but still needs a bit of touching up. DBZ has a pretty good track record for great sequels to stinker games, Budokai 3 and Tenkaichi 3 are two of the best DBZ-based games ever and both of those had pretty flawed first titles. I have high hopes for a Xenoverse 2 with more customization and many of the flaws ironed out. Despite that, this is a game every DBZ fan has to play at least once in their life, if only for the ability to make your own character.

Mabinogi is that crippling nostalgia that you have trouble quitting cause you wanna remember the good 'ol days, buuut those are gone.
Let the rant commence;
I would never recommend this game. To start off, it's a game that you're gonna come out of wasting alot of time on and with almost a perpetual sense disatisfaction because it is gonna twist your arm so damn hard to spend cash, especially if you feel like you're at a impasse and not making any real progress and after you made that progress than what? You can do Hardmode Dungeons or Phantasm or Alban Heroic? Ooooh, neat. Hope thats enough for you, if not tough luck cause thats all you have to look forward to. You could've also made 10x as much from those HEAVILY RNG based endgame dungeons by just doing gacha, which is the only frequent update to this game btw. That should speak volumes.
Plus, regardless of what this game's blind♥♥♥♥♥community says, it's dying. Slowly but surely, this game is dying. Sure, there may be pockets of activity from a good event that encourages you to stay logged on as long as possible (I've been playing for years, but alot of my time spent on Mabinogi wasn't spent actually playing it.) and from a gach bringing in a good handful of premium whales to supply them with the minimum to bother in keeping this game up and running, but those are when we get our bursts of activity and that has been the case for
.
The community is... unsteady ground because frankly it has some of the most autistic weaboos I've ever seen. It really makes me long for the days when this game was actually about norse/celtic mythology instead of a plethora of forgettable storylines that vaguely, if at all, connect to one another, creepy and revealing outfits that your underaged character can wear (seriously half the clothing designs scream that the designers have some repressed skirt and little boy clothing fetishes), and a whole lotta♥♥♥♥♥kissing on the forums that can turn rabid if you criticize too hard.  Not to say they're all bad of course, but... lets just say some can be rather bipolar and/or nauseatingly shallow, so be prepared for that if you do decide to play because frankly Mabinogi can sometimes be compared to the standard high school experience because the community are often pockets of cliques and petty drama. Sure, it's entertaining, but more than half our asses are too grown for this nonsense.
We got lacking content and a ridiculously strong biased towards the paying player (p2w basically, and cause I know someone gonna say it's not. Reforges. It's simple as that because even if YOU paid gold for them, someone still had to buy that♥♥♥♥♥♥ genius. With cash. Whats that? What about events? Well, what about them? You'll get a handful of reforges at best and anyone whose reforged knows it's the most ridiculously RNG aspect of this game. Sure, you could POSSIBLY get say r1 with less than a dozen or you could end up buying hundreds of reforges for some piece of gear for it to not even rank up. Frankly, reforges are a big deal because with them multipliers got introduced. You can deal some seriously high and consistent numbers with reforges that would beat a non-reforged player 20x over. Plus there are alot of other non damage reforges that can basically secure you a winning advantage. Now devcat is bad at balancing so instead of say AI improvements, HP (Hit Points a.k.a lets just make everything tanky) sponges, which make reforges all the more important and btw this game has a repair system with durability, uh huh, those are still a thing and them with HP sponges don't mix well. That isn't even mentioning that fairly often we get some pretty strong stuff within the gacha, like endgame equipment stuff, so imagine being someone who worked hard on a piece of equipment only for it to magically pop up into the gach with either a version similar or daresay better than yours.
"Paid hundreds to get r1 on a instrument? Well, ♥♥♥♥ you we're still putting it in gacha. Did you just spend millions of gold enchant protecting that armor for those heavy damage giving enchants? Okay, see now we gotta put your armor, those enchants, AND the armor with those enchants into a gacha. How do ya like them apples, ♥♥♥♥♥."
It comes to a point where you wonder what the point is in even working for anything.
This isn't the case with ALL equipment, since there is some endgame gear that has never made it into gach, but the vast majority of it has and the VAST majority of Mabinogi's equipment is gacha exclusive. Now I will say this 'equipment' is mainly fashion, but to a frightening degree thats the only part of this game thats still really catered to and thats because practically all fashion is gacha exclusive. HMMMMMM... is that a trend I see? No, it couldn't be.
My favorite thing about this game was probably the combat aspect. It had a very rock-paper-scissor type combat where you needed to choose how to fight based off what your enemy or enemies were about to do. I will say there is ALOT of variety in types of combat you can choose to use. This game doesn't go by a traditional class system as all classes are available to you to use whenever you like and that is only limited if you choose a race that isn't human. (Giants being unable to use Archery, while Elves can use melee but are extremely restricted in weapons and stats.) After a certain update, the strategical part of this game basically got nuked. See, the skills and classes are still there, but once you hit endgame you find your gonna be more often than not spamming one damn particular skill over and over for dps or aoe. Sure, you might switch it up a bit and spam another skill for dps or aoe, but the powercreep is so real with certain skills that its just so much less a hassle to just use that skill than kill more durability trying to hipster it out.
Don't get me wrong, I have alot of fond memories with this game, and I'll probably at least occasionally play (by that I mean more than logging on and afking) because I've made some good friends there, but as fond as I remember Mabinogi... it's current state leaves a pretty bitter taste in my mouth.

If you like One Piece or Dynsty Warriors you probably like this one.
The port is typical Koei Tecmo stuff. No mouse control, texture quality is quite bad even on "High". Definately played better with controller though I didn't have any problems playing on keyboard other than having to constantly reset the camera (I recommend you rebind the camera center key to Space or something like that). The game itself runs pretty smooth, no crashes, glitches or frame rate issues. Frame rate cap is configured or removed from the options menu, so at least there's that. Game has little-to-no AA and it can get a bit grating.
The gameplay is typical Dynasty Warriors stuff - take control of some overpowered character and proceed to barrel through thousands of enemies until you win. There's little to no challenge even on "Super Hard" difficulty, gets a bit grindy and repetitive. Has a huge character roster and many of them have alternate move sets depending on their costumes, mostly version before and after the 2 year time skip in the story.
The story covers all the major battles in the One Piece series up to and including an "original story" Dressrosa and takes quite a few liberties with it to make it fit the game. About 95% of minor/supporting characters are removed completely or replaced with generic NPCs. The rest of the story is told either in simplified cutscenes or in text summaries. Overall a faithful but lacking interpretation.
This is an incredibly enjoyable puzzle game. Although the story only clocks in at 3 hours the level editor and Steam Workshop ensure that you will have hours of fun even after finishing the game.

Analogue is like a digital book. There are a few images here and there (the images consist of two different AI characters, both show different emotions during the story), but other than that it's all text. And at times the player is asked to use some sort of command prompt. It's all fairly basic, but if you've never worked with command prompts it can be a bit tricky I guess, especially since there's a time based event later on in the 'game'.
Like I said, there's a whole lot of reading. In daily life I rarely read so it took a bit of adjusting for me. It can be boring at times, even though the story is solid. Just don't go and expect a proper 'game' here. It isn't anything like that. But if you like a good read I suggest you give this a try. You might just be surprised. I wouldn't really recommend it to anyone else though.
