----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
With regret, at this point in development 04/05/2015 I would have to give this a thumbs down with an advisory of "Check back regularly". I will periodically update the review as progress is made.
It has sparks of brilliance and oodles of potential unfortunately interspersed with some truly regressive UI/Gameplay systems coupled with extremely poor performance/graphics.(currently) Playing it I could not help the nagging feeling that a lot of the decisions relating to the gameplay experience are not taken primarily by a game designer as much as by a technical programmer (at this point). Just my opinion. Complexity is never a problem, Impediments to gameplay are.
A few points:
It was £14.99, could have been worse.(regularly on sale for about £11)
The animations/lag, performance and graphics/textures need a lot of work which is understandable, (Update 20/5/2015 - But disappointing after seeing the impending launch announcement. How much do games really change graphically from beta to launch, I can vaguely recall only 1 or 2 ever that drastically improved from beta despite all the rhetoric and promises. I have to say this team of devs are very communicative and the community (what there is atm) has been great and I applaud that and certainly hope they achieve what they want. Altho experience has taught me to be very cautious in my expectations with games in this position.)
The combat system has great potential.
(Update 20/5/2015 - Grown on me even more, very enjoyable and full of depth, multiple weapons, skills, stances, great stuff)
The gathering/ harvesting seemed slow initially and I was beginning to tire of the slooow progress bar but I believe it sped up after my skills improved, thankfully.
(Update 20/5/2015 - Gathering/harvesting is similar to fallen earth/darkfall. like it there? You will like it here.(Take note I am not talking about crafting))
The non combat skills/ non combat ways of playing show what can be done when the will is there. (Heavily influenced by what has come before) I did not think I would have any interest in the entertainer skill lines. Who knew...
(Update 20/5/2015 - Again, grown on me, love it. Multiple buffs, camps, no complaints).
The mission system - A nice idea but needs some serious work especially as it will primarily be what a lot of people will be doing at least initially. You basically receive emails from questgivers randomly from a pool offering you jobs based either on your skills or a filtered list you choose. Great idea. In practise however....
(Update 20/5/2015 - - The following has been improved, still very indie like, but better than before, still needs overhauling not tweaks)
The unhelpful dot system...(map/ui) is like going thro a timewarp. No names of npcs, (trying to hover over the tiny dots to get a name to show is not fun especially with moving colour coded, no explanation, npcs). No icons, no guide, no direction for quests (rarely or sometimes just counterintuitive with colour clashes and light dark issues) Instead taking the novel approach of having npcs that like to move about and also disappear at night. (inconvenient to you as a player, sounds good and immersive on paper.... its not) The only time I could tell night from day was the pseudo day/night cycle of entering buildings. Bright outside and eerily dark inside regardless of gamma.
Music and sound effects are buggy, raising in volume despite the ingame settings. Footstep sounds are located incorrectly on headphones.
(Update 20/5/2015 - no change).
Crafting/Looting Materials graded A9 -F0 ??? Looting an npc for C9 skins is very immersive..... which leads to...
The crafting system. Let me put it in perspective. 12 hours in (now 17...)(now... 27....38), having devoured every resource/guide for crafting on steam, the internet and ingame I could find I have still not crafted the first or any aspect of the robotics tree and accept that I probably will not in the forseeable future. (01/06/2015 I refuse to quit until i craft something in that skill-line) A first for me. Calling it overly complex does not do it justice. Insider knowledge is needed.(38 hours in I would adjust this statement to say it is just extremely convoluted)
(Update 20/5/2015 - Using a 3rd party craftmap utility combined with 3 (currently) google spreadsheets and going thro the  npc inventory and crafting database ingame I am breaking it down step by step what is needed, but is this a good design? Should I have to do this? How many will do this or even want too? Time will tell. It still seems too unwieldy to work. Applaud the concept but I still believe it will change. I have reached skill level 37 in robotics (01/06/2015 now 50s....) tho by applying skill points from a secondary xp system. (100 I believe to reach craftable bots, not the components)
Thread about how complex the system is showing components needed for 1 item only. This guy nails it:
I get it. This drive to get away from casual gaming. I am with you. BUT complexity for complexities sake is just wrong. The idea that you are going to get hundreds of players all specialising in individual aspects (not styles or branches of) each crafting profession so they can support each other on a server is beyond wishful thinking. I have no doubt this system will change, or adjustments will be made, before or after launch once its experienced by the masses.
Its a sandbox. (good)
Skill based systems rock. (and always have)
Performance is hit and miss and obviously needs work.
(Update 20/5/2015 - A lot of work considering the announced release date. 30 second lag upon loading in. Lag crossing server boundaries, random lag. Performance drops the longer your in game.(memory leak?) 10 sec lag when opening the new ui map. It goes on).
Aspects of it remind me of a cross between Fallen Earth/Star Wars Galaxies and Darkfall Online. (The original)
It truly feels like an alpha from many years ago with a lot of work/feedback needed. But an alpha with a hell of a lot of potential. I have only briefly touched on a lot of it. I could write a lot more.
Update 20/5/2015 - I think the only question is if you should spend money on it in its present state, not what it will be as your not purchasing that, as its going to release f2p eventually. You are buying this product as is right now. I think unfortunately 27 hours in I would just wait for the f2p release if I could go back. It needs a hell of a lot of work and seeing and playing it in its present state it feels a bit of a gamble how it will turn out. I would love for it to work out but experience teaches caution.

Well, it's been some time since I made my first review, and this game has been through quite a lot since then.  Some changes .. not for the better.
First off, the character creation really isn't much to look at.  Heck, there really isn't a point of it, as you'll mainly be wearing a full suit of armor 24/7.
They also completely changed the tutorial, which not only puts you with people of the other faction you start out with (that should have been a choice AFTER the tutorial) but it feels way cluttered and more confusing than before.
But overall, there is too much going on and not enough information about it.  You can't really talk in channels when you are a new player (just one for Newbies where no one talks at all), you need to spend a lot of time looking through the Game Database (as the tutorial and game itself doesn't explain a fair number of things), and it just wants you to do so much (which could have been spread out a lot better over the tutorial and the game itself).
With these new changes, I really can't recommend the game now until things get polished more.  It's an interesting concept, as there isn't that many sci-fi MMOs out there, but has a lot of work still to go.

TL;DR: Fun game, but lazy port (Graphic and online wise) and the developers don't even give a reason why we get the ps3 graphics instead of ps4. Let's hope the modding community saves us all. Come on, Koei didn't even bother adding controller button guides for controller users, they might ''think'' because it's PC we all use keyboard and whatnot... Ridiculous, they probably don't care for the PC gamers.
This game has been pretty fun so far. As a One Piece fan I would love to recommend this game, but this port does not deserve possitive ratings for the lazy job that Koei did.
The gameplay is a 7/10. Simple controls and combos, but it sure is fun beating the crap out of hundreds of enemies in front of you :). The difficulty could be much better imo. I would love it if boss fights actually made me feel like my life was on the line. Boss fights are simply all about button mashing and dodging a few attacks. Naruto games have decent challenging bosses sometimes, they could take an example from that.
Graphics... I give it a 7/10, but they could be a 8-9/10 if they didn't mess up: This is the no.1 thing that makes me and many people rate this game as negative. From what I've seen and heard the graphics are a straight up ps3 port, which shouldn't be that bad, but come on, PC is boundless when it comes to games. Consoles are restricted by their hardware forever, PCs upgrade/improve constantly. So why did they not give us the ''PS4'' graphics? I call this a lazy port.
Story, 9/10. Whether you know One Piece or not, I think the game does an impressive job of telling you what goes on and why, without going too much into detail. For the lengthy story of One Piece, I think they nailed it at story telling.
Soundtrack/Voice, 9/10. Voice actors are the same as the anime (japanese voice) which is amazing, best quality we can get. Soundtrack is alright, it can get a little repetitive sometimes, but it does its job.
Online/Co-op: 8/10 ... There is NO online mode. But hey, don't consoles have some sort of online mode? Well, that is a myth for us PC gamers. Apparently we dont get online functionalities at all. At least we get an offline 2 player co-op mode, which is pretty fun if you bring a friend over. Still, lazy port again not giving us online mode like on consoles.
For the first One Piece port, they did a bad job, or at least didnt provide any reason for their failure to deliver the best. If they ever release a sequel on Steam, I will definitly not pre order it until I see whether they care about the PC community or not. I'm dissapointed, but I'll make sure to have fun and get the best out of this game, which probably shouldn't cost £40 in its current state...

There's grinding, there's microtransaction, there's flashy anime costumes and hairstyles (most cost real money or hundreds of hours of your time to acquire).

Unfortunately, I cannot recommend this game.
Don't get me wrong - it's a fun game. And it plays well. And the developer is extremely active. The UI is absolutely atrocious, but you get used to it. Great flexibility and the ability to easily change classes by midgame. From a gameplay/value perspective, it is well worth your $2 and you will get your money's worth out of it.
However, most of the gameplay revolves around being at keys and waiting for tokens to appear on the screen so you can mouse over them. For hours. If this is your idea of riveting gameplay, this may be the game for you. Granted, most idlers involve clicking on something over and over or upgrading something again and again, but they differ from this one in a major respect - ClickRaid has no afk or offline progression to speak of. None. As soon as you miss the aforementioned tokens, your progress grinds to a halt...so playing this as a background game while you play something else is not an option.
Additionally, a newly implemented "Season" mechanic has split the community and found many of the seasoned 100+ hour players basically starting alt accounts for bonuses on their main accounts. And you have to party up - your progress will only be a fraction of anyone else's if you don't. This will happen on a monthly basis, so you have this to look forward to as well.
Like I said - I cannot recommend this game. But it may very well be the game for you, and so I leave you a fair review on it. The sound is good, the frequency of updates excellent and the developer involvement is welcome (though at times heavy handed). They have a Discord channel as well, if you're in to that sort of thing like some of these young whippersnappers are these days.

Quantum Conundrum - a game that sit somewhere in shadows of its more popular puzzle game brother - Portal. And while both of those video games are 3D puzzle games with platforming elements, the similarity really ends here. The concepts of the two franchises are different and I wish people would stop comparing them or claming that Portal will always be a better game without even playing Quantum Conundrum. If you're a fan of the genre, you will enjoy Quantum Conundrum even though it might be a bit too easy after playing other, similar titles.
But, enough of that. It might be already clear, but I did enjoy Quantum Conundrum A LOT. And I probably enjoyed it a lot more than Portal 2. Yes, the story is pretty much a filler, it doesn't go anywhere and the ending is a set up for the sequel (which hopefully will happen although I doubt it...). Yes, the puzzles are mostly pretty easy and after getting tricky they still can be solved in under 30 minutes, But I still enjoyed my time with Quantum Conundrum...
Its concept is interesting. The game gives the player the control over the enviroment instead of one particular thing (as with Portal and QUBE). It plays with physics letting you make elements weight more or less, slow the flow of time or even the entire gravity of the room. And it does so in unexpected ways such as makes you throw boxes so you can basically fly through the level using the gravity or lets you bounce on the platforms using a couch that you can make heavier and then lighter to fling yourself upwards. Those little mechanics that make the player say 'yeah, that clever' and then use those mechanics and mix them up in another level of the game. A concept of dimensions gives a bunch of possibilities for those mechanics and (again, hoping for it) there are a lot of paths that a sequel might take.
The puzzles are never too hard. Something I dislike about puzzle games is the difficulty curve that gets really high after a while without letting the player understand what he should be doing. Quantum Conundrum teaches the player its mechanics and does a good job at it also bringing back things introduced in previous chapters in the later ones. The player never gets stuck for good or frustrated that he can't figure out a solution. The levels go by pretty fast and it gives the player the feeling of progress which, of course, pushes him forward through the game. I never felt like the game is too easy. It gave me a good challenge showing me what I can do and then mixing it up and making me do it. I never felt mad at the game for having some riddiculus solution for a puzzle. It wasn't complicated. It was always a simple concept.
As for the story, well... I didn't really care too much for it and I don't think it is a bad thing either. The story was just there as a filler, the narration was okay and I see people really liking the professor. It just wasn't my thing, but it also didn't overshadow the gameplay. Everything is presented in a really lighthearted way, the graphics are bright and colorful and the overall game has a lot of character.
So what about the negatives? There are negatives. As I've mentioned previously - the story is just a filler, it doesn't go anywhere and since the checkpoints bring you back to a set spot, you often have to listen to the same voice clip over and over again. The puzzles are simple, but not too simple and Portal veterans might breeze through the game. There are also corridors between levels that act as hidden loading screens and a "story time" kind of deal. Those get repeated pretty fast and they're mildly annoying. The fact that they are in fact just a window of time for the game to load the next map, also might result in a bit of a frame drop from time to time. Also, I should probably mention that Quantum Conundrum loves platforming a lot more than other 3D puzzle games. Something you should probably have in mind.
Overall, I had a fantastic time with the game. It wasn't anything amazing, but it has a lot of potential and character to it and I wish we see a sequel one of these days.

Now everyone has to experience my Original the Character, SSJ VEGECCULO (do not steal!).  He's the grumpiest and strongest fusion in the universe.
In all honesty, I love this game.  I love it to bits.
I can understand the resentment for the grind, but with the Skill Shop in place, the grind is practically non-existent.  Namely, I could spend all my Zeni on the expensive skills, do a few more Parallel quests and probably nab a few of the lesser skills through just beating 'em, and have enough to come back and buy more of the expensive ones.
Now, this isn't to say the game is perfect or anything, as those aspects to the game, and many more, are still there and are certainly off-putting to some.  I've been playing MMOs for 15+ years now so, my views on the grind and difficulty curve may be different than others'.  The combat is still as fluid as just about any of the other DBZ fighters, and it's a great PC port.  The only things that bug me about it are, as other reviews have said, the lack of transformations for anyone except Saiyans, and the lack of actual "clashes", or whatever you want to call them, in the game.
For example:  In DBZ Budokai Tenkaichi 3, Krillin could get the powerup to "release his potential" during the Frieza arc.  Piccolo, could powerup twice with a "Nail Fusion" and "Kami Fusion", which would just buff him out.  Given, Saiyans would have *more powerups* than others because of the different levels up Super Saiyan, but still.  Frieza had some of the most unique options out there, with his regular transformations, or the amazingly overpowered option to get rebuilt as Cyber Frieza upon death.
As for the "clashes" I was talking about, ever since Dragon Ball GT:  Final Bout (maybe even earlier), if you fired beams head-on, a button-mashing or other type of contest would occur to see whose attack overpowered the other's.  Nothing like that is in the game, unfortunately.  The closest thing is, if you attack at the same time, you both enter a quick automated fight where you both bounce backwards afterwards, gaining a bar of energy in the process.  No interaction, no ability to overpower or anything.
It still seems like there's content happening with the game, however, as some of the problems I've read seem to be fixed.  So I'm hopeful, and still think the game's absolutely worth checking out, especially if you can grab it on sale.

Yes, even after 15 hours or more of playing Borderlands, I've still haven't completed the game. Borderlands is filled with adventure to explore and survive and with the additional DLC, it increases the playtime to a hundred. Thus, I have decided to be fair, since I haven't fully completed the story and I do not intend to due to the amount of games I have and also because this game is freaking long, I've decided to set this as a first impressions review and not a full review
Borderlands is a game developed by Gearbox Software and published by 2K Games. The game is a first person action game where you loot as many items as possible and have a huge line-up of guns and stuff. The story takes place in the fictional world of Pandora and you have the objective of searching for the hidden treasures of Pandora
There is a many story to follow, but Borderlands has so many side missions and places to explore, you will surely loose track of playing the main mission
The gameplay is simple, you shoot as much enemies as possible, grab their loot and upgrade to make your arsenal as good as possible. Over the course of the game, you get to explore parts of Pandora whilst taking contracts and following the story. To be honest, there were so many side missions that I kind of gave up with following the main story and I will just go onto YouTube and watch the ending there
Borderlands is known for it's shell shaded graphics and I must say that it really does make the game unique in its on way. The sound effects and animations especially during gunplay is amazing and so satisfying. The only thing I would complain about is the music, it's so depressing and low that it made me not want to play the game. So much so that I turned off the music and played my own
That is the thing I would complain about Borderlands, there are so many side missions that it is possible to completely forget about the main storyline of the game. To be honest, the game's storyline isn't the best I've seen. The characters are amazing and all have different character traits. My favourite has to be Claptrap who has such a wonderful attitude and makes you always smile after a difficult mission
The game is not easy, and as your progress through the XP system, the harder the missions get. So much so, you will die over and over again until you have enough XP to be properly upgraded to tackle the mission at hand. I thing I've got to complain about is the amount of back tracking the game has. Once you get a contract/mission, you go, fight the enemies and finish the objectives, then go all the way back and get your reward. And this is how the game is over and over again, the amount of back tracking really makes me not want to continue playing the game
And that is just one aspect why I do not want to continue playing Borderlands. I feel like I have played so much of it that I feel that I have satisfied myself enough to move onto Borderlands 2 and Borderlands: The Pre-Sequel which are lying in my library waiting to be played
Whilst you're reading this review, you may be thinking to yourself, "God, he's complaining a lot about the game", and in one aspect yes. Borderlands has some things that really make me want to complain about it. But on the other hand, the statisfying gunplay and character development was so good that it made me want to continue. But I personally felt that after the 15 hours or so of gameplay, I can't play anymore of Borderlands
Borderlands is a completionist's wet dream. To explore the planet and collecting sweet loot is amazing, but for a casual gamer like me who likes to start and finish a game and move on, Borderlands is a fantastic game but not a game I can finish
Borderlands is not for everyone but it is a game everyone should give a try and see if it's the game for them or not

The gameplay is designed to mimmick the tennis played by the pros on tour. All players have a set of stats spread into different categories (like Forehand, Backhand, Volley, Service, Movement and Special Shots) accompanied by a specific playing styles (Defender, Power Baseliner, Volleyer etc). All these attributes will determine how powerful and precise your player is and also how many errors they make. The aiming system takes some time to get used to, but you can easily configure the difficulty most suitable for you and practise in the Warmup Mode.
The graphics, reminiscent of the early 2000s, are the only downside of the game, while sounds are realistic (and different) for every surface.
Career (or World Tour) Mode is extremely detailed, with tournaments every week of the year (including Davis Cup and World Tour Finals championships), full rankings, head to head and other in-depth stats. You can create a new player or choose from the huge list of recent tennis stars and legends, from both the men's and women's tours.
Perhaps the best aspect of the game is the huge ammount of mods made by a dedicated community on
. You can add clothes, animations, courts, players or even completely overhaul your World Tour in order to perfectly simulate real life tournaments (for example ATP Patch and WTA Mod).

Hehe, a review for EVE. Where to begin?..........To be honest, there isn't a good place to start. The game is huge. The amount of things you can do are almost endless. Wanna go inside a wormhole and take your luck against the rats? Good luck. Go exploring in uncharted space? sure. Attend a high pitched battle consisting of 700 odd players because someone threw a fit over rights to a moon? If you're in the right alliance, go right ahead.
In the 13 years that EVE has been around, players have made history in the world of gaming, from the largest battle ever created, to some jackass diverting a force three times the size of his own in order to save a 4,000$ titan. The reason why these things happen is because of the complexity of the game. There are a 150 odd ships to choose from, hundreds of ways to fit each one, and the best part is, they're diverse. There're mining ships, ratting ships, PVP, exploration, capitals, and each one is bonused towards it's intended role. There's politics that affect each player. Recently there was (and still is) a war between an alliance called goonswarm and thier allies, and everyone else. The npc empire Amarr just hosted games in an effort to find the next heir to the throne, after their empress got killed by enemy ships. What I'm trying to say is that EVE is essentially a living, breathing universe. There is absolutely no reason why you'd get bored.
Alright, so are there some negatives? Yeah, a few, at least in my opinion. First things first, the learning curve is steep. Like, Mt. Everest steep. It might take a few days to get the hang of it, but there're people that'll help you. There's a help channel where your questions will be answered. That's probably the greatest thing about eve: the community is the most mature audiance I've ever been a part of. Another negative is the fact that you have to have certain skills to operate certain ships/moudules. All told, EVE has about 20 years (give or take) worth of skills. It'll limit you in the early stages of the game. Not by a lot, but it will.
Overall, this game is outstanding. There is no other game like it. Elite Dangerous doesn't even come close. If you can afford 15 dollars a month, I'd recommend it. Also, don't forget the 14 day free trial.

An indie game that relies on text to communicate it's story. You play a hacker assigned to retrieve data from a vessel that went missing centuries ago. It makes you feel like you're a hacker in a old computer system, trawling through files and occasionally figuring out puzzles.
It also has roleplaying elements as you are forced to interact with the ship's AI personalities whilst discovering (through questioning and reading) what happened on the ship. If you're a fan of anime and asian culture (specifically Korean? I think) then the depth the story takes you will be fascinating, if you're not as interested then you'll get tired of it pretty quick.
Upside, it's cheap and it's really short. There are multiple endings and the game has a deep story, if you're interested. If none of this sounds appealing, or if reading large slabs of text on screen troubles you, avoid this game.

One word describes this game fairly well: Complicated.
I'm not a person that jumps into an MMO for story honestly so I can't tell you much about that, but what I can tell you is that this game is a complicated mess of wonderful excitement and achievement.  This is a game that won't have you getting bored at end game and making an alt because you can do whatever you want for as long as you want and you'll be playing for ages doing so.  Or if you're like me, you'll be skipping all over the place and end up a confused mess.  This game isn't the prettiest game (yet?) but if you're into crafting, this game has that in spades. If you're into easy questing, once again, it's there.  If you're into exploring, there's a huge map to explore with massive environments everywhere.  If you're into a great community, I haven't met a single unfriendly person yet and I've put a good 40 hours into the game (I was playing before it was on steam)
This game sends you into a world like a baby, confused, barely knowing how to breath, giving you the basics that you need to get by.  You'll learn how complicated the crafting system is, and the basics of crafting but there's so much more to absorb it's quite overwhelming at first. If you ask people though, they'll always help you out.  There's so much to find, so much to do, and so much to craft it's insane. After 40 hours gameplay time I'm just starting to get my bearings on how the crafting system works, I haven't even looked into the housing system or anything else.  I've just been gathering and crafting for that much time.
All in all while you'll start out a bit confused, you'll learn, you'll laugh, you'll love, you'll get frustrated but you'll keep coming back for more.  I highly recommend this game for anyone looking for a deep, complex, smart game to play instead of "Collect/kill this many whatever and come back to me" kinda game.

After playing through the current version of the game it is fair to say that Repopulation has copied some things from SWG -- the worst parts -- then added some new stuff into the mix.
What did it copy? The grind. Yes, RePop is a grindfest of epic proportions. A second job if you want to call it that.
The claim of the developers is that the game doesn't have XP at all. Rather that by using skills you randomly gain skill points for that skill. The end result is the same, you progress by repeating the same activity over and over. Some missions do reward skill points but these are far from the primary soruce of progression. In some ways this is actually worse than SWG when you think about it. You level defensive skills by taking damage, so to progress you have to allow yourself to get hit -- how is that meant to be fun? Want to level resource gathering? You need to spend time cracking rocks open one by one and chopping trees down by hand. At least in SWG you didn't need to sit there repeatedly clicking the screen to level gathering skills. You would actually get more fun out of MS Word.
For some bizzare reason they claim their crafting system is inspired by SWG. Don't be fooled! They have completely missed the spirit of what SWG had for crafting. Resources do not shift or change in the world. They are static resource nodes. The quality of the resource is defined by your skill in extracting it. They took the idea of item and resource quality from SWG but removed the best parts which made the SWG economy feel alive. A unique item is certainly produced, but only due to random bonus events which sometimes become available for the crafter to use. Player A and Player B can easily make exactly the same item due to the mechanics so there is no way for someone to gain a reputation for being an especially skilled crafter.
Speaking of skills. RePops developers claim that apparently characters have no levels and yet they do have levels for mobs. So that basically means that players DO have levels, but they aren't displayed. Someone needs to explain to them that no levels means that you stand an equal chance of defeating all enemies in the game equally unless they are intended to require multiple players. Again, the developers seem to be intentionally misleading players who haven't played the game yet.
Next, you have the 'sandbox' element. True enough, you can go anywhere and do anything. Except that there isn't really anything to do. Your motivation? Gain levels. Collect stuff. Kleptomaniacs would love this but in this day and age MMOs have learned put enjoyable narratives alongside sandboxes and RePop doesn't do this. All missions are generic and there is no 'plot' which pulls you into this fictional world they claim to have crafted. It feels as if what made SWG enjoyable was its franchise and universe. RePop unfortunately lacks character and has a look and feel that is rather generic which contributes to its faults.
It actually kind of reminds me of Tabula Rasa in many ways... and that game didn't last long either.
Early development means there is room for change, but you would need to gut the game entirely and start over to get away from these failings and that isn't going to happen. I actually regret donating now, so save your cash until post-launch and see how popular the Repopulation is after a couple months.

As a kid, Mabinogi was my gateway MMO into playing other MMO's. It left such a good impression on me that every other MMO just doesn't give me the same experience Mabinogi has. Myself being a person who enjoys the PVP/PVE and RP aspects of MMO's, Mabinogi has everything you could wish for. It really is one of those games that has something and everything for everyone.
Character customisation, community guilds, quests, guild wars, player-run market, dungeons, hundreds of major quest-lines, constant new "generations" of main stories, player-hubs, homesteads, pets and other microtransactions, unlimited level cap, lenient skill systems. This is only some of the features of this game.
Personally, Mabinogi excelled more than other MMO's because of it's free combat and skill system. Although classes were integrated, you can switch between them at whill, for free. And at no cost. There is NO LIMIT to skill points. Although this may prove to be grindy, it's addictive and fun.
I keep coming back to Mabinogi, and I admit to have a profound love for the game- but unfortunately, I can never achieve that nostalgic, blissful feeling of jumping into an unfamiliar game, an unfamiliar world, and having no idea where to begin.
I wonder if new players still get that feeling I know myself, and so many others agree about.
Give it a shot!

a bit awkward. The sprinting is a bit odd, and I do think that your stamina lacks for the
most part. Not sure if I am doing something wrong, but I tend to find my character to be exhausted a lot. It does add a bit of realism, but a marine soldier should be in better shape ;)
Interstellar Marines also features two campaign missions, as well as an introduction course.
The introduction shows you the mechanics and all, which is to be expected. The campaign missions succeeds in delivering tense gameplay, which is very neat. At times, it can be more atmospheric than a horror game. The way the robots and environment is designed, can be very tense. That aspect of the game usually comes best to show in the campaign missions, as the multiplayer part resembles the usual shooter more. It has the normal gamemodes, such as DM and Capture the Flag (or points)
The graphics, sounds and lighting are all amazing, and adds to the atmospheric and beautiful part of the game. You can also customize the shadows, resolution and more, if needed.
As of now, the game only includes 2 weapons. You have unlimited ammo, but a range of 2 weapons still feels limiting. More weapons will obviously be implemented later, though.
Yes, it does lack quite a lot of stuff, and no, the progress that have been made so far is not overwhelming, compared to the amount of time used. But the people behind this game is truly passionate, and I am 100 percent sure that there is nothing they want more, than this to become a great, challenging and enjoying game.
TL;DR:
In this current state, I would not recommend it for the average gamer, looking for a shooter to play through. For now, it's a game to support and follow, and the devs makes sure to interact with the community. Buy it if you're ready to support Interstellar Marines on its journey. Hold on with your purchase if you're looking for a common full-game shooter.

The design for everything is like a Pixar film: bright, colourful and charming.
The gameplay is a lot like Portal: easy to come to terms with but requiring out-of-box thinking at times.
The plot -- or rather, speech -- you're constantly berated with is like a bad culmination of both: unending one-liners, bad puns, non-sequiters and dissenting jabs at your ability(s).
You're treated to four different filters, or dimensions as they call it, that impact on the world around you: fluffy, heavy, slow and reverse. Naturally you can only use one at a time but require multiple in order to solve the puzzles before you. Transporting large objects, for example, requires that you make it light (fluffy), throw it, slow down time, run round obstacles, switch back to fluffy and catch it again. The ways the game has you using these different dimensions in unison may not be initially intuitive, but they certainly arent illogical.
Its got that same wonder and feel to it that the original Portal did. I dont think the gameplay elements are strictly original, but the way it handles and presents them (much like its pseudo-ancestor) provides much satisfaction that it makes a rather hard thing to dislike. It perhaps skirts a little heavy on Portals tailcoat, but it'd be a wholly different thing if it didnt.
You won't feel bad for playing it, but you may feel a little guilty for giggling at the portraits in the games when viewed from different dimensions.

Quantum Conundrum is a puzzle game centered around a weird science contraption that switches dimensions.
Players take first-person control of a young child who comes to visit his scientist uncle at a crazy mansion. Upon arrival, the silent protagonist learns that his uncle is trapped in another dimension, and it is up to him to save his relative. In order to do this, all three of the generators in the mansion will need to be restarted.
The puzzles are made up of simple elements that are combined into complicated and elaborate puzzles. Puzzles are completed by moving around objects, which are mostly just boxes. Heavy weights are used to trigger pressure plates, boxes can be stacked to climb on, and there are a whole bunch of other unique solutions that are pleasing to discover.
This game is amazing. Quantum Conundrum is well made, it controls well and it is almost flawless.
It is perfect for people who like puzzle games like Portal. It is definitely worth to buy.

The game is amazingly well done, it's everything I always wanted in a DBZ game.
Pros:
-Loading screens are nonexistant
-Gameplay is really fluid and well done, NO LAG OR FPS DROPS - EVEN WHEN SPAMMING ABILITIES OR KI BLASTS OR ANYTHING (I run this on a Lenovo G510 laptop, you look up and compare specs)
-Pretty decent customization, though it can be a pain to unlock stuff though I don't really mind it since it's not a lot of grinding (Maybe 3-5 reruns of missions giving your wanted rewards at the most, normally 1-2) even though it's semi RNG
Cons:
- You need to know the history of DBZ aka MUST HAVE WATCHED THE SHOW otherwise you won't get a number of references in the scenes
- You won't be able to start off with a character and spam Ki Blast and hope to pass through everything, you actually have to learn to play the game/fight.  This is a fighting game NOT AN RPG (though it is semi online.... and feels a bit RPG ish)
- Not all parts of the DBZ series is included in this game, moreso the minor things like Frieza's two henchment: Dodoria and Zarbon though I still wish they were included
- NPC's can be a little dumb: it took me ~9 tries to do a mission involving Krillin's NPC on Namek because the mofo kept going off and getting rekt by a frieza henchmen, causing him to die and forcing me to restart the mission cause everyone on my team needs to survive.  10/10 for realism though
Maybe Pro/Maybe Con:
- You will actually need to learn how to play this FIGHTING game, aka pull combos off etc.  There may be a time when you get killed by Raditz, a Saibaman, or worse yet... Yamcha..... but it's all part of the learning
- The game cuts a few things out like the numerous forms of Frieza, which helps make the game feel less repetitive but might anger some people since they don't get to fight each of Frieza's forms
- You have to unlock everything on your own (costumes, abilities, transformations, etc.) - mainly through an RNG system via Missions/Quests based off the Campaign/story, might make having some things feel rewarding and worthwhile to use while also a pain in the butt to obtain
- Though Transformations (ex. Super Saiyan & Kaioken (x1, x3, x20) ) offer temporary powerups on damage or whatever while it drains your stamina, I feel like it's not important enough to consider it mandatory.  It's more for aesthetics, but still it does offer a temporary powerup boost.  Transformations aren't full, so if you have a character with Green Hair and go Kaioken, you get a Red Tint and Red Aura on your character.  Personally I don't find it to look bad and like it this way than the full color change when transforming but that's up to you to decide.
Overall:
I recommend this game to anyone who has watched DBZ as a kid and loved it.  Even if you still don't remember the story episode for episode (Like the time Goku spends 50 episodes charging a spirit bomb for Frieza), it's easily worth $25 if you buy this game for 50% off.  I think it would also be worth buying for full price at $50.... but that's up to you on whether or not you can wait for a sale/discount.  This game offers you to play via keyboard controls, but I haven't tried that and I personally use an Xbox controller instead (great gameplay with it).
tl;dr
Game is easily worth $25 - probably even the full $50, no performance issues + fast loading times (I run this on Lenovo G510 laptop), if you like DBZ BUY THIS GAME ALREADY AND PLAY IT ASAP

You're required to download logs left behind by the deceased crews of a spaceship and put them together to find out what happened. If you're willing to do just that, it will all makes sense in the end and gives a rewarding experience for you.
Don't let the animesque designs put you off. If you think this is some petty waifu simulator game for weeaboos, then you're painfully mistaken. You'll be too busy getting engrossed with the story. There IS a romance feature, but consider them as a bonus, since the main focus of the game is not about getting a virtual girlfriend for you; if you want those kind of VNs, look somewhere else.

Borderlands is a science fiction first-person shooter (fps) game with role-playing elements developed by the company Gearbox Software. It represents the first game in the Borderland series.
+ It features a grim and unclean cel-shading-look in combination with strong contrasts, which results in a cartoonish graphical style.
+ The unusual, humoristic events and cinematic moments contribute to the game’s atmosphere.
+ Elaborate loot system creates a broad spectrum of weapons and items that support different play styles.
+ Four classes with various skill trees and weapon priorities offer sufficient customization options.
+ Well done online collaborative campaign gameplay allows for a flexible and fluent multiplayer experience.
o Each of the four DLCs introduces a challenging mini-campaign.
o Solid sound design.
- Repetitive side missions offer little variety. Ranging from go-get-it-boy-and-bring-it-back, over collect-all-the-stuff-I-dropped to kill-a-bazillion-of-those. They are tedious.
+ Selected illustration of stereotypical side characters with a cynical attitude and wry sense of humour.
o Solid voice acting.
- Simple storyline. As if a lobotomized zombie has been given a pen to smear down a one-liner.
Borderlands is a challenging and entertaining fps experience with (over-the-top) humoristic moments, and the right amount of loot collecting aspects. However, the paper-thin story remains uninteresting and most of the monotonous side quests lack long-term motivation.
Estimated time for 100 % completion: +60 hours
Singleplayer achievements: 72
Multiplayer achievements: 8

Estranged may have been an exciting and interesting foray into a video game world a few years ago, but its archaeic puzzle designs and simplistic gameplay beg the question "What is this doing in this generation?" A Half-Life 2 Mod, Estranged tells the story of Fenwick the Fisherman on his journey through a spooky island community populated by ghouls and other nasties. Along the way you must solve physics puzzles including fan favorites such as the "Put A Crate on Another Crate" and "Throw A Rock At The Breakable Thing". The story and environment, while interesting, are nothing to holler about and the game itself is simple in both combat and puzzles. Many of the game's conundrums are over before they begin and the entire mod feels like someone spent an afternoon with the HL2 creation kit. That being said, the mod itself has great musical quality and the level design looks quite nice even in the post-Source age. Do these qualities save the mod, however? Unfortunately not. Even being free, the designers will have to think of some new tricks for Episodes 2 and 3, because if you've played Half-Life 2, you've already seen this mod.

Finally played this again today and remembered why I left.
With over 1,000 hours just in the steam verson of this game (thousands more before they connected Steam) let me try to sumise why the cute graphics do NOT make up for the complete lack of anything else resembling a game.
Quite simply, the leveling/skill system is so easily broken (especially if a new player does not understand how the combat power system works)-- there are items to make training skills even possible. Possible! Not helpful or easier, but literally POSSIBLE. Due to the massive influence combat power (CP) plays in the very basics of the game, it deters high-level people from playing with new people. Not that there are many people to play with and even fewer who are open to interaction.
While G1-3 and G9-12 have interesting storylines, all other generations fall very. very. VERY flat.
G18 part 1 is overly long and complicated (though the climax is thrilling, i will give it that), but G18 part 2 is... forgettable at best. Three of the five characters have no more personality than their name... which is actually just their profession ("Culinary Artist", "Starlet", and "Treasure Hunter"-- very interesting right?). Four of the five follow painful stereotypes which make them incredibly boring. Culinary Arist? he's fat and likes food. Treasure Hunter? he's tan and haughty. Also disappointing that of five characters only one is female and the only female is overtly feminine (quiet, withdrawn, compassionate, etc.)
G19 needs a MASSIVE overhaul; the mini bosses are so powerful they completely negate the literally divine powers aquired from earlier generations and have several attacks that cannot miss and can instantly OHKO you (this, on top of the fact that they ALL must be done solo, without dying-- for a supposed MMO it's a very individualistic game!) It's so backwards that there is a cutscene to tell you to use a shielding skill before the boss attacks-- but in reality the shielding skill does almost negligable damage reduction!
After just replaying one of the G19 battles, I will also add that the AI meant to assist you is completely worthless. They will go off and lose aggro for the boss, even if it is directly in front of them-- one will hold his sword over his head endlessly until the boss knocks him down.
Nexon the company is completely useless for support-- for TWO YEARS I was glitched (as in, I could not RECEIVE the quest to complete it) so I could not complete the final quest of G12- and their 'support' for this problem was that 'they do not provide walkthroughs for quests.' I'm fairly sure not receiving a quest is not the same thing as asking for a walkthrough, but okay, Nexon, whatever you say, I guess. (Two years later when G14 came out, the problem was patched).
Likewise, if you DO buy the premium currency/card/whatever- you MUST spend it. If you let it sit in your account, It will be automatically removed if you do not spend it. (I'm not even kidding, several times through the years I've had odd amounts of money be "spent" on Maplestory-- as low as 52Nx, or $.52, and as much as $20). This money is apparently removed because...? It prevents hackers? To prove it's real? I don't know, I've never gotten a clear answer from them.
Nexon is so awful at managing their game there were several hackers and scammers that were extremely popular for several years-- because they were never banned. Despite numerous complaints against them, they continued their game for years before someone decided that illegal and harmful activity should probably not be going on?
The game itself is glitchy and laggy and overall inconvinient. Just finished battling a tough group of commerce bandits? How about five more spawn there for no reason. For some reason the text used in game uses a ridiculous amount of resources to load, yet this has never been fixed. There's a recent problem where character's art appears OVER their text box making the text unreadable.
Much less important but no less vexing, almost all the female outfits have skirts/are overly revealing and there is a disappointing lack in unisex clothes.
In conclusion, what once made this game so disgustingly addicting was the social aspect. Perhaps having a group of pre-existing friends can help you with this, but as it stands the game is quiet and lonely-- and without a good plot to hold that together.... it simply falls apart at the poorly coded seams.

I wanted to log a few hours into this game before I gave a review.   Leaving a review of an alpha game is kind of tough so this will be more of a first impression than anything else.   I’m a crafter, so this review will come from that standpoint.
There is definitely a resemblance to SWG and Ultima online when you play this.  It’s a game where the crafting actually matters.  If you want to run dungeons to get uber gear this isn’t the game for you.  If you want to be known on the server for being able to craft some of the most sought after items then you will have a home here.
The crafting is immense and can take some time to get into.   Most items need many components to craft.  The components come from several branches of crafting.  You can learn them all but it takes time to raise your skill.  Some of the items you can craft are:
Robots (pets)
Genetically Engineered Animals (pets)
Implants
Harvesters (mineral, wood, water and so on)
Housing Items
Weapon and Armor Fittings
Vehicles
And many, many more items.
The crafting can be difficult to understand at times but the community is great help.  After about a week I was able to make my first robots.  There is a work order system so if you need mats you can request them there.  There is also the ability to have your own shop merchant at your house or in the city if you belong to a player nation that has built a city.
There will be nation vs. nation pvp and city sieges (Mechs).  There will be hardcore and standard servers.
Abilities include pet taming and vet skills (You can raise a mount).  You can be an entertainer or diplomat.   There is no class system, you only limited by the skills you pick up (and you can get them all).
There is definitely a lot more to cover but I haven’t gotten into much more yet.  I’ve got about 90 hours in and feel that I have barely scratched the surface.
If you enjoyed SWG and games like Dark Age of Camelot this game is probably for you...

Hehe, a review for EVE. Where to begin?..........To be honest, there isn't a good place to start. The game is huge. The amount of things you can do are almost endless. Wanna go inside a wormhole and take your luck against the rats? Good luck. Go exploring in uncharted space? sure. Attend a high pitched battle consisting of 700 odd players because someone threw a fit over rights to a moon? If you're in the right alliance, go right ahead.
In the 13 years that EVE has been around, players have made history in the world of gaming, from the largest battle ever created, to some jackass diverting a force three times the size of his own in order to save a 4,000$ titan. The reason why these things happen is because of the complexity of the game. There are a 150 odd ships to choose from, hundreds of ways to fit each one, and the best part is, they're diverse. There're mining ships, ratting ships, PVP, exploration, capitals, and each one is bonused towards it's intended role. There's politics that affect each player. Recently there was (and still is) a war between an alliance called goonswarm and thier allies, and everyone else. The npc empire Amarr just hosted games in an effort to find the next heir to the throne, after their empress got killed by enemy ships. What I'm trying to say is that EVE is essentially a living, breathing universe. There is absolutely no reason why you'd get bored.
Alright, so are there some negatives? Yeah, a few, at least in my opinion. First things first, the learning curve is steep. Like, Mt. Everest steep. It might take a few days to get the hang of it, but there're people that'll help you. There's a help channel where your questions will be answered. That's probably the greatest thing about eve: the community is the most mature audiance I've ever been a part of. Another negative is the fact that you have to have certain skills to operate certain ships/moudules. All told, EVE has about 20 years (give or take) worth of skills. It'll limit you in the early stages of the game. Not by a lot, but it will.
Overall, this game is outstanding. There is no other game like it. Elite Dangerous doesn't even come close. If you can afford 15 dollars a month, I'd recommend it. Also, don't forget the 14 day free trial.

If something as a neutral review was avilable, that would more likely be the option I would pick. But in the lack of it, I'm afraid at least from my experience with the game, the bad aspects outnumber the good ones.
On the good side, there is indeed an interesting variety in minigames, mutators and scenarios. Often implying a different strategy in order to attempt to win the game, or at least to prevent others from gaining more points. And of course, what else good points do you need for a fun party game experience? Nothing really.
Most of the bad points however come in what some may look as pet peeves, but at least my friends and I did find a little bit of a nuisance.
For starters, the "vanilla" version of the game (mutatorless) does appear to have a big flaw, which is jumping. It may have to do with the spacing of the platforms more than anything, but we really did struggle to get used to the platforming. You fall way too fast, and don't jump that high and while visually the jumps are more than doable, attempting to do it with a controller of any kind is more tricky than it should really be. And yes, double jump mutators and whatnot might solve this problem, but that is why it was mentioned it was a problem with the "vanilla" version. But without mutators, game such as the Death Race, are simply too hard to beat (at least, more hard than it should be).
Next is the lack of visual aid when it comes to identifying different platform "block types". When you play with the maximum four people at a time, most likely the screen will always display the largest view in order to keep in camera every single player. But when that is the case, it starts to get a little hard to distinguish between normal platforms, teleporters or other greyish elements.
Speaking of teleporters, it does seem a little broken that nothing tells you which teleporter is connected to which. Come on, even just colored lights would have been enough. For minigames such as "Escape From The Homing Missile" not knowing where a teleporter might take you could mean either going to a safe spot or right into the rocket. As sometimes it isn't as simple as "up and down" or "left and right". Sure, we can learn all the patterns after trail and error, but why did we have to go with the hazzle of learning that in the first place?
Also, before starting any new game session, you are told to select the type of levels that you want to play, and then you play a shuffle selection from that grab bag. But, was it really necessary to add the countdown on local play? I understand the need of it when the game is played online, but when playing locally, it just made us rush and many times not even select the maximum allowed amount, an interesting mix, a selection of those we havent played, or at least something that wasn't that monotonous before the time ran out. And that is another complaint for local play, why is there a maximum allowed of minigames to play? The fun comes out of the randomness and variety. Why limit the amount of variety you can have at a time? You don't go play Mario Party expecting to only play the different versions of Face Lift (A little extreme of an example, but you get my point).
As an additional minor (and I mean MINOR) complaint, the tutorials literally are reduced to: Use the stick to move, a button to jump, and "Move Or (you) Die". Sure, nothing else might be needed but... why was there no mention of teleporters? I know how they work, but as they were as gray as regular platforms we didn't notice most of the games had them somewhere, they blended in as some sort of "differently decorated platform". Or why said tutorial never made some mention that some games require a press of a button to do something else than jumping? (And yes, the last one sounds like my friends and I are lacking in the brain department in some way. But when you are talking and laughing, miss out to read the instructions, and the first minigame that you EVER play consists of laying mines with a button... what you end up with is a bunch of dorks trying to stomp, squish into walls, push to "cliffs" without ever trying to press a button) TL:DR, it might not hurt to add to the small tutorial: "Oh and listen, there are teleporters, they look like this. And some games require you to do an extra action, just use this button then."
Now, from a technical standpoint it appears that even on a 950M (Not too good, not too bad of a graphics card) with the appropiate clocking settings, RAM, paging, etc. The game seemed to lag a lot. I would normally blame it on the specific model of my laptop, but it does appear several other users have had issues with several different rigs. But that is more a case by case basis so I can't blame it on the game.
We also had some trouble trying to play with controllers and having them being detected, but that also happens on more games than just this, so again, maybe not a problem with the game itself. (I hope).
It is not a bad game by all means, but honestly, it was more of a "one-off" experience than something I would actively be playing with my friends. But if you believe none of the complaints I wrote are something you are likely to experience or consider a problem, then go for it.

The game started out as the most social game there was, in terms of player vs. player content. Vital flaws in core gameplay has been there for a decade now, but remains unfixed as CCP (the developers) focus on adding more microtransactions, more unnecessary gameplay overhauls. CCP has been going the same route that Runescape took years ago. Focusing on flash and desperately trying to "stay competitive", when such a thing is wholly irrelevant in the first place.
EVE is a niche game. It will forever remain a niche game, no matter how much CCP bends and spreads its butt cheeks apart to invite F2P players, making it easier to get into and easier to gain SP.
EVE was basically the last large MMO I truly respected. CCP stood their ground for 10 years, but I suppose every MMO eventually has to either go under or become a corporate money-milking machine that drains the last ounces of cash out of the players still playing it. All the luck to CCP in their future endeavors, thanks for all the fish.
Unless this game undergoes a complete 360 manuever, going away from a ridiculous micro-economy the likes which belong in EA and Ubisoft games, I will never give it another chance.

So.... I used to be a Naruto watcher. I loved Naruto... Naruto was my introduction to the anime world in my early teen years. So I'm biast.
UN Storm is amazing in so many ways.
1. Its visually stricking.
This game has such a great looking over-world. When you're Naruto walking in the Hidden Leaf Village, theres kids catching bugs, people socializing, and dogs running around... it's one of the most dynamic over-worlds I've ever experienced. Its not just NPC's standing in groups with dialog above them, it's like a real world.
2. The gameplay.
Its ALSO visually stricking! and I think that's one of the most important things about a fighting game. A bad looking fighting game to me, is a bad game. Visuals are a very important thing to me where skill isn't the most prevelent part of the game. Theres at most 3 combos, 2 ninjutsu, 1 throw, black and evade like in any fighting game, but the simplicity of the game itself is its own strength. This game very well could be the gateway drug to fighting games.
3. The story.
Oh god... so nestalgic. I've never finished watching Naruto because I started watching other anime and Naruto was over 150 episodes... I didn't have time to lock down on one anime and plus TOONAMI ENDED ON CARTOON NETWORK WHICH CAUSED ME TO HAVE SEVERE NIGHT TERRORS FOR THE PAST 3 YEARS. Finally playing through this game and seeing the end of Naruto Shippuden was very.. very nestalgic. I almost shed a tear. Almost.
Its a good game. and its only 10 dollars. If you have any affinity to the Naruto franchise, you owe it to yourself to own and play this game, even if you've finished the anime.

Estranged may have been an exciting and interesting foray into a video game world a few years ago, but its archaeic puzzle designs and simplistic gameplay beg the question "What is this doing in this generation?" A Half-Life 2 Mod, Estranged tells the story of Fenwick the Fisherman on his journey through a spooky island community populated by ghouls and other nasties. Along the way you must solve physics puzzles including fan favorites such as the "Put A Crate on Another Crate" and "Throw A Rock At The Breakable Thing". The story and environment, while interesting, are nothing to holler about and the game itself is simple in both combat and puzzles. Many of the game's conundrums are over before they begin and the entire mod feels like someone spent an afternoon with the HL2 creation kit. That being said, the mod itself has great musical quality and the level design looks quite nice even in the post-Source age. Do these qualities save the mod, however? Unfortunately not. Even being free, the designers will have to think of some new tricks for Episodes 2 and 3, because if you've played Half-Life 2, you've already seen this mod.

In DRAGON BALL XENOVERSE you revisit famous battles from Dragon Ball Z and GT with a custom character. Most important events within the DBZ & DB: GT timeline start changing in the worst way, Trunks is forced to request the help of a strong warrior who will help him to keep the timeline in the correct way.
You can choose from five races: Buu, Human, Saiyan, Namekian and a Frieza Race. Each race comes with differing stats. The character's look can be customized in a variety of different ways.
After the character creation part you are brought in by Trunks, who is a member of the Time Patrol and the action directly starts.
The gameplay is simple. You have 2 attack buttons and an energy shot button, a ki bar, a stamina bar, 4 super attacks, 2 ultimate attacks  and an escape move. Supers and Ultimates use ki and teleporting/guarding/escape moves use stamina.
The story mode is immersive, it is packed with interesting scenarios and intense battles.
Xenoverse operates like an MMO. Beyond leveling up and applying points to various statistics, you can purchase and use an assortment of clothing and special techniques for your fighter.
Alongside the story missions are offline and online Parallel Quests, which act as supplemental scenes to the main narrative. Here you also fight on the side of the evil guys instead of the actual good guys.
Once you unlock the entire roster, you will notice a huge lack of important missing character transformations and movie fighters, e.g. Master Roshi, Janemba, Majin Vegeta, Baby and more.
There is local multiplayer as well as an online arena. Unfortunately, most people who will challenge you for a PVP battle are using god mode. So, if you want to battle other players, you have to be careful with the decision for an opponent.
The visuals look pretty good. Characters look accurate and well made. The graphics are perfect for a Dragon Ball game.
The soundtrack is amazing. The background music, the music during fights and cutscenes fits perfectly. Of course you can also find the song "CHA-LA, HEAD CHA-LA!" in the game.
From time to time there can be online server issues and you will get disconnected or you just can not connect.
Overall, it is still a must have for fans of the Dragon Ball series. For others who are not familiar with the series it is probably too repetitive.

Dragon Ball Xenoverse is the best Dragon Ball game OF ALL TIME. All other Dragon Ball Z games are a cash grab so huge they fail to deliver a good product. Xenoverse, however, delivers a great game that is original. The story goes as follows. Something is messing with history, so Trunks summons Shenron to bring a warrior strong enough to defeat whatever or whoever is causing these distortions in history. You, the protagonist of this game, is summoned and is now your job to fix the distortions in history. From the very momment you enter this world, you are given an original plot line, which is different from the many other DBZ games. Which is why this game is so good, it delivers originality to the series. Next, the visuals are outdated by most peoples opinion, but the sacrafice was well worth it for that anime art style. Finally theres the gameplay. There is a simple fighting system that you would expect from a DBZ game. You can fly around, shoot KI blasts and punch. You are allowed to bring capsules on all of your fights that have effects such has healing you and your teammates and make you stronger. If these capsules didn't exist, this game would be impossible, but this feature also allows for more epic fights. The hub world of TOKI TOKI city contains shops, offline, online, world tournament and local fighting desks, shops, the time nest and paralel quest desk. Which brings me to the three modes of the game. Battles, which is standard in DBZ games which involve opponents fighting each other for fun, time patrols, which is where you do the main story and paralel quests where you can go alone or with friends to an alternate time line where certain people were to lose instead of win or it is in sync with the timeline. It is confusing, I know, but it just works.  Overall I give this game a 9.9/10 and a definate buy with DLC. Why this score? The Repopulation is a Sandbox MMO, and not just by title. I've never felt more free in an MMORPG than I have with The Repopulation, you can do weapon crafting, armor crafting, fishing, mining, log gathering, plenty of combat skills, plenty of generated quests (and I didn't even scratch the surface with this).  Don't expect some half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥cookie cutter "A to B" quest ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t.
You don't even have to do quests as a matter of fact. You could just gain experience doing other things. You will get sent quests via ingame mail and you can choose whether or not to do them. They also give you quests based on what you like to do, so let's say you only choose quests that have to do with crafting: The game will realize this and send you similar types of quests. There are also "Engagements" which are basically public missions.
Okay, now that I got that out of the way here are some of the pros and cons in my opinion:
PROS
+An ACTUAL sandbox mmorpg
+Tons of things to do
+ An in-depth crafting system
+ Feels like SWG
+ Nice soundtrack
+ Faction PVP system, where you have the option to go rogue and make your own nation
+ Caters to both PVE & PVP play styles.
+ Over 75 different skills to master
CONS
- (CURRENTLY) In late Alpha, so there are quite a few bugs (Disregard this con once the game comes out)

The only reason to play this game now is to hang out with old friends and run through stuff. If you want to play this game seriously, you need a lot of time and determination as there really is no level cap nor is there a super-imposed end game.
My advice to new players is to join Alexina server, as it has the largest surviving population and has a lot of friendly long time players that help out newer players, and start as the Warrior Talent. The reason for that is Warrior skills are the more useful skills to rank up in the early game. Also, one of the most usefull skills in the game (Windmill, which you should rank up first) becomes an apsolute nightmare to rank the higher your level gets. Leveling Windmill, Smash, and Shield Mastery will give you the best possible starting point to start ranking other skills.

Move or Die is a brilliant game!
So a quick peek at the type of games I own doesn't really lead to titles such as this (though since becoming a little obsessed with MoD I have bought "similar" games in a fancy schmancy bundle of couch co-op titles). I was enticed in by the Rick and Morty cameos and once I'd watched a couple of videos I decided to give it a go. Best. Decision. Ever!
The game is made up of multiple game modes to play online, via local network or just a load of controllers and a sofa crammed with four people. I personally tend to use a Steam controller or an Xbox 360 controller to play the game and find the controls pretty easy to use. Lag is occasionally a problem but this is always the case with online games, and shouldn't put people off missing out on this gem.
The rounds are basically mini games that you play against three other players (or AI bots) and you earn points based on how well you play. The points from each round are then added to your score, and the first to a predetermined amount (usually 50) wins. I really enjoy that when playing online, each player (not just the host) gets to choose game modes and mutators (minor changes to the game, such as jetpacks and double jump) that are played in each round. This is particularly good when your opponents have unlocked game modes that you haven't, and vice versa.
I did find that there was a bit of a learning curve with some of the levels. My first few rounds were abysmal! But once I got the hang of what I needed to do, I started to win rounds and eventually win matches overall! I find the daily challenges can sometimes be frustratingly difficult, but the game is so fun it almost doesn't matter.
The community itself is pretty much always friendly and fun, I've only ever once had a player throw their toys out of the pram, and this was just a case of a sore loser. It was a full on "ur cheating ermagherd?!?11!?!!!eleventyone11!11!!" and rage quit, but the game is wonderfully equipped to deal with people leaving mid game by applying a penalty to repeat offenders and retaining all XP earned whilst the opponent was in play. Thanks, devs!
It has now become an almost nightly ritual in our house to play the daily challenge and a few online matches. There's a fierce rivalry going on and gods forbid if one of us chooses a mutator that the other hates! It has yet to ruin friendships but I can completely see why it might!
DON'T GET BITTER, JUST GET BETTER!
I would absolutely recommend this game, and encourage those on the fence to just go ahead and buy it! Ahhhh go on.

This game should be considered something not easy to accomplish. The game is a pay2pay game, if you don't follow: After you pay for a starter pack on steam, you must pay monthly subscriptions, or try getting an item named "PLEX" (Pilot License EXtension.)
For those who don't know what PLEX is, and how expensive it is read on below:
- PLEX is an item which allows you to gain one month of gametime or to be redeemed for one of the rewards below:
- Gain 3500 AURUM, a currency which allows you to buy Ship skins, and Character clothing, and other services (see below)
- Gain 30 days of a "Multiple Training Certificate". If multiple characters are used (to a max of 3) on a single account, and you want to train both characters, the "Multiple Training Certificate" gives you an additional training queue.
Now that PLEX is out of the way with, i want to talk about the statistics of how money is being made, and how easy this "PLEX" is availible to get.
"PLEX" at the moment of writing scales from 1 Billion "ISK" (Ingame Currency: InterStellar Kredit), to 1.5 Billion "ISK". "ISK" is relatively easy to get in small numbers (especially with project exploration, if youre willing to be bored to death), but getting something about 1 Billion in ISK is something very hard to accomplish.
It is very hard to explain how this game works (VEEERRRYYY STEEEEEEPPP LEARNING CURVE), but as far as i know, theres 4 main roles in the game (as stated in special edition tab):
- You can be a skirmisher, who runs through "combat sites" to eliminate bad ships (PvE) and gain loot in exchange. I am not familiar with this, because i never took this path.
- You can be an explorer, someone who traces down space anomalies (Wormholes, Data sites: Read down below, Relic Sites), "hack" the sites, and gain (expensive) loot in exchange. This is quite a hard path to go down, because it takes a lot of money to get the equipment to be prepared for this.
- You can be a colonist (youre not really "the colonist"), which "colonizes" (more kinda industrialises) planets and exploits them in order to gain materials, which can be processed at the planet into end-products, which are worth quite a couple of ISK on the market.
- You can be a industrialist, which mines asteroids (ore can be sold directly) for use in blueprints, whereoff the end product results in either a ship, a module, or whatever you can come up with, as long as its nothing out of the ordinary (Special (event) loot)
But its quite hard to get started as i stated before. It takes a lot of time to get the starting skills trained (Skill system), even with the Prototype Cerebum you'll get from start (A one-time use item, which you can't buy, which speeds up training speed considerably). Training times can scale up to 1 MONTH, which basically means you should've either sold your "PLEX" by then (to speed up using skill injectors, for ~667 MILLION ISK) or you would've used your first "PLEX" by then.
So, i wouldn't recommend this to the average player, unless youre sitting on a pile of cash, and you want to pay your first 12 months training skills using the subscription system. DO NOT (unless you want a lot of ISK at once) BUY PLEX, because its a LOT more expensive than actually taking a subscription.

Dragon Ball Xenoverse is the best Dragon Ball game OF ALL TIME. All other Dragon Ball Z games are a cash grab so huge they fail to deliver a good product. Xenoverse, however, delivers a great game that is original. The story goes as follows. Something is messing with history, so Trunks summons Shenron to bring a warrior strong enough to defeat whatever or whoever is causing these distortions in history. You, the protagonist of this game, is summoned and is now your job to fix the distortions in history. From the very momment you enter this world, you are given an original plot line, which is different from the many other DBZ games. Which is why this game is so good, it delivers originality to the series. Next, the visuals are outdated by most peoples opinion, but the sacrafice was well worth it for that anime art style. Finally theres the gameplay. There is a simple fighting system that you would expect from a DBZ game. You can fly around, shoot KI blasts and punch. You are allowed to bring capsules on all of your fights that have effects such has healing you and your teammates and make you stronger. If these capsules didn't exist, this game would be impossible, but this feature also allows for more epic fights. The hub world of TOKI TOKI city contains shops, offline, online, world tournament and local fighting desks, shops, the time nest and paralel quest desk. Which brings me to the three modes of the game. Battles, which is standard in DBZ games which involve opponents fighting each other for fun, time patrols, which is where you do the main story and paralel quests where you can go alone or with friends to an alternate time line where certain people were to lose instead of win or it is in sync with the timeline. It is confusing, I know, but it just works.  Overall I give this game a 9.9/10 and a definate buy with DLC. Why this score? Being a Borderlands 2 fan originally, I came into this game expecting a product inferior to its successor. However, I found that Borderlands is a fun and engrossing game that rivals Borderlands 2 in almost every way. I enjoyed experiencing the title that gave the Borderlands universe its start and found it had a quality story, challenging gameplay, and the same vast expanse of weapons that are signature of the franchise. I would recommend this game whether you are new to the Borderlands games or even if you've already played the second game.
My praises aside, there were a few things that I found to be disappointing. This game is not as good as Borderlands 2. The story is interesting throughout, but ends abruptly and has little payout for all the work you did to get there. Secondly, the locations do not vary greatly from one another. The entirety of the game takes place in the same sort of desert environment, with very few exceptions. Finally, the last big thing that I found to be a flaw was the lack of customization. You're characters have very limited options in terms of skills and all the skills feel very inconsequential in terms of changing the gameplay. The skills generally just gives buffs to your character rather than change how you'd play. This lack of customization also carries through to the appearance of your character and vehicles, which is a bit of a nuisance.
Overall, I found this to be a great game and is definitely something a recommend checking out.
