This was originally an extremely fun game with amazing gunplay, with fantastic physics, hit detection, progression systems, and player customization. In fact, before I downloaded the game via steam, I had logged over 1000 hours playing via the game launcher. But that was four years ago. In the past two years, it has been completely demolished into one of the most horrible cash-hounding games in history by a takeover from a terrible game host named Aeria Games. All this company does is try to profit in any way possible, whether it be from making originially permanent guns timed, shoving horrendous AP offers in your face, or trying to create a shop system where it is impossible to play the game without buying AP. In a recent update, every single gun in the shop is timed if you wish to play with in-game currency, meaning that you will farm for hours upon hours on end and save every single euro just to see your gun quickly expire until you spend 20$ of real cash for each new gun. The bottom line is, this game was made into an intrinsic pay to play game by an extremely greedy developer. I do not recommend this game, not just because I don't recommend supporting the host, but because the host has literally ruined the game's overall balance and fluidity.
EDIT: The host, Aeria Games, is still extremely greedy and shoves cash offers in the most insane places, but the good news is they finally got SOME semblance of sense and brought back permanent weapons purchasable with in-game money. Now, these weapons are almost twice as expensive in some cases as they were before Aeria Games took over, but at least you don't have to spend any real money. I would recommend playing this game for the gunplay and the community, learning the recoil patterns and unique feel of each distinct gun can be a lot of fun. It is definitely not a spray and pray game like Call of Duty, and the ranks, progression, and supply points (for in-game currency) add a level of progression that provides an incentive to keep you playing that Counter-Strike does not have. However, I would still not spend any real money on this game, as every cash offer is a major rip-off.

First things first: it's a visual novel. If that's not your thing, this game offers no significantly different mechanics to win you over.
That said, it is one of the best games I've ever played. As an impartial observer of the past, you try to understand an entirely different people who lost their history and culture while isolated from the rest of humanity. You know they all died suddenly and it doesn't take long to figure out how. It's the "why" that drives you to complete this games gut-wrenching story, knowing all the while that it will be a horrific conclusion.
There is nothing happy about this game. It's the kind of story with characters that make you feel physically ill and events that make you shudder or at times angry. At any point in time, you can interact with two characters: one who disapproves of the world you're exploring and one who defends it.
In the end, it's a brilliantly written morality play where any good, justice or kindness are hard to find.

The game is in alpha, if you gripe about buggy stuff in betas, or full releases, stay away from this game in it's current state.  The game needs a lot of polish, and can, at times, rattle a nerve or two.  However, the game is fully playable, has a great community, great staff, and great development team.  You will almost certainly never see anything about thievery in the game.  Arguments are generally quick, and allowed to vent themselves out.  The whole atmosphere of the game is very helpful.
Developers are constant presence on the forums for, both, Steam and the main site.  In-game GM's are a constant, and interactive presence.  9.5 of 10 times you need a GM for something, there is one there for you.  You whispers GM's directly for any questions, or help with bugs.  For the most part, the community will help with trying to resolve your problems before you need to speak with a GM though.  We answer the same tired questions from new people like they did for us when we were new, and nobody complains about it.
Never be afraid to ask any questions in the game.  You'll always find someone to answer your question, and without belittlement.
As for the actual gameplay itself:
Pros -
1. There's an immensely huge crafting system that will wreck your frail little minds.
2. There's vehicles, and mounts.
3.  There's an entire line of skills and crafting focused around taming, training, and healing pets; which can be used as mounts as they evolve.
4. There's PvP.  However, atm the PvP system is a bit goofy, and arena based.  There are PvP contested areas in the world, but not currently activated for PvP combatants.  Like, you can go there, kill mobs and stuff, but can't be Pk'ed.  That will change with upcoming patches.  Also, there will be a hardcore, full Open PvP with loop drops.  This hardcore PvP server will be every definition of Hardcore.
5.  You can mine, fish, gather plants, log, and set harvester machines down to do the looting for you.
6.  The economy is player driven, so there is a lot of trade going on constantly.  I'm not going to lie to you though, at the game's current state, the market hotly debated upon.  There's this whole grade quality vs demand thing vs skill thing going on...  It would read to be more complicated and broken than it really is, so you'd have to experience it for yourself to understand it.
7.  There are many, many different wpn choices you can choose to specialize in.
8.  The world is huge, and it can take a long time to travel to some places.
9.  There's player housing, both, instanced and open world.
10.  There's player built and run cities.
11.  There will be flight.  There was talks that once drakes are tamable, you can fly them as mounts.
12.  There will be space flight, and other planets in future expansions of content.
I'm sure there's a lot I'm leaving out, but I've listed a good bit.
Cons -
1.  Endless bugs and glitches.  (it's alpha, stuff happens)
2.  The whole economy, and crafting system can be very overwhelming to new players.  At times it can still be confusing for old people.
3.  Crafting needs a lot of love.  There are aspects of the crafting system that are hotly debated, and need some serious tweaking.
4.  Not everything is in the game yet.  (like I said, it's alpha.)  Some things you're just going have to cope with.
5.  You will get stuck a lot.  Happens to everyone, and is usually fixable with a number of in-game commands, or other tricks.
6.  Things will go invisible, and you will have to exit to desktop a lot.
7.   The map systems are glitchy, and at times will white-out, blackout, or brown-out; causing you to exit to desktop.
8.  You're going to experience periodic server crashes.  They are not frequent, so you don't have to worry about crashing every ten minutes.
9.  Questing system is glitched, and needs a lot of love.  Some quest you cannot complete, the tracking system is far from helpfu, and the rewards need a tweaking.
10.  There is night and day system in the game in which NPC's are highly reliable on.  Most NPC's are out only during the day, but some are out only during the night.  This can make questing difficult, and confusing.
There's a lot more I could put here, but I'm not here to scare anyone off.  The overall game-play is still very fun, very doable, and highly worth it in my opinion.  As I've repeated several times in this review, it's an Alpha game, we as a player in an Alpha Phase game, you are /will be a tester.  Testers report the bugs encountered to help improve the game.
If you feel you can be patient, helpful, and want to make a difference in something, I encourage you to purchase this game and join us.  We're all friends here; even the people we dislike we get along with.  That's the type of community we have.  A good one.

Tennis Elbow 2013 is a MUST for tennis fans.

After 60 or so hours played in this game I think I'm ready to write a review for Click Raid.
I've always liked clicker games, but after a I lose interest in all of them - but with Click Raid's multiplayer it kept me drawn in because it didn't feel like I was in a solo journey - joining a server is as easy as it can get and there is a chat feature, so you can meet people and chat with them while grinding away.

It's really easy to present your suggestions there and get direct feedback from the community and the one man developer Slikey. This is the first Early Access game where the "We want to take feedback from the community" reason of going into Early Access is actually true. If you just take a glance at the change log you can see people's complaints and features are being swiftly implemented everyday which is what I like best about this game right now, every day there is something to look forward to.
When compared to other games I've played where I've spent more than 10x the price of this game and the hours I've gotten fom them then Click Raid definitely wins the trophy in that regards. 2$'s spent in return for 60 hours of fun is a win in my book and I plan to continue playing this game for many hours more.

Downloaded on Steam mainly to write this review.
So, first mistake most people make when approaching EVE is they look at it like a generic game. This is no game, this is a second life. A chance to be who and what you want all while flying some beautiful ships (or in the case of some reviewers your Pod/space).
Have I done mining? Yeah, have 4 alts just for that. Have I done PvP? Yes, high, low, and null. Mission running is a nice break from running sites for PvE and can make you some good ISK (in game money).
Are noobs constantly being screwed over? Only if stupid enough to accept duel requests or loot something that tells them (and they have to acknowledge) will allow EVERYONE to attack them no matter the security status of the system (suspect flag). Saw this when I was browsing the Early Access games. Was a little hesitant at first because most clicker games I play are FREE TO PLAY (with in game purchases) but for the £1.59 price tag I thought why not.
Started playing this game and straight away liked how it played. I'm use to playing Clicker games so it was easy to get into.
There is quite a bit you can do but still needs a lot of content added to compete with the other clicker games,
at the moment you have your basic objective of getting as high up on the stages as you can, Prestige whenever it gets slow and repeat. In between that you have Quests which reward you with Boss souls, and Damage Bonus% which allows you to get higher in Stages.
Boss souls are used for Artifacts which currently there are only 9 of those. Currently 15 heroes to purchase with XP which is like your gold from other Clicker games and only used on Heroes for now. Raid souls can be used to increase each Hero Defence and Power, Defence being a max of 90% and Power being unlimited.
Competitions happen every 24 hours and I believe they last for 24 hours. They are fun to compete with others but they do need better rewards.
Multiplayer is this game most fun part. Never seen it before and you see others moving their mouse pointers killing enemies and bosses trying to get further in stages, I'd also always recommend always joining someones room.
The Developer is one of the best I've seen in a while. Listens to everyone and gets those bugs/glitches fixed at an incredible speed. Suggestion are not taken lightly and strongly listened too. If you have a good Idea it will probably be placed into the game.
All in All, Very pleased with ClickRaid. Don't be put off by the buy-in price tag, it's the only money you will be spending. Others click games can have you spend £100's to get far if you don't wanna put time into it.
TL;DR Great game, worth the price. Needs more content but is still Early Access. Dev listens and responds. Fun multiplayer with up to 4 friends or players. 10/10 recommend.

Quantum Conundrum is a first person puzzle platformer in a similar vain to
and
. There really isn't much more to say.
The game was developed by (not so famous) Airtight Games - studio responsible for developing fairly mediocre (if not bad) Dark Void. With help however came Kim Swift, who used to work at Valve as Lead Designer for Portal. SHe took the position of director for this title.
In game, you take a role of a silent 12 years old protagonist, a nephew of Professor Fitz Quadwrangle on visit to his uncle's mansion. After going through the basics (short tutorial sequence), something goes wrong and you are left with a mission to restore mansion's power systems and eventually free up your uncle.
Main gameplay is fairly similar to the one from Portal. Each room presents some kind of puzzle, which you have to solve by using one or even multiple dimensions. There is however more jumping than in Portal. Actual precision and timing is highly required to solve many of them - if you are bad at this or simply don't like it - you may want to avoid this game. What I can say is that jumping controls are fairly precise - far more precise, than original ones from Unreal Engine 3, that this game is based on. So if jumping puzzles aren't a problem for you, you should find a game to be quite entertaining.
Unlike most Portal-like games, this game doesn't forget what made Portal good. It's not just generic Puzzle Platformer - there is some character to it. A lot of which is a result of great script, supported by exceptional voice acting of John de Lancie (known mostly for his role of "Q" in Star Trek, but also "Discord" in MLP:FIM and William Miles in Assassin's Creed Revelations and Assassin's Creed 3).
Other element that overall adds to game's character is graphical style. I wouldn't say it's a great looking game, but - it certainly doesn't look bad. Everything gives nice, pleasant impression of being almost hand painted. It's a lighthearted game and graphics style, humor and voice acting really shows that.
Overall? I think Quantum Conundrum is a great first person platformer. A price of 14,99€ may be a little high, especially when compared to Portal 2 (which offers far more content for this amount of money), but - if you don't mind jumping puzzles and you want more of Portal-like experience, check out Quantum Conundrum!

If you’re looking for a in depth game that rewards those willing to put in effort and work at something, be it combat, crafting, exploring, dancing in a bar whatever floats your boat. This is it.
While the game is Alpha at this stage with plenty of bugs and unfinished features it’s still more fun than any MMO I've played in years.  The Development team is the best I've seen in forever, the type I never thought I'd see again in this age of Early Access and Pay to Test.  Devs are on the forums actively responding to feedback, asking for information and actually listening to the community.  There are GMs online in shifts to trouble shoot issues and help gather documentation for the development team.  Really it’s something else.
The game itself is complex. So complex one could get a panic attack just looking at the crafting of something as simple as a combat knife.  It takes some effort but all the tools are there and the community is excellent even for an Alpha group.  So it’s hard to go too in depth in a review about any feature without writing up a huge section so I’ll leave it with general statements.  There is ton of information on the site and forums if you’re interested in more details.
Everything they advertise about the game is there and then some. It may not be fully fleshed out but the bare bones are there and one can get a clear idea of what the finished product will be.  It’s not like so many early access games, I’ve tried my fair share, that boost all these things they want then when you get in they have two or three things kinda working sorta and tons of features nowhere even on the horizon.   Repopulation at this stage has at least a skeleton of every major feature in place that I have looked into.  It needs a lot of fleshing out but it gives you a good idea of what they plan and that they are actually working to produce what they promise.
Updates are common, It seems they have slowed down to about one a month.  Slowed down to what most people consider the “normal” rate and many times faster than what I have come to expect from Early Access games.  But don’t let that make you think it’s just some tiny little fix a few bugs patch.  The notes are huge. Tons of changes, bug fixes, balancing and fleshing out content in amounts that are staggering.  Again, this isn’t something we should be so shocked or awed about as it “should” be the norm.  But again we live in the early access era.  Final note on the patches, I don’t remember the last game I was as excited about patches as I am with this one.  They put up patch notes as soon as they release the current patch and add finished features ready for the next patch as it goes along.  Really nice to have a Dev team that isn’t “Vague” on what they are working on.
If you do buy in know it’s not all peaches and cream.  There are bugs a plenty, crashes happen but the game is more stable than many “released” ones I’ve played recently.  It’s not optimized so at times it can be laggy, I have a pretty good rig so don’t notice it much.  Mostly when opening certain menus or entering a new zone.
Combat is better than I thought but still needs tons of balancing and is fairly simple.  There is a system in place for stuff like this attack causes this debuff so you use this one to trigger this debuff ect that’s pretty decent but the fights are either really easy or really hard.  There are some open world “dungeons” in place to give you a feel for what they plan and it works rather well.  But it still has a long way to go.  It is kind of complex in the mixing of different armor’s and weapons combined with the flexibility of the fitting system to the point there is no “best” build as all will work well used right.
Crafting is amazing. It’s why I first came here and I am not disappointed. It still needs some tweaks but it’s the first game in a long while where crafting wasn’t just important but the back bone of the game.
If you’re like me you’ve been burned by the “Early Access” so many times you’d rather walk into traffic than try it again.
This is the first one I’ve ever been truly happy with making my purchase and I wish I had started up sooner than later.
The last thing I can say is out of all the games I’ve played on Steam over the years, this is the only one I was willing to take my precious game time to sit down and write a review for.

Going to have to give this a thumbs down in it's current state.

The game has overly complex, poorly implemented, and poorly defined game mechanics.
Entry barriers, to do anything other than shoot stuff, are very high.
The crafting system is very complex, overly so, and relies on an in game database that is hard to navigate and only vaguely describes the processes required.
Combat is very weak, especially melee, and the mob ranking system is convoluted.
(sometimes a mob is easy to kill and sometimes the same mob will kill you in one hit because you forgot to take time to mouse over every mob and decipher the bizarro rank system)
2/3rds of the maps are PvP, only 1/3rd of the game maps are available to players that do not
wish to PvP.
The mapping system is both weird and broken, needless arrows constantly popping up, can't find mission goals some of the time. The minimap is completely useless and I covered it with the shift-m map (because the regular M map is totally trash no one uses it).
The housing system is not easy to use and provides nothing in the way of storage, it has no benefit except to set up a player store and that store can only be used if players stumble across it or you have sent them a waypoint to find it.
Progression is based on repeatedly using a skill and will require many, many, hours to gain ground. (casuals will not progress much)
Every activity is super grindy, you will have to spend dozens of hours searching and gathering before you can make even simple items.
The mission system is the same, repeat, repeat, repeat, with most missions just running back and forth for very little reward.
The game will cater only to the hardcore that can spend many, many, hours in game.
If you have no life, no job, no family, this game will help to fill that emptiness.
The UI is poorly implemented, windows are not locked to screen edges, text overlaps and overruns windws and text on the mission review is so small it is nearly impossible to read.
It's graphically at least a half dozen years out of date, characters are truly ugly and the maps are quite dull and colorless (with the exception of dull green/brown.)
Character animations are absolutely awful, very amateur.
Zone lines are the worst I have ever seen in an MMO, textures do not match and it is a horrific stutterfest of 2 FPS crossing them.
(oh what fun to stutter across a zone line only to be insta killed by a plant...)
Runs on the Hero engine...
I understand this is an "alpha" but as it sits this game has too many weaknesses and a super grind style gameplay that will only appeal to a small number of people.

No.

No.

The goal of the game is to find the saved logs and explore them, revealing the scandals, secrets and connections leading to the fall of the Mugunghwa.
VERDICT: Very short, but great game if you are okay with having to read a lot and not having a "real" game. Amazing storytelling, 9/10

Hero Siege, where do i start.
First off, i found this game a while ago and wasn't very interested in it because of the price, graphics and looked like a cheap knockoff of Diablo 3.
A few days ago i saw it on sale for $0.99, so i went and bought the 4 pack for $1.99 and gave 2 copies to my gaming friends. We tried it, one of them lost interest in about a hour and half of gameplay, while me and another friend somehow got hooked to this game even with it's really bad start.

Here are my pros and cons:
Pros:
-Fun if your into one shotting everything from 1-150
-Your friend can join you (my friend made a new character and i brought him through Inferno difficulty and got him to 70+ in levels)
-LOOT
-Neat and useful, sometimes funny relics (#StickmanSteveForMVP)
-Classes are for the most part distinctive in playstyles
-You can play with up to 3 other friends in a PRIVATE AND OFFICIAL SERVER (yes pls)
-You can also host an open server for people to join (good luck getting people to)
-You can name your character anything, and you can reset your skills, talents and even rename your character for an ingame currency called rubies.
-There's a leaderboard for Wormholes (endgame stuff)
-There's a chat section you can talk to people while you wait for your slow as hell friend to turn on what feels like his 1998 windows computer, get his dial-up running, and spend forever getting on skype and finally the damn game.
-There are many difficulties to go through while you level up which includes, Normal, Nightmare, Hell, Inferno, Agony, Destruction, and Toxic. Right now my paladin is level 145 and im finally moving to Destruction to hopefully get to 150.
-The devs seem to care at least a little bit about the players which is good enough for me.
-And most importantly, they have the best relic, Stickman Steve. His quotes are amazing, and his voice is that perfect type of annoying that you'll love.
Cons:
-Many glitches, but can be fixed by going to the next section of an Act (The game is divided into Act 1-7  and Chapters 1-5 for each Act)
-Your items not appearing when you get ingame (which ONLY happens if the server is down and you connect on peer-to-peer, since the items are saved server side, until the server is back up, you have no items)
-Server crashes happen 3-4 times in the past few days, but the devs said ti was because alot of new players joined and it crashed the servers, so they are upgrading it over the next little while to hold more players
-The damn animation for picking up potions that end up getting me killed once. At least there is a relic to insta-pickup items so it cancels the animation for picking up potions and relics.
-Dying resets ALL the relics you collected (when your playing with 1 or more people this only occurs if both/all players die.
-You only really need to put your skill points into health as items will increase your skills for you and Damage/Mana has an awful scaling per point you allocate to it, so it is only beneficial to allocate them into health.
-There is only one active guild i see on US that has a decent playerbase, and that is 3G, although i've made my own guild with just my friend and i, and we're having fun playing as the underdogs.
Overall, as bad as this game looks, i kinda have fallen for it. If your like me and dont mind the grind, even if it's 150 levels and like 6-7 playthroughs of the same maps and Act bosses, you should give this game a shot, especially if its on sale. And if you see me in chat (The Boss), feel free to join my guild or to start up a convo, cause we both know i'm just waiting for my 1998 windows, dial-up, slow as hell friend to finally get on.

As with all Visual Novels, the story telling is great! While maintaining the humor and action of the tradtional shooter games, the story is protrayed in such a way that can easily and cleanly wrap up the borderlands series. (Or at least Handsome Jack's Arc of the world since BL3 is in production...)
I love how games like this give you the option to completely define the characters to your perference. Rhys is a little bit of a hands on ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ for me due to the responses I picked, while Fiona is a bit more of a humble theif with morals looking for some more thrills in life. Completely diffrent then how my friend played through the game, and for him Rhys is a sweet guy and Fiona is a bit more of a ♥♥♥♥♥. It's really cool how you can deliver the canon story in diffrent ways based on your decions.
There's also some life lessons to be learned when watching Rhys interact with his life long hero, Handsome Jack, but who really cares about the meanifulstuff anyway?
It's a good game and worth a play if you're more into the lore side of Borderlands rather then the gameplay. Ties together many loose ends, and tosses in some shockers that will have to be addressed in BL3 since this game is confirmed for the canon timeline, happening after 2.
Not much replay value though unless you wanted to go through again and try being diffrent with your responses, (Example being: not a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with Rhys like I was lol), but there's not that many diffrent outcomes based on what you pick and the main story carries through either way.
It is a visual novel, and like any good story, I might give it a quick reread down the road. Personally it is my favorite Borderlands game.

A visual novel/adventure game. Colony ship was sent from Earth to distant stars but disappeared without a trace. Six hundred years later it was found drifting through space. Player’s task is to download ship archives and logs, but soon they will find out details behind tragedy that took place on board and led to ships demise. Two AIs could help the player, but each one is unreliable narrator.
This title holds special significance of being the first visual novel released on Steam.
Visual novel is a very niche genre and arguments are still raging if they can be considered "games" at all. Typical VN does not have much of "gameplay" but require a lot of reading; user input is limited to selecting one of answers in dialogues. On top of that, Analogue is very minimalistic graphically: it has only two drawn characters and mostly clean white backgrounds. However, Analogue provides additional means of player interaction - a computer command line in which you type to "hack" the system, gain access to various logs and move the story forward; it has even timed sequence when you have to prevent ship's reactor from exploding.
Not too lengthy, with nice music and intriguing mystery story this can be excellent entry-level visual novel. Don't hate Analogue, give it a try.

Although I'm not a big fan of shooters, I enjoyed Borderlands.  The cartoonish graphics and humor placed throughout the game meant that it didn't take itself too seriously.  I don't know what prompted me to buy it, knowing it's a shooter, but I'm glad I did.  I'm more into RPGs, simulators, and adventure games, and Borderlands has some elements of these; maybe that's why I was drawn to it.  Generally, shooters turn me off because I don't have the reflexes of a hyperactive adolescent to survive very long.  But Borderlands offers a somewhat non-linear play style--I hate games where you just run through a tunnel from start to end, even if it's carefully disguised to not look like a tunnel.  If a particular mission is too difficult, then choose a couple of different missions until you level up enough to get past the difficult mission.  I did that when I tried to battle Skagzilla.  I just couldn't survive even a few seconds worth of battle with this thing, so I went on to other things and came back later in the game.   Unfortunately, some of the boss missions must be completed to open the next map.  But once you figure out their weaknesses, it's not too hard to get past most of the bosses.  For example, I just stood by the entrance door to Sledge's lair and slowly weakened him over time.  Yes, most (but not all) bosses, you can leave the battle, do other stuff like refill your ammo and health, then return.
It was an eriee, suspenseful, and interactive experience. I recommend anyone who likes slender, gary's mod, and of course hal-life, to try out this game, it's free just download it and play!

Oh, holy hullnuts, where to begin?
My first impression of Gunpoint, on Greenlight, didn't really sell me on it. It looked like just one more pixelated, retro, run-of-the-mill Jump 'n' Run.
However, it is anything but.
Gunpoint is a tense, fast-paced spectacle of intuitive 2D-Action. You play as Richard Conway, a freelancing spy. During the game it is your job to break and enter several highly guarded locations. You're being helped in this endeavor by your bullfrog superjump trousers, and your smartphone, which is capable of rewiring an entire building. At the beginning ofthe game, Richard is framed for a murder he didn't commit and must now jump around like a frog on meth to find the true culprit.
I could waffle on about the graphics, but that would be tedious. So I'll say this: Gunpoint's gameplay makes up for it in a multitude of ways. There is never an unwinnable situation that you can't think your way out of. Sadly, the game is pretty short, clocking in only about two hours. But those two hours have more substance than every AAA-game of the last year combined.

I'm reviewing this based on hundreds of hours of gameplay.
The Steam hours played for me is not accurate, I use the launcher outside Steam so it doesn't count played hours anymore.
That said, let me start with the facts of this game:
- The community is small (at peak hours maybe 30k ppl will be playing it, in comparison to like 90k in a game like BF4)
- The learning curve is steep, very steep.
- You need real time to learn skills you can use in game
- A loss in the game has actual consequences
- Barely any PVE content
- PVP content only created by players
- Sandbox, as in player created content PVP and economy, nothing else. (this is not a sandbox game whatsoever)
- Graphics look good
Now let's get to phase 2, my opinion:
I have played this game for a long time. I can't say I have ever enjoyed playing it whatsoever. The only real sitisfaction this game gave me is when a skill completed. I am personally more of a PVE player, as I usually don't have time to get in a group, roam for a while and (hopefully) get some kills. Let me just say this, if you like pure boredom and PVE, by any means necessary go buy this game and install it right now! You will not be disappointed. The only PVE content in EVE are missions, mining and exploration. All three are extremely limited and not profitable in game unless you are lucky hitting a sleeper cache in exploration (only available to you if you have insane scanning kills, which take a lot of time to train)
PvP in this game is alive and well, so if you enjoy that, by all means try this game out. You will not be flying anything fancy anytime soon but hey, if you get a kill in a frigate class ship and you are having fun who gives a rat's @ss right?
Try joining a corporation as soon as you start the game, one that is active and can show you the ropes. Otherwise you will be stuck grinding missions from lvl 1 to 4 which feels like eternal damnation till you have waited long enough for some important and long skills to have trained.
I can't say more than this honestly, the game feels very inactive, the developer CCP feels very uninspiring to me and changes to the game seem to make people more angry than happy.
The player base can be very frustrating to deal with too, not a sentence is said without swearing, and taking advantage of people in this game is VERY common practice. If you want to be treated fairly play World of Warcraft on a PVE server, no harm can be done there. In EVE people will take advantage of you if you let them and scams are just as ordinary as burger joints in America.
Try EVE out, flame other people, rage from time to time, spin your ship around in the hangar for what sometimes seems for hours at a time, kill a mind numbing amount of npc or mine thousands of rocks and gain nothing in return!
All this for just $15 a month.

*Repopulation Status Update: This game is NOT dead. However, the game has now changed hands from Above & Beyond Technologies to Idea Fabrik, meaning further development will be handled by a new team of developers. It is planned to be released using the previous Hero Engine setup, not changing over to Unreal engine.
The Repopulation is a Sci-Fi Sandbox MMORPG that recalls many of the ideas that drew me to the MMO niche to begin with. One might choose to spend their time dancing or playing music at the bar, crafting top end vehicles for themselves and their fellow players, hunting down alien monsters, engaging in warfare with other players, or even building and decorating their own home in a player run city. And that is only scratching the surface.
I've tested this game for well over 100 hours, and I found it to be exceptional and a truly unique gem in the MMO market. It has a feel like the old days of Star Wars Galaxies, which is something i've wanted to recapture for a long time now.
Recent developments have been somewhat...traumatic. I adored the previous developers, and I'm as leery as anyone about what the future may hold for The Repopulation. But I refuse to become cynical about such a uniquely promising game without good reason.

Since this game has been out for 7 years, I'm only going to mention stuff that I feel others didn't touch on.
I actually beat the entire game. It was my first time playing it. It was fun. There are over 100 missions on the core game (without the DLCs) alone. Taking your time with the core game alone, the full game runs at about 55 hours. The three DLCs (minus Mad Moxxi's Underdome Riot, which I talk about below) adds about 20-30 hours to the core game.
I have a few criticisms:
1) I did not like the music. It wasn't bad, but I didn't feel like it matched the animation of the game. Add to that, they were all very ominous and daunting like the Fallout 3 DLC "The Pitt" and a) it can get exhausting listening to it for 55 hours, but also b) The scenes change in the game, yet the dreary tone of the music doesn't.
2) You aren't allowed to pick your mode of play (easy, normal, hard/normal, hard, very hard). After I beat the game once as a soldier, I wanted to play a different class (siren) on a harder level/mode, but unfortunately that wasn't an option. If you want the game to get more difficult, you have to beat the game but the caveat is that you can't play on a more difficult mode as a class you haven't beaten the game with, which defeats the purpose of wanting to play other classes with a challenge.
3) Checkpoints in regular game/"core" game act as checkpoints should. Checkpoints in DLCs ONLY act as checkpoints if you die. They don't bring you back to your last checkpoint if you restart/reboot the game which is inconvenient because then you have to spend anywhere from 5-30 minutes making your way back to where you want to start from again.
4) Mad Moxxi's Underdome Riot is an archaic DLC. If you want to know why, check my review on that too.
P.S. Steam's review process is defective. I tried submitting the review multiple times days ago and it wouldn't work.

Analogue's pacing was spot on as Christine Love continuously keeps the reader engaged in the story and the dialogue with the likeable AI heroines. The actual setting itself is highly plausible with believable journal entries and character interactions. There wasn't a moment where my suspension of disbelief was broken, allowing me to immerse myself into this enjoyable, albeit short, story.
The overall presentation was excellent; while it may be a superficial thing, I haven't seen a physical layout in a visual novel this aesthetically pleasing in a long time.
That being said, Analogue does leave something to be desired. While the entire tale is told in its entirely and its loose ends are cleaned up nicely, it left me feeling unfulfilled. At the end of the day, Analogue is less of a game and more of an interactive story. If you aren't the kind of person who enjoys reading, you're probably going to want to pass over this one. I would give this game a solid B+; I highly recommend it.

I've been following TRP for a very long time and am probably one of the longest running testers outside of friends and family.
To start off, TRP certainly harkens back to the golden age of sandbox MMOs and heavily references titles from that era such as Star Wars Galaxies, Vanguard, Anarchy Online, and even Ultima Online.
If you cut your MMO teeth on World of Warcraft, and you liked it, bu and play TRP at your own risk.  TRP is sandbox, not a themepark.
***THE REPOPULATION IS A SANDBOX, NOT A THEMEPARK***
You set your goals and you achieve them. Simply leveling up skills for the sake of leveling is meaningless in this game.  It's what you can contribute that matters.
A lot of player's first mistake is assuming that the game revolves around your character; it doesn't. There's no hero's journey here. TRP revolves around real, tangible accomplishments.
Last night my nation, the 47th Legion, found a city plot and began construction of our base. That base means 1,000x more than my personal character achieving grand master in rifle skill. In a sandbox like TRP the character progression is completely ancillary to server accomplishments. This is a game about learning where materials are, how to refine or manufacture awesome stuff, finding a patch of dirt to call yours, taking said patch of dirt away from people you don't like, exploring, building your brand and/or businesses, building a community, et cetera.
In TRP you actually have to accomplish something that matters.  There's no race to max level, there's no instanced raid progression, there's no gear treadmill; you just go out into the world and make your way however you can.
If you want some real freedom in an MMO for once try out TRP.  If you need to be led by the nose and constantly handed feel-good-confirmations and gear trinkets hit the back button right now.

I didn't know what I was getting myself into when I first launched the Demo for Analogue: A Hate Story. All I knew was my opinions on visual novel games were shifting and I was in the mood for a sci fi story.
My initial thoughts were thus...
"What Da Fuq am I playing?!? I'm shifting through dead people's blog entries on a derelict space vessel that somehow became feudal Korea!?!? Why's the ship's AI dressed as a teenage schoolgirl and explaining how women weren't included into family trees to me!?!? I can't pronouce any of these goddamn names?!?!"
It was borderline maddening, I felt like i was missing something and pressed on with the full game, hoping I would find the hidden meaning of Analogue.
And man I did...
Analogue, although appearing very basic, even rudimentry at face value; is one of the best, most cleverly written story I have ever enecountered in a game. What begun as what seemed an unassuring story twists into a dark, unsettlingly detailed tale about the lives of the people who lived centuries before you whose world inexplicably came to a sudden end. And as you read more you feel it, the mounting fear and tension inside you, unable to divine the story's next turn. As the tidbits of the plot are revealed non-linearly, you start conceiving your own nightmare scenario. Its a lot like reading a suspensful horror novel; its not the words that scare, its your own imagination that conjures the most unimagination thing possible. Thats what Analogue makes you do, it makes you visualize a world you cannot even relate too by our modern perspective and bias. Than add in what must be one of the scariest twenty minutes in my gaming life, as well as multiple endings; and what you have is a sublime testament to narrative, pacing and delivery in gaming, or storytelling for that matter.

This game is more like detective game mixed in a with chose your own adventure novel but is affected more so by what you choose to find out and how.  Do mind you, there is a lot of reading in this game, but it's not without some memorable characters as well as AI personalities that change their behavior as well as what they reveal to you depending on your research/reading and answers.
The game is set in the future and played through a pseudo command console/user inference with human-like AI personalities that react to what logs/mini-stories you show them as well as how you respond to their questions.
Advice for enjoying this game: look for a character you care about and dedicate yourself to finding out more about them.  Or...if you find yourself unimpressed by the people you're reading about, try digging up dirt on the AI's that are trying to assist you, there's some bizarre twists for all of them.

Okay so... This game mostly grabbed my attention on the fact that... Well, dragons. Plus the retro look got me extra interested. So I got this game on the spot months after playing the demo. And I friggin love it. The plot is as simple as, a group of baby dragons were born while their mother was taken away by evil robots. The group's first instincts are as follows.
1. Realize mother is missing
2. Steal a bunch of weapons and clothes
3. Let's shoot some robots.
These are the strangest baby dragons in existance and yet the coolest. Also why is there only three in the intro when there's four elsewhere? Not to mention they all have names if you check the original website's press kit page and look for the images of the four characters.
Blue Dragon: Larimar
Red(Orange?) Dragon: Ruby
Pink Dragon: Coralie
Orange Dragon: Amber
Okay so chances are the pink and orange one are female judging by the names. But I'm not very sure at all honestly. *shrug*
That aside, the game is simple bullet-hell like platform shooter game. You get your basic yellow blaster. (Which is actually a robot arm. Who knew?) No ammo limit but you gotta spam tap the heck outta it to kill. Kinda hurts after a while. Although there's a machine gun that has rapid fire automatically. Every weapon has a super ability and all of them provide super fire power with infinite ammo for as long as it last and you can hold the trigger for the time being. Execpt for the laser weapon. You just get a screen-wide laser sweep. But that's cool too! The game's soundtrack is one of the biggest things in this game for me. It's so catchy that I bought the soundtrack only a day after I played the full game! I must admit, the main theme (Named, "Dragon Bros!" which plays at every boss fight.) really gave me that, "Intense, energy rush" feeling. Like I HAD to win this for the sake of myself. It motivated me to keep on trying no matter what. And I love it when music gives me that vibe. It's all the more worth listening to from there. Now then... The bosses. The game's bosses don't grab my attention too much in any way at all really. But I love em otherwise.  Just nothing worth pointing out. Soz. Although I do want to point out that I love the game's sense of rhythm in it's music. 90% of the time things in the level will be moving in some way to the beat of the music. Even traps! It's quite crazy and makes you want to just sit there and shake your head doesn't it?
So let's chop things down into simple to understand bite-sized pieces.
Gameplay: Bullet-hellish Platform Shooter
Main playable characters: Larimar (Player 1) and Ruby (Player 2)
Plot: A group of baby dragons get their mother taken away. And what do they do? Steal weapons and go on a mother fricken hunt.
Overall this game derserves as much as it can get. Considering this game is still in early access however... I do want to say that I'd be careful buying this game if I were you. As chances are, it's in developement hell. I'm hoping it comes back out and gets on the move. Because I'd hate to see this game go to waste. I really would.

The mechanics for this game are great, the dialog is pretty amusing at times, the graphics look really good and it had a nice humour to it. I just didn’t feel too great about this game, and after a little while it became a chore for me to finish. All in all it’s still a good game, maybe other people feel differently about it to how I feel.

pros: innovative puzzle mechanics (consisting of fluffy, heavy, slow, and reverse dimensions that can alter physics and objects in the level), stats and collectibles are available for completionists, enjoyable soundtrack, and an art style that gives this game a unique aesthetic.
cons: platforming can be tedious, some lag spike issues, better dialogue is desired - because the main voice tells dry jokes constantly and gives hints to a puzzle when you don't want hints. And there is a level near the end where you have to stack 15 boxes to get to a higher ledge... some level designs are definitely questionable. You also can't quick save/save slot, there is an automatic checkpoint save but you can't even load that file, so when you leave the game you have to start from the very beginning of the chapter.
Overall, most of the early puzzles are easy and I did find a few that were challenging, some level designs could of been improved, and the single player campaign takes around 5-6 hours. Quantum Conundrum season pass comes with additional DLC missions (reviews on the comments) and a soundtrack folder.  And for those who didn't know, this game was directed by Kim Swift (ex-Valve employee,  designer of Portal).

Dragon Bros is a traditional 2D side scrolling platform shooter for single player or local co-op.
You play as a cute dragon against robot enemies which come at you from the sides and above and burst into fiery explosions when defeated. It's family-friendly (no blood or gore) and has a retro feel with button hints being displayed on old gameboys, a fun little detail.
The enemies drop coins which you collect to charge up your Y button which you can then activate to boost your weapon for a few seconds. There are also occasional special weapon pickups (shotgun, laser, machine gun etc) all of which last for a few seconds before you revert back to your basic gun. The screen works in a kind of ratchet method whereby once you've moved right a certain distance you can't then go back/left to pick up any missed coins or weapons, which can be a little frustrating. At intervals you're given the 'halt hand' and the screen stops for you to clear a blizzard of enemies before you can move on to the checkpoint which usually follows. There are 3 or 4 satisfyingly tough bosses to defeat throughout the game, and this is where I would particularly appreciate full auto-fire to save my poor trigger finger.
The game has a main map showing your route and checkpoints, but you can only jump in at points showing a trophy. There are points in between but nothing happens when you try to select them, which is confusing. Speaking of confusion, having defeated Professor Processor the game seems to be telling me that I've completed it, but the level overview shows a final section which is unreachable. It's possible that this is a spare section earmarked for new levels yet to be implemented. I don't know.
There is a storyline but there's not much to it, and if you want my opinion this obsession gamers have with storylines is ridiculous. Why would you need one for a game like this? If you want a story, read a book or play an RPG.
You can use keyboard or controller, although this type of game really needs the controller. The default button mapping is a bit unusual and takes some getting used to. There are 3 controller mappings available in-game but none of them have twin-stick mode which I think would be better. The left stick is used for both moving and aiming; you can aim left, right, up and diagonal and you do a lot of upwards shooting at the flying robots. You can hold left-trigger to anchor yourself in place and fire around you but I found no use for that at all.
I used the default settings with my Steam controller and it all worked as expected, although my trigger finger was starting to ache after a while because the auto-fire is quite slow so you have to pump the trigger to fire fast, which you want to do all the time!
I'm not good at these types of games so I put it on the easiest setting (out of 5) but having no co-op partner makes it twice as hard so overall you could say I was on medium difficulty. With that said, I think they've got the difficulty just right. It was challenging and I had to retry some sections many times but none of it was impossible. Early sections were nice and easy, and on harder difficulty settings I think it would challenge even an expert player.
It has a chunky, pixelly retro vibe and chiptunes to match. I can imagine myself playing this on a big arcade machine back in the day.
I agree with others who have said the camera view is far too close. It makes the game feel cramped and you don't have enough warning of the incoming enemies before they're upon you. By the time you read this it has probably been fixed already, as there is an update promised soon to address this, so no worries.
I played mostly on Linux, with a bit of testing on Windows just to make sure. The gameplay is smooth and responsive, no lag or glitches. It does have some strange behaviour in Linux if you try to switch it to windowed mode so don't try. It's best in fullscreen anyway, and can handle up to full 1920*1200 resolution.
11 achievements but they seem to be out of sync. When I get an achievement, it then drops the previous achievement I got. For example, when I defeated Professor Processor I didn't get that achievement but instead my previous one (Beekeeping) dropped instead.
Steam Cloud support which works cross-platform!
The store page says it has Trading Cards but there are none at the moment.
In-game stats but no Steam Leaderboards, which could be a nice addition.
As far as I can tell I completed the game (see above) and it is rather short for the price. It has a lot of replay value though - you can try to beat your times and go for harder difficulty settings. The good thing is that you know exactly what you're getting before you buy - the store video shows what you can expect, it's a side-scrolling shooter, so if you like this genre then I think you will enjoy this game. If you're in any doubt you can try the demo version.
There's nothing unique or ground-breaking here. It's a straightforward platform shooter, well executed and a lot of fun. There are still one or two rough edges to iron out - it is in Early Access after all - but nothing too serious.

Alright. I'm a huge One Piece junkie. I've been waiting for this game for quite some time. But I'm also very adamant about my video games so I'll do my best to stifle my bias for just a little while so I can discuss some pros and cons that I see evident already.
Pros: The game plays smooth. I have a decent rig 2.8 Ghz i5, 8gb ddr3 gskill ripjaw, 4gb EVGA Nvidia 970gtx, and a 3tb hdd. I've never hit a hiccup and I wouldn't really expect to with this set up. So if it doesn't play smooth for you, don't shoot me for saying it runs well on mine. Personal experience.
It holds very true to the story. The depiction of the canon story hasn't been done so faithfully in any other iteration of the franchise that I've experienced yet. There are mini events you can trigger which work outside the norm such as [Spoiler!!] Iron Mace Alvida showing up in the first Buggy mini arc when she didn't team up with him until after Buggy got btfo the first time. [End Spoiler] That being said though, it isn't immersion breaking.
Combat depth and combos flow very smoothly and it doesn't feel "jumpy" like I did in One Piece Unlimited World Red.
Stat complexity and customization is very deep and you can adjust particular characters stat priorities in any way you'd like to fit your (or the characters) play style. Of course, this isn't too big of a deal if you're playing on easy or regular because the game is easy on those settings, as it should be. Playing on hard should ensure a level of challenge to the point where character customization is something you should pay attention to and not "auto assign" your tokens.
The cast! Any fan can appreciate the number of playable characters which have their own unique spin to them that depicts their fighting style or devil fruits very accurately to the manga/anime.
Now time for some cons.
I won't sugar coat these because they irk me.
I use an Xbox One controller. But... for some reason, all the key prompts on the screen are still stuck as if I'm using my keyboard! This is immensely annoying for someone trying to start with the gamepad seeing as there is no real correlation between what button POSSIBLY COULD BE and what is mapped to the keyboard. So upon trying the game out on a gamepad for the first time, you'll have to do some trial and error. Which I did and I accidentally released my Kizuna Rush while there weren't a lot of enemies around. Annoying! Pls fix.
This game is near impossible to play on the keyboard. This gets a line all of its own. Then again, this game was developed for consoles and controllers so take that as you will.
Its a PS3 port! Noooooooo!! I didn't spend this kind of money on a computer of this caliber, to have Koei Temco port a version of the game from last gen. I'm very disappointed in this.
And finally, the lack of an online co-op mode. This would have been a fantastic place to allow One Piece fans to meet and mingle through different mediums!
All in all, this is a good game. It feels good, it looks and runs good, and it holds true to the One Piece story that we all know and love so much. Our favorite characters are portrayed very well and it SUUUUUUUUUUUUUUPERRRR satisfying to lead a huge group of enemies in line for a massive 100+ KO special :p
Keep in mind that this is a fan game. Most people who aren't interested in the One Piece universe probably wont be picking up this game but if there is someone who you want to get into the story and hasn't been receptive, this could be a perfect opportunity to invite them over for some 2 player local co-op to ignite that beautiful spark and pass on this story to even more people.

I despise this game. Truly and utterly.
I remember when this first came out, I was expected updated graphics, voice acting, puzzles, and story.
What I got, was a lazy re-release of the original with the added bonus of not having to switch disks. Woo.
Hal's voice acting is exactly the same from the original. All of the lines of dialogue, save for the obvious villain, is the same but with different voice actors, but why couldn't they get a new voice actor for Hal???
I liked that they kept some of the old music from the original, but interspersed was music from other games (specifically in Maxine's Diner with the Phantom of Venice club music that is totally out of place for a 50's style diner).
One would also think that if they're going to cut corners and reuse old assets (and seriously, the only changes to the environment where tiny things like books in the library being replaced with callbacks to older games, adding in vending machines, getting rid of the payphones, and a handful of other minor changes), you'd think they'd take more time to work on the character models, the dialogue, the story, SOMETHING!
Similar to the original, there's not many puzzles, just 18 coded messages from a dead guy who I'd honestly like to kill myself with how horribly his clues are written (just be sure to find ALL 18 with their code signatures, or you'll be stuck guessing randomly at the final puzzle)
I mentioned earlier that the villain is obvious, and they are if you're familiar with the story of the original. The final confrontation is... less than impressive. Just like the rest of the story~
The story is the exact same from the original with a small addition shoe-horned in to give it a different villain, but similar ending.
I wouldn't recommend this to anyone ever. I'd much sooner tell people to play the original, 2 disk struggles and all, than this garbage.
Don't waste your money.

Lots of potential, lots of fun in Multiplayer, and hell, just doing co-op is fun! Helps you work with friends and even random people, when they actually LISTEN... alas, first world problems.
Devs are rarely responsive to people who send them actual input on how to fix things, and game lags everywhere, especially in the storyline missions. NeuroGen Incident map is REALLY laggy, but fun. Good for a scare, as the CTRs make sounds that are akin to Aliens, and can sometimes come out of nowhere, reminiscent of Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Vegas 2 on the XBOX360. The reason NeuroGen Incident is usually so LAGGY, is because when you start, they LOAD THE ENTIRE MAP. You can glitch things to not happen in order, which isn't how it's supposed to go, but best to go in teams of two when doing such things, makes the game more interesting. The lag is what kills it though. The other co-op map, Assault on StarCrown, is much better, as it MUCH smaller and deals up larger areas, making it a player favorite, when it IS available.
Servers in Co-Op are, sadly, set to their maps, and DO NOT CHANGE, when it should. For co-op, though, there are only two maps for a storyline, where there are almost a dozen mixtures for much smaller maps, and even several that deal in the multiplayer maps of taking out the CTRs, survival, objectives, etcetera.
Do I suggest this game? When it is fully completed, or if you really want to get in on stuff and even be on the list of people who helped support the game in early access, then feel free to buy it. It's fun either way, much as it still has a LOOOOOOOOOOONG way to go.

One of the few games out there with such depth.  I've just completed my second week on this game and have been amazed by the vastness of the world and item (read: crafting) system.  I've never played Ultima Online or Star Wars Galaxies, but other players ingame say that those are the closest comparisons.  I like to think of The Repopulation as a Runescape on steroids with a touch of EVE Online. While I could talk about various aspects of the game, I'm going to focus on crafting which seems to be the strongest point in the game currently.
Pros - Crafting
There's a highly complex crafting tree for making things like weapons and armor, vehicles, consumables etc.  I specialize in Armor Fittings, which enhance the stats of your armor.  Unlike most MMOs out there, the armor and weapons themselves don't matter as much as the fittings which you insert into them.  In order to craft Armor Fittings I rely on other players to harvest ore, wood and plants which I then turn in to refined metal bars, firewood and chemicals to craft the components that I will eventually need to make a single fitting.  If no one is gathering Calibrite Ore, and the auction house is empty, then I must go out and gather some myself.  Armor Fittings are one recipe of the larger Armor Crafting discipline, which is itself one of several hundred skill paths players can choose from.  The interesting thing is knowing that you rely on other players on your server to gather materials that you can't gather, and to craft items you can't craft yourself.  While you can theoretically DIY, it takes significantly longer than bartering and buying/selling to and from other players.  Plus, advanced items require dozens of ingredients to come together.
Cons - Crafting
The system can be daunting to players who are used to very simple crafting systems like World of Warcraft and other theme park MMOs.  In a theme park MMO you would mine ore, refine it into bars, then use that to create items.  On The Repopulation each ore gives different properties to a finished product (armor penetration, damage, resistance, movement speed, critical hit).  Ores also come in varying grades with a letter prefix A-F and an integer suffix 0-9 which can only be harvested by those with high skill in the corresponding ability.  So to make a very good quality Armor Fitting I would need to hire a Master Miner, and a Master Ore Refiner just to ensure that the metal bars I have are the best possible.  I would also need a Master Forager to gather plants, and a Master Chemist to synthesize the compounds I need.  I could do it all myself, but training 4 skills to such a high level would take months to attain.  Recipes are highly complex, and you will find yourself opening your web browser to check on agents, and sub-ingredients to make those agents quite often during crafting.  Once you do get the hang of it, though, it gets much easier and manageable.
Cons- Other
The graphics leave something to be desired.  The engine seems old, so the models ingame from players to NPCs to the environment are lower quality than most people are used to in 2015.  As an alpha game there are some bugs and glitches that still need to be ironed out.  You can phase through objects when zoning between areas, and the combat seems clunky rather than fluid.  With a still new player base, everyone's still in that learning process so it gets frustrating at times when trying to find others to help you build cities or craft items that you need.  The game is not easy to play and requires some thinking.  After playing the game for two weeks it feels like I took college courses in Chemistry, Geology, Mechanical Engineering.  If you're looking to just zone out, then the crafting system isn't for you.  But the combat and doing missions is still very viable for someone not looking to get too involved.
For a quick overview here are the numbers:
There are about 15 different weapon types you can choose from.
There are currently 100 or so skills you can choose to specialize in.
There are around 1,000 recipes to choose from when crafting.
There are 60,000 levels for each skill.
Level 500 Mining took me about 1 week of gametime to reach, but each higher level takes more and more time.
Simple crafting recipes require about 4 different ingredients to create.
Advanced crafting recipes require about 20 different ingredients.
There are 52 types of harvestable nodes in the game (ores, wood, plants...)
Each harvestable resource can be further broken down or combined with other resources to create even more complex components.
Quick Tips:
There are no levels in this game besides your levels in each skill.  Someone can have 6000 points in Fishing, but have 0 in Combat.
Monsters become easier/harder to kill depending on your weapon type and your armor type.
To get "better" weapons and armor, you must add Fittings to them to add stats.
Weapons and Armor have almost no stats besides Physical Resistance without Fittings.
The world is mostly player-owned apart from the starting cities.
The economy is 80% player-run and 20% vendors and NPCs.
The world is large.  It takes a very long time to traverse the landscape on foot, which is made easier with vehicles.

Secrets Can Kill was the very first Nancy Drew video game and was originally released in 1998.  Twelve years later, Her Interactive decided to give the game an engine makeover and re-release the game in 2010 capable of running smoothly on modern Windows computers.  The original game remains intact, only the engine displaying it is updated so the original acting, story, gameplay, puzzles and graphics are still there.
There is no doubt that Secrets Can Kill shows its age.  The update is great and makes the game installs and plays smoothly (we tested via Steam) without any problems on Windows 10, which is great.  The game is much shorter than, say, Shadow at the Water's Edge, which was released right after the 2010 remake of Secrets Can Kill.
The game is a classic, it started the entire Nancy Drew series and is well worth a play.  My eight year old said that even she still enjoyed it very much, while obviously not as good as the later games.
The acting on this original title, as the writing for the characters, leaves them extremely flat.  They don't really feel like living characters at all and it makes it hard to really be pulled into the game.   The number of locations is very limited, although this is pretty common in the Nancy Drew games in general.
Overall the game is dark and feels a bit creepier than it should because of the flat, lifeless characters and the sense of being "trapped" unable to explore very broadly.  The game has some dark elements and the puzzles are a bit hard and non-intuitive.  You spend a lot of time looking at bulletin boards and in the end, none of it makes any sense.  But it has such historic importance to the gaming franchise that it is valuable for that reason alone.
Overall the game is worth playing, but very weak.  If you are looking to test the series, this is not the title to try.  If you are dedicated to playing through the series in its entirety, then this title is, quite obviously, a must.  And starting with the 2010 remake is not a problem at all as the game play elements are left completely intact.
If you don't mind a bit of reading, want to try something a little different and love a good story, I'll recommend this!

This game has a fair bit of promise to it.  The plot is sadly barebones/nonexistant as of this time and you're unceremoniously dropped into the action; great if you want to just jump into the action, less great if you want to know why you're a dragon kid going around shooting everything up.
The gunplay feels really solid.  The base gun isn't bad, though one-shot-per-button-press is pretty annoying.  If it would slowly autofire (with the Ultra Combo system letting it go into hyperdrive) with the option to button mash for hairy situations, that'd be much more enjoyable to me.  Other guns feel really satisfying (especially the shoulder-mounted Laser gun which makes your char grin in glee when wielding.)
Boss fights are definitely pretty enjoyable, good rhythm between dodging bullets, dealing with mooks, and trying to find moments to unleash hot lead into them.
Music is also pretty good and solid overall if you like chiptunes.
Overall I'd say if you love Contra run-and-gun action, pick this up.
EDIT: The autofire addition was patched in, as was being able to swap away from the big guns to save ammo.  Always awesome seeing devs listen to reviews!

Well, this was a small surprise. This is an original game built on the Source engine and Half-Life 2 assets. It's free to play too.
You're a sailor who is having an accident with his boat, crashing on the shores of an island. The place seems abandoned, and indeed, you quickly learn that not everything is as it should be. Something has gone wrong and you'll get to trek around the place to figure out what's going on, and trying to help the people you meet.
What I first noticed was how good it looks, considering it's built on what seems to be an earlier version of Source. The second thing was the atmosphere, which I think they did a very good job with. The place really feels abandoned, and it's accompanied with well-timed, atmospheric music. It seems obvious that they found a lot of inspiration from games like Half-Life 2. While using several assets from that game, they have really managed to make it their own creation.
The characters you meet have been given convincing voices. The game is also sprinkled with clues and memos, including newspapers, scribbles and interactive workstations. They managed to get a little humor in there too. The game is absolutely linear, but here and there are rooms and places you can explore, even though they rarely hold anything useful, just like in real life. At times the game seems a bit stretched out though. Some parts could've been skipped without hurting the story and experience.
It took me about 2 hours to finish. After finishing the game I noticed I had some achievements left, so there's a little bit of replay value there. This is just act 1, so there's more content to come, but I know nothing about it. Apparently, Occulus Rift is supported for those that have that option.
I don't see any reason not to try it out, considering it's free. I think it was surprisingly good.

The story might be the weakest part of the game(writing-wise, else its quite well executed for what it is) . Someone is rewriting the history and you need to stop them but first you need to set history on its normal course which means that you gonna take part in big fights from the manga/anime. There are cutscenes in both anime(2D, trying to make you nostalgic) and in-game(3D) style. The story is quite short(I needed 6 hours to beat it)  but in between each Saga you can do side quests to level up. By doing story missions you unlock masters and side quests to bother with later on.
Here comes the important part of the game.
Combat is Faaaaantastic. It almost grasps the feeling from the manga... apart from the long charging scene filled with useless dialogues... there is none of it...  but the fast paced action is there to stay.
During fights you have 4 basic attacks : normal and heavy attack, range attack and throw attack(combo from guard and range) . You can also dash from danger, then you have 4 super attacks that can be ki bursts,strikes(physical attack), transformation,power ups and "other" . If you decide to save up Ki you can use ultimate attacks which often are varietion of super attack but stronger. At at the end there is 1 last skill slot for evasive moves. I used controller and didnt really made sense to me to have 7 skills and having 1 empty button. 8th skill could be for transformations but thats only my opinion.
At times combat may feel repetetive(only if you make it so) because you may end up doing same combo over and over again until you change your skill set.
The game lets you make your own Avatar in DB universe(you can still play as other characters if you unlock them). Creator isnt that great imo but still does the job just fine. You can change height body,hair,skin and such but the variety isnt big. There is even voiceover but yet to hear my character say a word.
In the game you can wear different kind of clothing and can even try to make yourself to look like your favourite character. Sadly the clothing is bind to different playstyle so you either pick your skills first or your clothing and work from there.
Also a bummer is that not all clothing can be dyed the way you want so you may end up just like everybody else.
You have 4 clothing slots(top,lower,hands,feets) that nets you bonus stats. Then you have Accessory of your own choice that is only visual gimmick.
Last but not least is the Z-soul that offers passive and active bonuses(those active during combat but its RNG based for most part).
Lets not forget and the consumables. You have 4 slots to use during combat so pick carefully what capsules you gonna bring with you. There isnt much variety but they usually either provide regeneration to HP,Ki,Stamina.
Apart from main story, game offers side and parallel quests. Side quests are often links between different main story events while parallel quests let you redo main/side quests but from different perspective(in main you fight against vegeta but in parallel you both are allies) . By completing main/side quests you unlock parallel quests that you can farm with other players for items/skills(unlocking stuff in general). While you can do parallel quests with other 2 players(either online or offline(in offline they are NPCs)), in side and main you are on your own.
Game features Master system. What does that mean? That you can be a student of manga's character and if you train enough he can teach you new skills and even help you out in fight. To unlock masters you need to finish main story missions. Then you have to find them in Toki Tiki(there can be only 1 master spawned at a time and they refresh after every completed quest). Once you pick a master, they will teach you one of their signature skills, use it in combat to master it and then go to be tested by the master.  Rinse and repeat till you fully unlock the master. Then you can change your master and do it all over again. Over time you can talk with you master and they can give you consumables or materials to help you out.
During missions if you use your scouter(you always have it even without having it in your accessory slot) you can find items on the group to pick them up.
When you defeat your opponent there is a chance to get material,clothing or even learn a skill.
While getting drops is RNG based, finding the dragon balls is squared RNG.
1. You need to find a mission that can spawn time patrol(aka other player's character) 2. Start the mission and find where and how it spawns 3. Hope the NPC spawns(its RNG based) 4. If it spawns and you beat it hope it drops Key Item(aka Dragon Ball aka RNG based). It often drops 2 items and usually the key item is 2nd notification if it drops.
I find this way to get Dragon Balls kinda stupid but oh well... its something .
Once you gather all 7 balls(can take 1-2 hours grinding if you put your mind on it) you can summon Shenron and pick one of those wishes : More money, Rare item, Clothing Item , Z-soul materials, Level up, new Ultimate attack,New Super attack, a playable character or to reset your stats or appearance. Once your wish is granted you ... can go grind them back again, you dont need to wait another year.
The thing that can make your game useless in the future. Everytime you play you need to connect to it .. even for single player . While it provides neat options like Online PvP or co-op parallel missions it still can hurt player's experience if you cant connect to the darn server. Anyway, you can still do "offline" pvp/parallel missions with playable character you unlocked OR you can hire player's character(the higher the lvl, the higher the cost). At first the cost may seems high but that changes quite fast.
Annoys me.. or more likely the lack of annoys me during the cutscene. At times is fine and at times is either missing or not timed correctly.
Its a great game. Combat is well made. Progression system is fun, clothing feels limited but the skill variety is big enough to keep you busy.
Is it worth it to get the game for the combat? Definitely!
Is it worth it to get it for the story? Nope, not a chance. Afterall the game is more about unlocking stuff than just beating the story.
