I'd like to go on record now and say that I've put more hours in to this game than anything else I've ever played. I started back when I was in seventh grade and this was my game of choice every afternoon and weekend through all of high school. I quit playing Mabinogi seriously about the time I graduated, then went back some time later. I've put way too many hours in to this game and I've watched it grow from the early stages to the game it is now.
Now, the I'll break down the game's biggest weaknesses as best I can and let you decide if you want to play this game or not.
RNG repairs: It's present in nearly every game at this point, but it's really bad in Mabinogi. If you have a sword with 12/12 durability and you take it down to 0/12 with lots of use, you can lose your maximum durability on a repair. Your 12/12 can become an 11/11 or even a 9/9. You can pour money and time in to upgrading and perfecting your weapon, getting the perfect enchants on it, and even spamming pay to win elements on it to make it perfect, but eventually you'll be sitting on a great weapon with 0/0 durability and no way at all to use it.
RNG upgrades: Once you fully manage to upgrade your weapon of choice, you have a special upgrade you can preform that either increases the damage or your critical attack damage. This upgrade comes in multiple "steps" starting from step 1 and going up to 6 (I believe step 7 was added as of the last time I played, but I have no experience with this.)
Step 1 to 2 will have a 50% success rate and cost about 100k per attempt. If you fail at getting to step 2, your step 1 weapon will go back to 0 and there's nothing you can do about it but try again. Every success takes you up a grade, every fail takes you down one. You could have a step 4 weapon and it can drop down to step 0 simply by failing what feel like coin flips repeatedly, each failure making your weapon weaker and costng you money to do so. As if that's not bad enough, there's a final 6th step you can reach from step 5 that has a 40% chance of success, and your weapon will DISAPPEAR if it fails.
What.. The.. ♥♥♥♥....
Imagine spending a bunch of money on a weapon, a bunch of money carefully repairing it, a bunch of money upgrading it, you finally manage to get it to step 5 then POOF! All gone, try again. Seriously, whoever thought this was a good idea needs ♥♥♥♥ing fired.
In-game economy: It's nonexistant. Seriously. Any item you can craft or get as a drop will also appear in the cash shop in the form of a gachapon or a set you can buy. Want to recover a little of your max durability on a weapon? wait for it to appear in the cash shop. Need more space or want to get around faster? Buy a pet in the cash shop. You can't spend money to get out of doing leveling, but you can buy weapons that will make your leveling experience feel like the easiest thing you've ever done. The only reason to raise any crafting skills in the game is for the added stat bonuses.
PvP: What PvP? There are multiple systems in the game for it, but there's absolutely no reason to do any of them. Players can do way too much damage and don't have anywhere near enough health to deal with it. Experienced players with enough money invested in reforges (see next point) can kill somebody (in a duel where you're supposed to do 1% of your original damage) in about ten seconds. There's no point at all.
Reforges: Oh boy, here we go. This, for me, was the nail in the coffin. This is what made me quit the game after so many years of hard work and commitment. Reforges are cash shop exclusives (with very very few exceptions through events.) A normal reforge will cost about $1.30 and gives you one roll at your gear. It doesn't change the gear's existing stats in any way, but it does add a new stat down to the bottom. Once you put a stat on your item, you can buy another to change it. I've seriously gone through $140 just trying to get the ONE stat I wanted on a single piece of gear. Not two specific stats, just one. You spend and you spend and you spend, throw your entire pay checks at Nexon just for a chance to maaaaaaybe get what you want. It got to the point I wouldn't duel anybody who used reforges, and I stand by my decision. You're literally buying your damage in the cash shop.
Reforge scaling: To put it in perspective, I could take the next few years and fully max out a character. Every skill. Maxed. No exceptions. I could then enchant all my gear and upgrade it perfectly to maximize my damage. The best bow with the best roll and the best upgrades, all the way to step 6.. Where to go from there? Nowhere.. Pretty good, pretty good... Now take a newbie with three month's experience and give him the same bow, let him max out just his archery skills (no added dex from other skill trees) and spam it with reforges till you get decent damage rolls. 10/10 times that newbie will do more damage every time with every shot than that expert. This game doesn't give a♥♥♥♥♥♥about your play time or your effort, money will always win.
In conclusion: There's tons more I could talk about, but I don't want to keep writing this any longer. This isn't recent, I haven't played this game in at least eight months. This is the resentment I feel towards Mabinogi and their publisher from how terrible their game was all that time ago, and I am positive it hasn't gotten any better. They add new 'harder' content but they increase the cap on the damage players can do as well, so there's really no point. Even if Mabinogi has some of the most entertaining progression I've ever played, you'll outlevel the progression and it turns in to a slow tedious grind on easy mobs and artificial difficulty thrown at you to make you feel challenged. Don't waste any time or money on this outdated trainwreck, your bank will thank me later.

I am glad the game was only $6.99 in this instance because if I had paid $20 for this game, it would have been a rip off, solely because the storyline is so short.
Final Verdict:  If you want to play the updated version of the original SCK, then I reccommend this game.  If you are looking for a game that will last more than two hours to solve, I reccommend the following Nancy Drew Games instead:
1. Treasure in a Royal Tower
2. Stay Tuned for Danger
3. Shadow At The Water's Edge
4. Ghost of Thorton Hall
5. Curse of Blackmoore Manor

This is a new title in a well established, well received franchise, set in the world of One Piece. Initial Review:
I will keep this brief, but add to it as I play. I have completed the initial tutorial for the game and am starting to progress through my chosen craft. Generally I prefer crafting, but do enjoy combat from time to time, so I went with Genetic Engineer. I supply my own Tissue and DNA samples which you get from harvesting animals, which need to be dead. I have dabbled into some of the other crafts and have quickly realized how intense the crafting in this game really is. It is very difficult to become your own supplier.
For instance, I can buy sterilizing agents(agent A), but I decide to craft them, so I determine which profession makes them. Turns out several, so I pick Chemistry, to make agent A, I need another item made with chemistry(agent B), as well as a raw resource, and an Acid(Agent C). So I go to make Agent B and find it requires another Raw resources and another agent from another skill(Agent D). For Agent C I need another craft skill, foraging, so I pick that up to find that I need a raw resource and more of Agent B. To make agent D I need A Raw resource, and who knows what else, so I just buy it. So to make a simple item, needed to make anything else in Genetic Engineering, I need 4 different raw materials, and 5 different crafting sessions, and that is with buying one refined item, which I need twice. I may still be missing a step, but to get those 4 different Raw materials, I need Foraging, Survival, Mining. I would also need a combat skill to be able to kill the creatures for some of those items. I guess if I wanted to keep it brief, I should not have mentioned the crafting system.
That said, it is a very well done system and it is exciting to see your work progress. I am ten hours in and have forgotten that there was no class selection, and the world feels very free and open, a much better feel for an mmo in my opinion. However, its not all sunshine and rainbows either. There are glitches, random crashes, graphical anomolies and everything else you would expect to find in a game. I have not knowingly joined a group(more on that later) or participated in PVP so I cannot speak on game balance. That said, it is definately worth the money, just remember you are basically buying a product that is still in Alpha. You are helping a startup to fund a brilliant idea and they almost always have a GM on to answer questions or help with bugs, which shows their commitment to making this game a success.
I am still listing it as a con because it is hard to find but here is some good information for new players.
- Pros -
Amazing crafting system
Enjoyable combat
Good Tutorial
Great Trade System
Complex Skill Tree
GM Support
- Cons -
Learning Curve (A manual would be nice, especially for the UI)
Auto Group (realized I was in a group for the first time yesterday)
Glitches (expected but a con none the less)

I was sceptical at first, but after trying out the demo I was hooked. Don't be fooled by the minimal interface or anime-style characters if either bother you - this game has a story to tell and does it in a gripping way, breaking elements into bite-size chunks that make you beg for more.
After playing the demo for its full length, I bought the game at full-price and continued to complete it in one sitting. For an entirely narrative-based game, a good 3 hours of gripping gameplay is quite a feat, and with only half the content unlocked and plenty more endings to see, there's a lot of space for replayability! Concept art prizes for completion percentage, too!
All I can say is 'give the demo a try'. You'll probably either love it or hate it, but I certainly loved it. This game hit all the right spots at the right times, emotionally connected me with a character, strained that trust, then ultimately rewarded both her and I with catharsis. Worth every penny I paid.

EDIT: This has been downvoted a lot since the workshop came out. Having gone back to the game, the main point still stands - if you're good with visual information and angles, every level plays the same and is over in minutes. It's cute, but I didn't love the visual style or the story (very shallow), and I didn't fall in love with it the way others have. At 80% off, I would buy it every steam sale - at full price I'd feel ripped off.
A classy game which plays exactly the way the demo would suggest, the main problems are that it is amazingly short (two playthroughs and a few hours of afk time, and you'll still finish it in less than the 10 hours on my record), and the gameplay locations and graphics get repetitive very quickly. The branching storyline doesn't really branch much, or meaningfully - this is very much an open book as far as (either) plot goes, and the special edition would only make it easier (thus shorter) to complete.
Thus I cannot recommend this game unless it's at 80%+ off - it's a cute concept but it's too little game for too much money, especially given that the bi-annual sales of triple-A titles often bring 40+ hour games down to less than Gunpoint's asking price.

Just...soo many flaws with this one, I had to really think about the positives of the game, however I never regret spending time playing a Nancy Drew game. While I can't rec this for other people to play, they still kept true to the spirit of Nancy Drew games.
♥ The dialogue was on point.
I always enjoy the little jokes and quirks that come with the dialogue in Nancy Drew games. I appreciate the fact that I can play the games with my parents and pets in the same room, without seeing my mom flinch, or my dad wince at a curse word or innuendo.
♥ The ending surprised me.
It was a change from how the Nancy Drew games usually end, though of course it comes with a positive, keep Nancy safe ending. It actually kept me guessing until the end of who killed Jake...!
✘ The puzzles.
There weren't many in this game and the one that runs throughout the course of the game failed to impress. It wasn't very hard and was so boring having to keep track of letters...they could have taken it a lot further. The most exciting the puzzles became was the one featured when Nancy has a timed, survival event. Bleh.
✘ It didn't take long to play.
Compared to other Nancy Drew games, especially the newer titles, this game took hardly any time at all to play. I disliked how they didn't make the world as full as they usually do...you can go to the diner, school, and aunt's house. There isn't a sense of time passing, no sleeping, no changing of day/night even. It feels very boring.
✘ The graphics made me laugh.
They're just so bad, even compared to other older Nancy Drew games. Along with this are the stereotypes - the asian wanting to be a doctor, the jock
, etc. The music that was never in sync and would blare suspense music while simply talking to someone, etc, etc, etc.
Overall I would only suggest buying this if you, like me, want to play every Nancy Drew game. Otherwise save your pennies and go buy a different Nancy Drew title!

I remember reading Nancy Drew books starting with age 10, alongside classical juvenile mystery series like
which will later encourage me to read
by Thomas Brezina, and eventually actual mystery classics like Arthur Conan Doyle, Agatha Christie, Gaston Leroux, Maurice Leblanc and countless others. But Nancy Drew will always hold a special place for me as the one cheesy, meticulous, smart alec; the lady sleuth who introduced me to the world of detective fictions as a childhood memory that I'm very fond of.
For the unfamiliar, Nancy Drew is a girl sleuth of age 18 who likes to poke her nose in mysteries all around. Here in this particular adventure, she is called in to solve a murder that occurred in a high school. A local detective contacted her to offer an undercover position as a student to gather information within the high school and solve the murder if possible. Already experienced in mysteries of the world, Nancy accepts. She is to snoop around the local high school, interrogate other students and collect clues to shed some light into the brutal affair.
is the first instalment of Nancy Drew game series developed by Her Interactive in 1998, which is remastered in 2010. Here, we have the remastered version of the original with its ups and downs. The graphics are definitely better - with a heavy uplift on character animation especially - and countless references to other games scattered around. Voice acting in these series has never been great, but considering this is actually the first in the series one should expect the cheesiest possible. My main complaint is that an already short yet enjoyable game has been cut shorter with some dialogues omitted and puzzles skipped as a tradition of "remastering" old games here too. Still, this wasn't enough to crumble the game down. In its essence, as any and all Nancy Drew games, this one is fun.
This is an old school adventuring game which sincerely doesn't hold hands with the player even with the easier mode. There are clues and references scattered all around, and if you plan to actually solve this thing yourself, - without a walkthrough - you'd better keep a pen and some paper around to do old school detective work yourself. You'll need your notes to solve puzzles and get a meaning out of scattered riddles. None of the puzzles or clues are actually hard, but it takes attention and some memory. On that manner, this game is an enjoyable brain scratcher.
Sadly, 2nd to 6th in the game series have never been remastered, and are quite old to be digitalized, thus they cannot be found in the Steam Store. If you are curious about these earlier games, your best chance of acquiring them seems like being lucky enough to stumble on a retail copy. I'll go fetch myself a decent youtube playthrough to watch them as a worst case scenario, 'cause this underappreciated, charming adventure series do deserve your time. Nothing magnificent or majestic - even a bit lame on the Scooby Doo caliber - but
is an enjoyable pass time for an evening for the mystery lovers who'd appreciate some basic old school challenge.

- follow for regular updates on reviews for other games!

Pros:
+ Character customisation is intricate.
+ The controls are easier to grasp than other 3D DBZ fighters.
+ Finally a new story! Kind of!
+ Beating up enemies with other players feels great.
+ Collecting new items and skills can be addicting.
+ Large roster of fighters. Includes variations of their timeline. (e.g. Vegeta during Saiyan saga to Buu saga)
+ Ressurection 'F' DLC content, including Golden Freiza.
Cons:
- Online matchmaking is close to dead at this stage. (By the time of this review)
- PVP is unsurprisingly broken and crap.
- Special/Ultimate Attacks are the only defining factor for characters.
- Combat could be seen as shallow as a result.
- Prepare to hear players spam their attacks continously, and give you little opportunity to contribute in a quest.
- Your character only goes up to Super Saiyan 1 in appearance.
- Loot awards are mostly random
- Special quest conditions are only activated randomly even if you fulfill them. (e.g. Fighting Super Saiyan 2 Gohan requires beating everyone else first before Gohan. Strangely, the game will only acknowledge that you did this 25% of the time)
Conclusion:
If you held off on Xenoverse, it may have been for a good reason. Still, customising and developing your own hero/heroine may grow on you. In the UK at least, finding viable matches for quests and PVP is quickly becoming hard as a lot of players have already have moved on from the game.
If a Xenoverse 2 has (ever) been announced by the time you read this review, you may be better off waiting for that.

Generic Attacks: X and Y.
Special Attack: B.
Charged Attack: RB
Dash and Dash Attack: A
Awakening: (Not sure what this is called officially, but it's what you do before you can use Kizuna Rush) it's either just RT, or RT and B at the same time (I'd have to test this further to be absolutely sure of one or the other).
Kizuna Rush: Tap B while Awakened
Change Crew Member: Up and Down on the D-Pad
Change Map View: Left and Right on the D-Pad
Reset Camera: LB
Set Target: LT

Having struggled through the original Nancy Drew: Secrets Can Kill and it's frustrating disc-swapping, I was keen to see what the Remastered edition was like. I think the team did a great job at bringing this story into the present level of difficulty and intrigue as the series' newest releases. One of the hit and miss aspects of the original Secrets Can Kill game is the culprit, and I think the remastered edition did this justice by turning it on its head and making it relevant, exciting and, most importantly, logical. It makes sense, which is something the ending in the original game lacked.
My only qualm with this game is that it was very short, shorter than most games in the ND series. It didn't stop me from enjoying it, not at all, but I finished it in one sitting, which is unusual for these types of games. Usually I stumble upon a puzzle I can't solve, get stuck and, like a champ, rage-quit for a while. (But I always come back).
If you want an easier to play, updated version of the Secrets Can Kill game, snatch this bad boy up. If you're new to these games and want to experience Nancy Drew at it's finest, I'd rate this one at about mid-level, just because of its length.
(As an aside, my ultimate ND recommendation is Treasure in the Royal Tower. Brilliant storyline, gameplay and characters.)

If you don't like reading, then this isn't the game for you.
But if you're the kind of person who, when they're playing any other sort of video game likes to read all the optional journal entries and log files of the departed denizens of whatever ruin you're slicin' up monsters in, then you'll find this a pleasant surprise.
The visual novel format does much to immerse you inside the game's world--you're not just a guy reading a book, you're a guy on a spaceship drifting next to an abandoned hulk reading the ship's logs about a doomed voyage while two AIs who aren't telling you the whole story comment on them.
It's not "anime". It's a story about politics, family rivalry, and inhumanity. It's one of the first "visual novels" to remember that the word "novel" is there for a reason.

The One Piece Pirate Warriors series has been around for a while now and has finally come to Steam. Join Luffy and everyone you know fight through the story all the way to Dressrosa. I will add a TL;DR at the end.
You are Monkey D. Luffy, the man who’s going to become the pirate king! You can choose to play the main story, a free log mode where you can select any character, or play dream logs. The combat is fun, fluent and will make any One Piece fan happy as hell. I have played around 32 hours so far and I still have a lot to do. The combos are swift and the team attacks are fun to use. You will unlock more characters as you play and a leveling system is present with characters. Different combos lead to different team attacks and so on. Honestly it's a blast to play through.
So the graphics are not realistic, but that’s the point. The art style stays true to One piece and perfectly recaptures the One Piece story arc. The voice acting is great and the cinematic scenes are awesome. The music fits perfectly with every moment and I may or may not have cried at some moments. Graphics and the sound mix perfectly to create an authentic One Piece game which stays true to its roots. There is a problem right now which limits the game's graphics, hopefully this will be fixed soon. There are actually multiple problems existing with logia users.
As I have said before, this game perfectly captures the essence of One Piece. If you have watched the show or are a fan you will not be disappointed. This is the first time I played this game series (because I don't own a Playstation 3 or 4) and I cried at how well this retold everything in some moments. I relived this series and kicked butt while doing it. The combat shows all the popular moves from Luffy, Zoro, Sanji, Nami, etc. The character rooster is a perfect size (for me at least). If you are a fan of One Piece don't worry you will almost definitely enjoy this game.
+ Retells the One Piece storyline

"Never forget 'Namjon yeobi -- Men are honored; women are abased.'" That's a note *Hyun-ae, the AI of an empty spaceship, leaves for you. Throughout the course of Analogue, you dig through correspondence of the passengers of the ship and share it with two of the ship's AIs, who seem to be at cross purposes. How you interact with them changes what information you have access to and ultimately what you come away with in the end.
Analogue is a visual novel, so if you never liked them, it's not going to change now. But otherwise, it's an interesting one with something worth saying.
If you're willing to pay a premium to support indie developers, grab Analogue right away. Otherwise, hold off for a sale price -- it IS pretty short.

BUYERS REMORSE:
As a long time hardcore player of SWG I was excited by the hype and anticipation for this game and have followed its development since 2012.  When I saw early access on steam I opened my wallet and decided to give it a go... it took me a single session of frustration to realize what a mistake I had made and what a lie the advertising has been.
Where to start... well first thing you will notice is character creation.  Simply put, it is awful.  It is one of those systems that is intended to make the player feel like you have unlimited customization but in the end still cannot produce the result you want.  The player is given lots of meaningless options but even then it is frustrating to control (more on this later) as it is one of "those" character creators where adjusting one slider pushes three others.  Character design is ultimately unappealing so you better like wearing your helmet.  The entire character creator (and the character models for that matter) needs to be rebuilt from the ground up IMO.
My next and probably largest complaint is with the controls and interface.  Much like character creation, we are given the illusion of lots of choice, but none of the choices we want or need.  I found myself wrestling with the controls constantly... not a good sign and it really takes away from getting into the game.  Remember the smooth, user friendly controls and interface from SWG that felt good to the touch and allowed you to become easily immersed in the world?  Apparently this design team does not.  Being able to ALT between mouse mode and third person would be a huge step in the right direction, but merely scratching the surface of what requires a complete overhaul.
Graphics:  Well, in fairness one should not expect too sophisticated of graphics from any MMORPG if you want complexity in the world while maintaining playability.  But some of the design choices here are just.... baffling.  The aspect ratios and fonts are such that I was suffering eyestrain and a headache after a mere 2 hours of play.  On top of that, the world is drab and lifeless aesthetically.  All browns and greys.  Lots of darkness.  It simply does not LOOK interesting.  Already mentioned that the characters look like garbage.  I do not kid that in addition to the physical discomfort I felt a bit depressed after playing for a couple hours from looking at such an uninspired landscape and world.
The game world is horribly scaled, a trend I see shared with more and more MMOs of recent times.  By this I mean, every structure you enter is enormous and out of proportion... large vacant spaces with colossal head space and lots of meaningless filler.  Remember in SWG, you would enter a structure and the proportions made sense?  The rooms were filled with items in what appeared a logical and meaningful way?  When you walked the streets of say, Coronet, nearly all of the buildings had some function and the scale of it all made sense?  This new style of MMO world gives us big, vacuous structures meant to provide the illusion of vastness.  It asks you to walk 3 minutes from one drab structure which is identical to the next in order, save for some stupid billboard outside.
To further compound the frustration of the experience, I could still feel the "rails" beneath it all.  This game is by no means a true sandbox in any sense.  It may have some sandbox-like qualities, but to compare it to SWG is an insult.  I was getting more of a "Star Trek Online" and "Old Republic Online" vibe from this game.  If you are a fan of those games but prefer a drab, lifeless, brandless sci-fi setting, then this may be the game for you.
If you came looking for the next SWG...... "move along".

An open-world RPG based on the Alien wasteland known as Pandora. I'll admit that i'm not the hugest fan of this game, but I'll put that down to a lack of hours put into it.

The Cooperative feature is the hidden gem in this game, which offers a whole new style of gameplay for you and a friend to delve into the open world together, and explore, fight alongside each other, and later argue intently over who truely needed that "insta-health pack" more.
The cartoonish feel to the game may appeal to majority of people who purchase this game, and as we've learnt from the likes of Minecraft, graphics aren't the be-all and end all of the game.

Who is this game for?
1. People who have played (and enjoyed) other games from the Borderlands series
2. People who like a good dark, but not too serious story
3. People who have played (and enjoyed) other Telltale games
4. People who want to explore the Borderlands lore further
Who is this game NOT for?
1. People who care more about gameplay
2. People who do not like, or care for the Borderlands lore (Obviously)
3. People who do not like Telltale games, but enjoyed Borderlands
Extrapolation
FOR
1a. Personally, I thought this game was fantastic. This is, understanding that I have played Borderlands 2, and the Pre-sequel. Another thing to note about the Borderlands in general is it's rather morbid sense of humor. Either you like it, or you don't. If you are interested in Borderlands, give this a shot.
2a. This game is dark. It has a number of moments featuing intense scenes that are, of course treated with a fair amount of levity - in typical Borderlands fashion. The story itself is pretty solid, usually playing off of the more dark moments with comedic commentary in a sort of anime kind of style. Overall the story is solid, but definitely not with out it's cliches.
3a. If you like Telltale then what you see is what you get. There's not much too it. Over all, very nicely animated - although filled with more cinematography then usual. Of course all in the Borderlands universe, and featuing strong well made charcters.
4a. If you wished there was more lore, and focus on Pandora then you've come to the right place. This game gives you Pandora (and Hyperion) from a completely different prespective, and it's fantastic. Just note that you'll be exploring Pandora through the characters. There is no exposition to be had in this game.
NOT FOR
1b. The focus of this game is in the story, not the gameplay. As far as gameplay is concerned QTEs (Quick Time Events) and couple of very simple hacking minigames are about it.
2b. Well, it's Borderlands. Space adventure. Ridiculous morbid comedy. Alien planet, and that's about it. Take it or leave it.
3b. It's still a Telltale game. There is no actual shoot and loot in this game (Which is to be expected). You have choices, moral decisions all from the same Telltale formula we know and love.
Final Thoughts
I liked the game. I did, in the end have some reservations about the ending, but outside of that thought it was pretty fantastic. If you want a meme answer "This game made me feel emotions towards a Loader Bot" would be the best response. Also, great music choices. Seriously go pick this up. It's worth your time, and money.
Game Recomendations

I would also recomend Dangan Ronpa if you want a much heavier on the reading, much more Japanese story focused game with it's own share of ridiculous morbid humor

Secrets Can Kill (Remastered) is the 1st of 32 (as of May 2015) installments within the Nancy Drew point and click adventure game series. It is important to note that this version (the version available on Steam) is a remade and revised version of the original game that was released in December 1998. The game was updated with refined graphics, puzzles, and user interface changes and was released in 2010 to match many of the more modern Nancy Drew adventures available at that time. Within this game you assume the role of amaranthine sleuth Nancy Drew and investigate the recent murder of high school student Jake Rogers at Paseo Del Mar High School. Eloise, who is a faculty member of the high school and is Nancy Drew’s aunt, is beside herself and called upon Nancy Drew to stay at her house while the local authorities have Nancy investigate the troubling events transpiring at Paseo Del Mar. It’s up to Nancy to go undercover as a new student while questioning others to find out why someone would want to murder Jake Rogers.
Nancy Drew adventure games are not your typical triple “A” open world RPG or FPS. As the genre mentions it is a “point and click adventure game” where one searches for clues, solves puzzles, questions suspects, and unravels a larger mystery through deductive reasoning. The game is not designed to be an engrossing universe or narrative. Rather, for me, is designed as a light-hearted story for anyone of all ages. It serves as a nice break from larger games and is easy to simply kick back to, relax, and enjoy. The plot-line of these games typically takes about 7-12 hours to unravel depending on your sleuthing skills.
This game in particular has a more realistic atmosphere that is a bit more intense compared to other Nancy Drew titles. You need to quickly comb the entire high school finding hidden messages and snooping into others’ lives before a murderer catches on to your cover and ends your investigative career for good. The dialogue, story, and game mechanics are well done and have enabled this original classic of the Nancy Drew series to age well. For those wondering if they should buy the original 1998 game versus this 2010 remake: I personally enjoyed the “antique” feel of the original classic made in 1998 and did not like all of the story changes that they made in this 2010 revision. However, if you don’t feel like constantly swapping out 2 discs (the joys of older games!) the 2010 version is still an enjoyable and an above average Nancy Drew title. If this is your first time looking at the Nancy Drew game series, I tend to recommend some of the more classic titles, which are in my opinion, of higher quality and contain some of the best narratives in the series (keep in mind though that the graphics and game engines of these games may be a bit more dated, being from the earlier 2000s). To understand if you might like these games I recommend checking out some of the more iconic titles: The Curse of Blackmoor Manor, Danger on Deception Island, Ghost Dogs of Moon Lake, or Treasure in the Royal Tower (the latter of which is not available on Steam). During the summer or holiday sales many of the Nancy Drew games are easily $2-$5 on Steam so just wait until then and you can check out these games as a nice cheap break from the usual FPS or RPG. Happy sleuthing!

Before you go any further, a primer: This is a game that is designed to be finished like a book. It is not one where you pit your -supposed- skills against computer- or human-controlled opponents. It offers a fairly refreshing twist to the way stories are normally told.
First off, let me say upfront that if action is all that matters to you (and/or you're not a fan of visual novels), don't even bother looking at this game - you're entirely incompatible with it and simply won't think much of it, so save yourself time and don't bother with the demo (or reading the rest of this review). In fact, the screenshots on the game's page are all you will ever see in the game, the rest is up to your imagination. You won't see the
or its interior, nor your own ship's. There is no voice acting, and all you will ever interact with are two AI individuals, and an override terminal through which you can switch between the two and perform some other tasks.
However, if you are willing to look beyond that, the storyline is actually pretty interesting. It's really hard to explain it without spoiling anything, and I think the description on the game's page does a fairly good job of explaining the context. I recommend giving the demo a go, it's well worth your time if you're willing to look deeper than the seemingly simple first impression - I was already captivated by the storyline in the demo, and so much so that it successfully persuaded me to get the full game.
Unfortunately, if you're still unfamiliar with the names, the questions the AI occasionally asks of your opinion will sometimes catch you off guard as you struggle to recall who they're talking about, and the inability to refer to the family tree at that juncture only serves to compound the problem.
At some point in the game, the override terminal will temporarily become an integral part of
story, so don't forget how to use it (although it should be easy to figure out how). It would be nice if it supported tabbed commands (i.e. pressing tab to autocomplete partially entered commands) and command history (i.e. using the up and down cursor keys to speed up entry of repeated commands) just like its real life counterparts, since at the abovementioned point in the game, you'll find yourself typing largely the same commands over and over.
All in all, a piece well worthy of your time.

The One Piece Pirate Warriors series has been around for a while now and has finally come to Steam. Join Luffy and everyone you know fight through the story all the way to Dressrosa. I will add a TL;DR at the end.
You are Monkey D. Luffy, the man who’s going to become the pirate king! You can choose to play the main story, a free log mode where you can select any character, or play dream logs. The combat is fun, fluent and will make any One Piece fan happy as hell. I have played around 32 hours so far and I still have a lot to do. The combos are swift and the team attacks are fun to use. You will unlock more characters as you play and a leveling system is present with characters. Different combos lead to different team attacks and so on. Honestly it's a blast to play through.
So the graphics are not realistic, but that’s the point. The art style stays true to One piece and perfectly recaptures the One Piece story arc. The voice acting is great and the cinematic scenes are awesome. The music fits perfectly with every moment and I may or may not have cried at some moments. Graphics and the sound mix perfectly to create an authentic One Piece game which stays true to its roots. There is a problem right now which limits the game's graphics, hopefully this will be fixed soon. There are actually multiple problems existing with logia users.
As I have said before, this game perfectly captures the essence of One Piece. If you have watched the show or are a fan you will not be disappointed. This is the first time I played this game series (because I don't own a Playstation 3 or 4) and I cried at how well this retold everything in some moments. I relived this series and kicked butt while doing it. The combat shows all the popular moves from Luffy, Zoro, Sanji, Nami, etc. The character rooster is a perfect size (for me at least). If you are a fan of One Piece don't worry you will almost definitely enjoy this game.
+ Retells the One Piece storyline
+ Graphics are perfect for One Piece (they should just fix the graphics bug ASAP)
+ Good sized character rooster with favorites
+ Leveling system
+ Great campaign
+ Free logs and Dream logs for even more fun
+ Combat is fluent
+ Cinematic scenes are amazing along with the voice acting
- Horrible optimization for the keyboard controls
- Controller buttons are not shown making it a guessing game to figure out your attacks at first
- Certain small things in the storyline are non-canon
- Large graphics problem existing within the game right now (hopefully fixed soon)
-♥♥♥♥♥♥support from developers
I am a huge One Piece fan (I have watched every episode to date) and I am so happy to have played this game. The release to steam surprised me and I got everything I wanted and more. This game made me remember those amazing moments One Piece has had and why I love the show as much as I do. I loved the combat and I can’t wait to continue playing!
One Piece Pirate Warriors 3 is the first in the series to leave its home on the Playstation system. The combat is great and the game really does feel as if you're playing through One Piece. It stays true to everything you know and the addition of free log, dream log, a leveling system, and a decent character rooster. You should have a controller to play this or you will regret it severely as the optimization for the keyboard controls are horrible to say the least. The buttons for controller are not displayed at first and will make you guess for a short while before you get the hang of it.Currently there sadly is a graphics glitch which is very annoying to some players. Overall this game is the perfect thing for One Piece fans to get with its visuals, music, gameplay, characters, and voice acting. However I would only recommend it to fans.

2/25/2015 - In the current iteration I feel the game is still in the core gameplay stage of testing.  If you don't know what that means, probably best to avoid the game until it progresses into a beta stage.  The developers always seem active and open to feedback.  GM staff is usually always available in game if you hit a snag with most issues.  /newbie chat is most times filled with helpful people (so long as you actually paid attention during the tutorial :P).
I would caution you to bring your engineering degree along if you plan on delving too deeply into crafting because it is quite literally rocket science.  Most crafts also have strong interdependencies relying on the other crafting fields, so it's not a recommended solo experience.  And why have we gotten the notion that MMOs should be solo experiences in all things?  You can eventually grand master every skill line on one character, but don't put the cart before the horse.  Soft cap is currently 6k per skill line (when you stop gaining abilities) with hard cap being 60k per skill line (with small gain improvement depending on the skill line after 6k).
This game is trying to recapture many of the sandbox aspects that have been ignored lately in MMOs.  One of the more important being the social aspects that I feel should exist in all MMOs.  You'll need people for far more in this game then hitting the queue button and waiting for a pve dungeon or pvp map with perfect strangers and then never see them again.  Personally I was excited to see sort of a re-imaging of the Entertainer from SWG providing buffs to people who stop into the pub/cantina (the /tip function is also in this game!).
I've also missed my Creature Handler and there's a few different pet style branches here as well.  Animal Handling - tame baby animals in the wild to fight for you/become mounts for you and maintain them with Vet Medicine (or let another vet maintain them for you), Robotics - build your own robot and outfit them with fittings to suit your needs, and Genetic Engineering - take tissue samples and dna samples from various creatures and make your own mad scientst one-shot consumable-on-use clone pets.
There are 75 total skill lines at the moment to discuss (as well as hidden skill lines), so I won't talk in depth about all those, but I encourage to check out the official site and wiki to learn more.
All in all, this game has a solid foundation to be a decent sandbox which the industry is severly lacking at the moment.  If that is a niche you miss or want to delve deeper into; consider backing.  If you'd like to play a more optimized game... continue to wait until this game moves into beta phase (still a few months out from time of posting).

Okay. I'm gonna be honest here. This is not your typical game. In fact, I'm not sure if I can call it a game. For starters, it is a visual novel, which is at best an atypical kind of game. Second, you will not have fun playing it. In fact, you will be appalled, /horrified/ by this software at times. As more and more information is revealed to you, you are told a story about thoroughly contrasting values, misogyny and arranged marriages in a society where people are ignorant of the very environment around them and women are treated like things, not like people. With all this said, though, it's worth going through it, because it invites you to think about how society can regress into archaism when it doesn't find a way to progress and, apart of the misogyny and arranged marriage dilemma, it also offers a question: When computers become advanced enough, what makes them different from humans? If you're a visual novel enthusiast and like things that make you think, you should have this.

While I haven't played much in this game, I am only really waiting until the release to dive deep into this game. It has so much, and what is best is that you don't feel limited. You aren't a "class". I can spend time fishing with buddies, each of us working on our skill, then I can go off hunting.
The game has no skill cap, but rather has diminishing returns on the odds of getting a skill up. So the long term players will be better, but that gap means less as you get higher up.
The crafting is insane, basically you can't make things from start to finish, well you can, but it won't turn out well. Each item made is often used in another process to make something else. Each step of the process takes into account the crafters skill with that specific receipe. This means you can be awesome at making batteries, but horrible at refining ore.
This means you can work a niche. I have met people who are basically only doing a few items, and they made good money.
The bard buffs (dancing) seem nice.
I recommend this game to people who don't like class systesm, want a very niche type crafting system, and more or less just someone who doesn't want to feel like they wasted time by helping a friend.

EVE Online is one of the best true-Sandbox MMO's currently on the market. It has some of the best graphics and in-depth skill systems I have ever experienced, and has among the most intense player vrs player environments that can impact any level of game play.
Alternatively, the game still is plagued with a slow skill progression where every player is stressed with how to make the best use of each of their 30 day subscriptions. Although the ability to "play for free" is a possibility players must invest both real time and real money, often times with multiple alternate accounts, to even come close to affording such things regularly. The harsh realism of space, and the hauntily similarities of the game to real life can make EVE online a "Real Job."
If a monthly-subscription simulation game with periods of dull conflict punctuated with infrequent mass conflict from a "Top-Down" real time strategic perspective is your thing then EVE Online can not be beat. Though the harsh reality and learning-"Cliff" of the game can be a detractor for many that can provide substantial sense of accomplishment for those who brave it.
As such, I wouldn't recommend this to everyone, just those who I feel fit into the very selective audience that EVE Online has grown accostomed to over the years. For most, the game can come off cold and unforgiving, though for the others the game can be and is a true gem that is unlike any other.

Quantum Conundrum is often dubbed as a spiritual successor to Valve's Portal. After all, they're both magnificent first person puzzlers by the talented former Valve employee, Kim Swift.
When wholly considered, the biggest similarity Quantum Conundrum shares with Portal is its narrative device. Puzzle after puzzle, players must endure the disgruntled remarks of the character's uncle whose behavior was clearly inspired by Portal's sociopathic artificial intelligence, GLaDOS.
Fortunately, the meat of this game, the puzzles, are original and incredibly fun! The player is given the ability to switch between four unique dimensions to get from room to room. These shifts include making all objects lighter or heavier, slowing down time, and reversing gravity. However, rarely will all four dimensions be available simultaneously, making solutions obvious and limited.
Despite its lack of replayability, Quantum Conundrum is still a welcomed addition to the puzzle genre worth playing.
Grade: B

Her Interactive's Nancy Drew games have been great for me.
With a mixture of puzzles, academic skills (ex. Morse Code, Shorthand) and adventure, these point and click mystery games are increadibly engaging to play with a small group of people, or perhaps just yourself.
I've been slowly purchasing all of HI's Nancy Drew games and playing each of them with my younger sisters, and with each game having it's own enviromental setting, puzzles, skills, easter eggs, game mechanics, jokes and characters, it has been a very enjoyable series that I will continue to endulge in.
It is worth noting that, in my opinion, the series has gotten stronger as Her Interactive have continued to get better.
If you plan to only get a single game in the series for now, try starting with a later game. The puzzles in Secrets Can Kill are not as refined as those in the other games in the series I've played, but it isn't to say I didn't enjoy the game.
I strongly recommend the series.

This game has a lot of potential. Many nice features including email mission system, and lots of skills to work on.
The skill system makes a nice change from the level grind found in most mmo games, players are not limited to linear progression, providing they have the right skill and gear players can go anywhere to advance. The skill system also has the advantage of allowing players to tailor gameplay to their particular taste, no need to make alternate characters.
However It's very unpolished at present and badly needs optimized to produce smoother movement and performance, opening the map makes the game lag like crazy, especially so in the already laggy city areas.
The graphics are not the most pleasing to the eye, could do with more textures, art work and better lighting, and greater diversity of environment.
The combat doesn't quite work, currently combat feels like you are fumbling around while trying to target mobs and activate abilities, even the fps mode combat feels stiff and awkward.
While fighting mobs they get so close to your character that you are practicaly shooting at your feet while trying to keep them in target, some bad AI combined with the weird combat system makes for poor gameplay.
Frankly they need to choose one combat mode or the other, trying to combine hotbar click combat and FPS combat through the same basic combat system is poor game design.
Exploration of the game is made difficult because of the death respawn system, the zones are quite large, upon death you are forced to respawn from the nearest city spawn point, this means you have to travel a fair distance back to where you were exploring, an ability to bind in the world or a simple time out mechanism would significantly reduce the demoralizing effect that death currently has for players.
Maps and waypoints ingame could use some refinement, making it clearer for players to find where their mission objectives are. Too much time is wasted trying to find mission objectives at present making some missions just not worth the trouble.
The game features an elaborate crafting system which many crafters will love, however at the same time this is likely to put many others off, alternatives for gear and upgrades for the more casual player may be advisable.

I recommend this game, yes.
Why?
Well, it's because it's the best dbz game in history.... albeit also the ONLY good dbz game in history...
*alert potential spoilers, you have been warned*
At any rate, here are the cons of the game:
Vast amount of blast supers and ultimates, but in the strike department, this game is seriously lacking, there's one crucial one, and the rest are mostly just... meh...
Being a strike based build is a waste of time, especially when blast supers and ultimates are easier to hit with.
PvP is literally dead already. Why?
It's because the sayjan race can have unlimited ki attacks, until their ki runs out. so they can just spam their ultimates at you. And if they pair it with that strike skill I spoke of earlier, they also have unlimited ki.
Go figure. Now add in a spice of super armour (no stagger occours) when equipping certain z-souls...
Yes, who would play against that? it's basically a legal cheat.
Character customization, while being a bliss in just being there. Is fairly limited. You need to wield clothes that gives stat increases or decreases, so that they fit your playing style, which means you'll end up with one outfit you like best, and then never try anything else on.
Oh, and you can't change colours on all clothing.
There are a few races missing.  from the dragon ball lore. Nothing that is quite impressive in the series, but even so, they are still lacking. Can't think of one in particular, but that is mostly because I don't know what they are called.
And no... As a sayjan, you cannot go ape
Here's one thing though: You can't do squat about your basic attack patterns, if you want something different, you need to change class and/or gender. (yes, genders have different attack patterns)
I get the idea, but it annoys me, since I love the grapple on the female sayjan, but hate it on the female majin, which is currently my main.
Oh, and grinding, there's also grinding, and let's not forget about grinding. Did I mention grinding?
Yes, there is ALOT of grinding. Drops are random, and NOT guaranteed to drop in the first place. you'll spend tons of time going through the same quests to get that specific skill, or clothing piece. and there aren't that many quests to do. all of them are the same, safe for 2. where you will ''search'' for dragon balls.
And  by search, I mean look at a dragon radar, land near the ball, and pick it up. Coulda been done better, but it's  nice change.
The main hub?... god that wasn't the best idea, jumping is pointless, and you can't even take off...
Waste of time. It'd been better with a menu. On the other hand, this would remove some immersion.
But it could have been done better. alot better.
Anything else that bothers me about this game?
Let's see here...
In the all the quests, you'll often face multiple enemies at once, who are experts at stun juggle attacks, also ultimate spamming sayjans, and alot of super armour.
Good thing you can bring 2 npc's along XD (even if they are just there to be obstacles for the enemy)
Now then, the money system is also pretty pointless. Once you have everything you need from the stores, money is overrated. the only thing you'll be spending it on, is health capsules (healing pots) and the like. Which are rather cheap, once you start accumulating money in the millions.
Oh, and the chat, is limited to commands. there's no free chat. BORING.
Now then, what's the good stuff? the ''nitty gritty'' of it?
Lemme tell you;
The story mode. It is EPIC. you will not only visit the different eras in dbz lore, you will face it altered, trying to correct it!
See, in the very first story, you'll face a raditz, who is stronger than the old radditz you know. So strong in fact, he broke free of gokus grapple, and survives, while goku still died.
Bummer. You're sent head first into battle, and save his behind before that happens.
And before you know it, you'll be taking on titans in dbz lore.
The level system is well thought through, though the current max level is a bit of a weird thing... How many games has the max level as 99?
Seriously, couldn't they go that one number higher?. It wouldn't mean much, but 99?
At any rate, you can invest points in several areas, including max health, stamina and ki, as well as the power of your basic attacks, strike supers, and blast supers.
Invest the points wisely, you can't redo them without gathering all 7 dragon balls and wishing for a redo, which brings me to the next point:
The dragon balls.
You obtain these by fighting other time patrollers during your quests (Not human fighters, rather an npc version of them)
And then you have a chance to get a dragon ball.
Once you have them all, you can make a wish, yay. Do so carefully though, as the wishes aren't as straightforward as one would think. but there are things you can only get this way.
Now then, what else is nice? The master system. You can gain a master, which is one of the characters from dbz lore, and they will teach you their skills.
Pretty handy. You will get some of the best ultimates this way. Also, after a quest, they may give you an item. Sometimes, during battle, if you are struggling. They will come to your aid!
alright... Vegeta versus vegeta, this is gonna be intere-wait what?!
Also, character customisation. I know it's not much, but it's the only dbz game that actually does exactly what everyone wanted. A game where YOU could create YOUR own character, and toss them into the world of dbz.
Now, if only they could have done better with the main hub... ah well, I guess there's always next time. Here's hoping for a xenoverse 2! (the ending certainly delivers a chance for a sequel, at least the vanilla ending. I have not played any DLC yet)
Now, do the cons outwheigh the pros?
Let's talk about price....
This game, is a whopping 50 euroes on steam. Not a small amount. and no. Don't buy it for that price, wait for it to be on sale, then buy it.
It's not worth it's price, but it's pretty damn close to being so. If only the main hub, and multiplayer aspect had been better. Perhaps an overworld like a traditional open world mmorpg.
But I guess we can't have the cake AND eat it this time, huh?
Well. In any event, thanks for sitting through this lengthy wall of text, hope it gave you some insight in terms of buying or not.
Remember; even though this game has it's faults, I love it. why?
Because it's the only GOOD dragon ball z game in the world. and it's not just the best of the worst. Nope. This game makes the others look like badly made flash games.

EVE Online is one of the best true-Sandbox MMO's currently on the market. It has some of the best graphics and in-depth skill systems I have ever experienced, and has among the most intense player vrs player environments that can impact any level of game play.
Alternatively, the game still is plagued with a slow skill progression where every player is stressed with how to make the best use of each of their 30 day subscriptions. Although the ability to "play for free" is a possibility players must invest both real time and real money, often times with multiple alternate accounts, to even come close to affording such things regularly. The harsh realism of space, and the hauntily similarities of the game to real life can make EVE online a "Real Job."
If a monthly-subscription simulation game with periods of dull conflict punctuated with infrequent mass conflict from a "Top-Down" real time strategic perspective is your thing then EVE Online can not be beat. Though the harsh reality and learning-"Cliff" of the game can be a detractor for many that can provide substantial sense of accomplishment for those who brave it.
As such, I wouldn't recommend this to everyone, just those who I feel fit into the very selective audience that EVE Online has grown accostomed to over the years. For most, the game can come off cold and unforgiving, though for the others the game can be and is a true gem that is unlike any other.

Let me start out by pointing out the obvious: EVE hates new players. The new player experience is flat out horrible: I kid you not, you create your character, you log in, and you find yourself in the middle of space in a small ship. That's it. Go, do your thing. Well, thanks for nothing! Yes, the "opportunities" windows will keep popping up on your HUD, but that just makes matters even worse, since those are not coherent, proper tutorial missions, just a net of achievements, basically. The real tutorial missions slumber deep within the "help" menu, which you can lure out by pressing F12.
F12. Seriously. The quests telling you the basics of how to get around in this massive universe are in a submenu of a menu, that can be opened by F12.
And that's just the tip of the iceberg, and only a mere hint on how cumbersome and overwhelming the UI of this game is, to a point where a second display is almost a must. Somebody once said that this game is basically "Spreadsheets - The Game", and, well, that's what it is, really. Everything important is in tables, texts and numbers, an unholy amount of raw data and information; I swear you could play this game without graphics even being there, because you do everything by clicking on table rows. Even the combat, yes.
That's another problem of mine. If you want in on EVE for the combat, then leave now, because the combat in this game is somewhat similar to Planetside 2 in the sense of being a logistics battle instead of the battle of spacecrafts. You need a good fleet commander and do what he says, and get the right amount of ships to the right place in the right time, and that's that. It's not your skill of flying your ship what matters, but rather your skill to counter-fit your ship considering the strengths and weaknesses of your enemy. To further prove my point, you can see a lot of YT videos, where a guy fights the whole combat in his tactical overlay, which, at that point, becomes a real-time board game. Yellow dots moving to purple dots, purple dots moving to yellow dots, that's it. Does it still require skills? Yes. A lot of skills, in fact. It's just not what you'd expect, and possibly not what you want to do when you think about space combat. Probably that's where piracy comes into play, because that's a way to fight small scale fights, but without a proper manual control over your ship it's just not that exciting (yes, you don't have manual control over your ship, you approach enemy crafts by telling your ship to orbit them or keep them in range).
Oh, since we are talking about pirates and piracy, let's just mention that there are enitre corps, specializing in piracy, WHICH IS FINE! Seriously, this is a sandbox game, part of the fun is that players can be "bad". The problem is that the war declaration system (wardec, wardeccing, or deccing) is a piece of garbage. So what is wardec, exactly? It's a system that enables player corporations to declare war on another player corporation, meaning that they can do PvP combat even in hi-sec space, where otherwise CONCORD (EVE's NPC police) would brake up the fights and hunt down the aggressors. This sounds about OK, right? Nope. The price of a wardec in the game is about 50 M ISK. Now, to put that in context, when the game was new, a PLEX (Pilot License Extension, this is basically gametime in a box) costed about ~400 M. That means 20€ could buy you 8 war decs, right? Well, now you can sell PLEX for 1.2 BILLION, but the price of declaring war remains the same, which means that now 20€ gets you 24 wardecs. The result? Entire pirate corps (so-called "wardec corps") sit on trade hubs, wardeccing EVERY. LIVING. SOUL. This is like if you could, in real life, walk into the police station, give them a checque about $50, and in return they would grant your family the right to do whatever you want with another family. So how can you play around this? Well, either you and your corp move out of the trade hubs, or change regions (and believe me, hauling an entire corp to a whole other region is so fkn annoying), or you can pay the ransom, because yes, these ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s usually want ransom money to drop the wardec, which is usually 100 M ISK and up. That's basically a death sentence to a new corp, so that's a no-go either. So you either jump systems over and over and over and over and over again, like space gypsies, or make some trial accounts and have some hauling alts, who never leave NPC corps (those cannot be wardecced) and do the hauling between your corp's AO and the trade hub - not immersion braking, not at all, nah.
And with that, I think we finally arrived to the whole cancer of the game: the lack of immersion. In EVE Online, you don't feel like playing a game. In EVE Online you feel like working a job. Hours and hours and hours of doing nothing but grinding, farming and running errands, fueled only by the hope of someday getting some enjoyment out of it in a form of a good ship or some nice equipment - meanwhile the market is filled with fake courier contracts, item exchange contracts and auctions, with which people are trying to trick you out of your hard earned money. The space is littered with space pirates, who are either some bored gamers looking for some fun, or actual horrible people, whose sole form of enjoyment is seeing you suffer; meanwhile decent guys roam around space like nomads, being chased and harrased. EVE is not a joyful ride in space, it's hell, a good example of what would happen if anarchy would overtake our current world; an apocalyptic wasteland, a man-eat-man universe, of which I want no further part.

Wow... And I really mean it, wow... This game was, in my opinion, beyond a "great game"! This is easily one of my favorite games, and it's been long since i last made a review, but I really feel that this one deserves it! It was full of awesome humor, great story, and as with most Telltale games, the choices really matters, and it's scenes made you care for even the smallest characters. I was constantly thinking what could've happened if I chose differently. The major scenes did in some cases feel a bit silly, but in a good, epic way.
The gameplay is the most important of it all in this kind of game. It was awesome, and i can't recommend this enough! The game felt really long since i pulled an all-nighter and barely noticed that I skipped out on both dinner and sleep. One powerful element in this game is the humor. That was the most important part for me since it has the exact humor I enjoy the most. The expressions in peoples faces and the sarcasms, they never end! Although it was really funny, it also nailed the sad moments and you really question your choices, making you really feel for the characters. I bought this game in the summer sale, and I thought it should be worth at least the discounted prize it had, since it's a telltale title, and man, the quality! Easily worth every penny i spent! I would be able to feel satisfied over my purchase even if it had cost over 50 bucks.
The graphics are of course neither good nor bad, since it has the cartoon artstyle, and it's hard to tell good graphics apart from the bad in those cases.
I didn't really focus on the sounds, sounded just like it should've, but the music is another story. They managed to nail every chapter and compelling moments with the perfect music for both atmosphere and feeling.
I am definitley replaying this since the ending can be one of very many possibilities, and what happens in the beginning can make a very different outcome in the end.
A contender for the best game i've ever played. One of the best purchases I've made. Simple as that.

An amazing gem that stands out in TellTale's already star-studded line-up. Through genuinely witty and funny dialogue, they manage to make every character endearing and likeable in their own flawed way. Even the robot characters have far more personality than the vast majority of characters found in other video games! They take existing well-loved characters in the Borderlands universe (such as Handsome Jack, Athena and Scooter) and build them up with far more depth than they had in the main games in the series. And the original characters are just as well-formed (with the likes of Gortys, Loader Bot, Fiona, Sasha, Rhys, Vaughn, Vasquez etc.) all earning their place as some of my favourite fictional characters of all time - not just those found in video games. The story balances light-hearted moments of comic relief with scenes of great emotional weight expertly. A single scene can manage to elicit laugh-out-loud moments and at the same time watery eyes - and it all blends so well. The characters are not only incredibly well-realised (bravo to the talented voice actors, writers and animators) but also enjoy meaningful character development that drives the plot forward throughout the tale. All of this is aided by an amazing collection of licensed songs, that make each opening credits scene a pure joy to experience (in tandem with their brilliant choreography that fits the music so well).
Tales from the Borderlands earns its place as my new favourite amongst TellTale's portfolio (I never thought The Walking Dead seasons could be topped). It is their best work yet and makes me incredibly excited for what they will bring next. I can't wait for Season 2!

Some general warnings about this game:
1. It will be free to play when it releases in mid-late 2015
2.The graphics are still very WIP
3. Most of the systems will be very intimidating when you first boot up the game, as they are extremely complex
Despite these reasons, The Repopulation is the best MMO i've ever played. I paid $20 for early access, and can say that the game is fully worth that price, let alone the low price of free later in the year. All of the features that you see are here: Once you get out of the tutorial, the game literally says "Im not giving you any more direction, go and do whatever you want." You can switch to action mode with Shift+A, and the game will play like Mass Effect rather than World of Warcraft. You can also switch into first person mode with shift + F, but it's a little buggy. When people say this is like SWG, they mean it. You can dedicate your time in this game to learning how to dance, and only how to dance. There's a skill tree for dancing, and throwing in different moves will add different buffs. You can also be a storyteller, a weaponsmith, a herbalist, a hunter, a pyro, the list goes on. When you start off in your beginning town, you will recieve emails which detail missions tailored to you based on the decisions you make. If you want, you can ignore them. You can select which missions you enjoy more. There are vehicles to ride, weapon classes to learn, ores to refine, all of this in an early access game. The servers are not empty; the chat is booming on the server im on, and there are more than 5 other servers to play on as well. Seriously, spend $20 on this game. Sure, it'll be free in about 5 months, but you really should not wait for this experience.  Just know that the UI and models are rough around the edges, and you should find hours of entertainment in this.

I bought this with a low discount. I felt ripped off when I was in the launcher, as I there are only two graphical options, no default keyboard config(many ppl recommend to play this game with a controller). After I got a good keyboard config(guide made by ThillinaC), I launched the game, hoping to find my moneys worth. After the prologue, my feelings about this game turned 180 degrees. I wasn't a Naruto fan, but the story of the game won me over. I wasn't a fan of fighting games, but now I have more of those in my wishlist.
This game isn't a good PC port, but it has the steady 30 FPS, so you can enjoy this game that it's better than most expect. Like every fighting game, there are a ton of characters with different unlockable skins, each one with their unique moves. Even tough you'll most likely end up with picking favourites, picking random characters will show you that each character can win if you have the skill. The battles aren't about tactics as much as about timing, as the controls are the same for everyone, just the way the characters execute the commands is different, which makes every character interesting.
The story is so good that it makes the game deserve an underrated tag. For me it's up there with games like Mass  Effect, since I've experienced many emotional impacts and catharsis throughout the game. It's all about the kid who turns out to be the hero that inspires five nations to believe in themselves again and fight the war to prove the opponent that peace in this world can be. The story can turn out to be enough to get a person out of depression.
There's also free roam and the sense of exploration brings many rewards. The missions can be replayed, along many bonus ones. There are a lot of extra battles, like tournaments and mission challanges, that make wallpapers be available for the desktop.
It's a great game, both in quality and quantity, but it's also a bad port. I won't complain about the graphics, but some texture models could have used an improvement. 9.3 is the score for the game and I(along many fans) look forward for the next game and every naruto game that comes after it(that's how much of a fan this game has made me)

(There's a lot of reading below this that I imagine most people won't want to bother with, so I wrapped it up in a simple pro/con system.)

Con:

Amazing game, I don't believe it's quite perfect, but it has many aspects that I've wanted in a DB/DBZ game for about a decade now. Make my own character, make it an RPG so I can level up (though Power Level seems to be ignored, sadly), learn amazing moves that I've admired since childhood (Kamehameha, Kaioken, Final Flash, Big Bang Attack, etc.), fight along side childhood heroes (Goku, Vegeta, Krillin, Gohan, Piccolo, etc.), and fight against childhood villains (Frieza, Androids, Cell, Buu, etc.). If you're a Dragonball Z fan, this is quite simply a must-have game. If you're not familiar with DBZ but enjoy RPG/fighting games, then this might be an enjoyable way to be exposed to DB/DBZ/DBGT.
Let's try and get my nostalgia out of the way to focus on the bad however... the customization is SOMEWHAT lacking. You should manage to make one roughly based on your likeness if that's what you're after, but you'll inevitably find others that look similar. There's not quite enough variety, especially with facial hair, at least for the Saiyans. Perhaps there's more available for Humans, but I've yet to make a Human character. Speaking of which, I was hoping to be half human/half Saiyan, but that's not available, though I don't see that as a big deal. The biggest thing that probably annoys me is how your hair only changes colour when you transform; I chose hair that was rather normal, in my opinion. It didn't stick straight up like I used a kilo of hair gel, expecting it to stick up once transformed.
It didn't for Super Saiyan, but that was ok, Teen Gohan's hair didn't stick up much upon  transforming either. For Super Saiyan 2 however, I still found that the hair didn't stand, so now with my second character, I've chose spikier hair on default. Something like Teen Gohan's default hair, but slightly longer. Another thing that kind of bothers me is how very difficult it is if you have to face several opponents at once, because it seems no matter how weak they are compared to you, all it takes is one punch, or one basic ki blast, and whatever combo you were in or attack you were charging, it'll be stopped. Sometimes you fight enemies who won't be phased when you punch them, like when Hercule attacked Cell. They should impliment that into the game. If a Level 5 character tries punching a Level 50 character, there should be no effect. Similarly, if two Saiyans of the same level are fighting, then if one is Super Saiyan 2 and the other is in base form, then once more, basic attacks should not phase the SS2 fighter. Do a little damage, sure, but it won't cause a flinch or anything. To be fair though, while Level 30, I was invited to fight a Level 60-something character. Even in Super Saiyan or Super Saiyan 2 form, I was easily dispatched, so it WILL be insanely hard to beat a higher level opponent, at least.
As far as I can tell, Super Saiyan 3 is not available, but I like that aspect. In DBZ, the only characters that I know of to have achieved SS3 are Goku and Gotenks, and of course Gotenks only managed it due to all the strength achieved in the fused state. If every Saiyan and their dog could become SS3, then it'd kind of ruin how awesome it is. Meanwhile, for SS2, there's Gohan, Vegeta, Goku, and of course I assume Gotenks has it though it would appear he just skips 2 to go straight to 3, so you can see that, although difficult to obtain, it's still relatively common. By the end of DBZ, the only Saiyans who haven't achieved SS2 are Goten and Trunks, though if you consider their fusion, then they have it all the same, so basically every Saiyan Z-Fighter at the end of DBZ are capable of both Super Saiyan and Super Saiyan 2.
That's all I can think of to mention off the top of my head, having just finished the main story of the game. Sure it's a bit pricy, but I consider it to be more than worth it, ESPECIALLY if you're a DBZ fan. This isn't just some quick little 8 hour game, then the rest is fighting online. I'm over 40 hours in, and I know for certain that there's A LOT to do yet.

Long have I looked for a MMO which apply to me, in my opinion a game should be about doing what you want and while you do it you shall have a very fun time doing so.
In many ways The Repopulation seem to be spot on, the crafting is very comprehensive, thers no doubt that this game was made by gamers who are really into crafting, having to ensure quality for every piece in order to have the highest end product is just spot on if you ask me.
Skill system is very interresting, we have seen in done before and with great success, you don't have any char levels, instead you gain skills by using the respecive tools, weapons or crafting.. theres even skill gain on using a mount!
You can easily switch between RPG mode (WOW style) and FPS, personally i perfer combat pulling in RPG mode for then to switch to FPS mode, during crafting or gathering professions my choice is clearly RPG view.
Everything in this game is based on players themself supplying eachother, and they don't make days long enough for you to do everything on your own (ofc you can still try), but eventually you'll have to settle with what best suits your playstyle and what you want to do. Want to switch later on? Sure, just start doing it, thers no limit as to how many skills of professions you can learn. Personally a perfer mining along with some simple hunting.
You remember Project Entropia (later on Entropia Universe)? This game is much similar to it, crafting is way more advanced and challenging, but mining isn't and thats maybe something which has to change, there was many miners in PE and the way you mined there is something that beats WOW-mining style any day of the week. Who wants braindead mouse clicking on a pixelrock? Not me. Im crossing my fingers for devs to look at different opportunities.
I'll clearly recommend this game to anyone interested in getting involved in the development of a game and leaning the game early on. It's far from launchable and new content along with fixes are added all the time. The potential of this game is pretty much limitless and if done correctly this game has the potential to be a very good game for many years to come.
Keep in mind tho, game will be F2P, what this means for server cost vs income per player is to early to tell, but thers no doubt that as I predicted some years back, F2P game are here to stay. But they also bring with them new challenges and in my eyes there havent been that many "successfull" F2P games, atleast which did apply to me.
Looking at the current state, my best guess is that the game is about a year away from releasing.
